articles.title: Myspace n’est pas mort : le réseau social des années 2000 prépare son grand retour
articles.text:
Les co-directeurs de Myspace l’affirment : le réseau social emblématique des années 2000 effectuera son grand retour au cours des prochaines années. Assisterons-nous au retour du Top 8, de la personnalisation poussée des profils et des musiques associées aux comptes ? Pour l’instant, rien n’est moins sûr, mais le réseau social devrait bel et bien revenir.
Bientôt le grand retour de Myspace ?
La plateforme iconique Myspace fera-t-elle son grand retour en 2027 ou au cours de ces prochaines années ? Il semble que cela soit bel et bien le cas. Dans le documentaire sobrement intitulé MySpace, Tommy Avallone, l’actuel co-propriétaire de la plateforme, est revenu sur l’histoire du réseau social, depuis son ascension jusqu’à chute. Mais surtout, Avallone promet le grand retour de Myspace : « Nous [lui et son frère Chris] sommes toujours propriétaires de Myspace. Nous allons relancer Myspace. Nous attendons simplement le bon moment pour le faire. Et si celui-là ne fonctionne pas, nous recommencerons ». Sur X, les millennials se réjouissent déjà de cette annonce.
 Millenials returning home to myspace: https://t.co/4CvVOCFIn6 pic.twitter.com/V3mILU9CNQ
— Lyros💫🔫 (@LyrosHazard) August 1, 2026
Pour rappel, lancé en 2003, Myspace a été l’un des premiers grands réseaux sociaux à connaître un succès mondial. Les utilisateurs pouvaient personnaliser leur page personnelle avec HTML et CSS (beaucoup ont appris les bases du codage grâce à Myspace). Ils pouvaient également ajouter une musique à leur profil, diffusée automatiquement lors de chaque visite, et classer leurs amis les plus proches dans le célèbre Top 8 . Myspace est devenu extrêmement populaire, à un tel point que la plateforme a été la plus visitée en juillet 2006, devant Google et eBay. Cependant, Facebook aura eu raison de lui quelques années plus tard.
Un retour de Myspace est-il crédible aujourd’hui ?
En 2013, Specific Media et le chanteur Justin Timberlake, alors copropriétaires de Myspace, avaient déjà tenté de relancer le réseau social. Cette tentative s’était toutefois soldée par un échec retentissant. Tim Vanderhook explique : « Nous avons vraiment essayé de le moderniser, mais c’était une entreprise différente à ce moment-là. Ce n’était plus le même Myspace ».
À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, Tommy Avallone a promis un retour de Myspace, mais sans préciser sous quelle forme. S’agira-t-il d’un retour aux sources avec une personnalisation poussée de son profil et un accent mis sur la musique ? Par ailleurs, Myspace pourrait miser sur l’une de ses spécificités qui en fait aujourd’hui un atout sérieux : recevoir des nouvelles seulement de ses amis proches. Les réseaux sociaux actuels nous inondant de contenus suggérés, un tel recentrage sur nos relations plus intimes serait bienvenu. Mais autant dire que rivaliser avec des mastodontes comme Instagram, Facebook ou encore X ne sera pas une mince affaire. C’est le moins que l’on puisse dire. En revanche, les plus nostalgiques seront certainement ravis par cette annonce.

articles.title: I tested the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max and it’s a great all-round performer — when it actually works
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max is a capable robot vacuum that delivers strong hoovering and mopping performance... when it actually works. With my unit developing issues after a year of testing, it's hard to wholeheartedly recommend.
Pros
- +Reasonably priced
- +Powerful app
- +Good hoovering and mopping performance
- +Decent selection of features
Cons
- -Very large base station
- -Unit developed issues
Why you can trust TechRadar
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max review: one-minute review
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max seems like a slam dunk in the robot vacuum space. Positioned right in between the budget and upper mid range sections of the market, it delivers strong vacuum and mopping performance that make it capable of tackling a wide variety of messes in your home.
With LiDAR technology, its mapping is excellent and the robot vacuum does a great job of navigating unexpected obstacles that it might encounter during a clean. The design isn't the most exciting, though it still has a good range of features like an extendable mop arm and automatic carpet detection.
The dock is large, which might make it tricky to fit into smaller homes, but it's pretty capable as well, with hot water washing and air drying capabilities to keep the mop pads clean between uses.
It's all underpinned by a competent app that's easy to use and offers key functions such as being able to schedule cleans, restricting the robot vacuum to certain rooms, and allowing you to customize the vacuuming power and amount of water used by the mop.
The elephant in the room is that my unit developed a fault after a year of testing, occasionally spilling water during a mop pad clean. It's unfortunate and, even though it doesn't seem widespread, makes this model difficult to recommend unreservedly.
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max review: price, range & availability
- List price $999.99 / £499.99 / AU$1,199
- Launched late 2024
- No longer available in Australia
- Limited stock in the US
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max has a list price of $999.99 / £499.99 / AU$1,199, and is readily available via the brand’s website in the UK. It often receives discounts too, taking the price down by £100 or so around major sales events. At this price it sits neatly between the budget and upper mid range price brackets, coming in much more expensive than under $300 / £300 / AU$500 favorites like the Roborock Q7 M5 but cheaper than the likes of the Eufy X10 Pro Omni, which goes for $799.99 / £799 / AU$1,699.95.
That latter model is a good point of comparison here, as it also features mop and similar LiDAR sensor setup. With this in mind, the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max is very solid value - especially if you get it at that reduced price point. Accessories like replacement brushes, dust bags, and mop pads are all available via the Xiaomi website at pretty reasonable prices too.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Unfortunately, this model seems a lot harder to come by in the US. You can find it on Amazon, but it goes for an eye-watering $999.99 and stock appears limited. At this price it’s significantly worse value and you would be better off spending less on an alternative. Its list price is AU$1,199 in Australia, but it appears to no longer be available either through Xiaomi's own store, or Amazon.
- Value for money score: 3/5
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max specs
| Suction | 8,000Pa | 
| Mopping | Yes | 
| Mop type | Dual rotating discs | 
| Robot size (W x D) | 13.78 x 3.82 inches / 350 x 97mm | 
| Robot height | ~3.82 inches / ~97mm | 
| Dock dimensions (W x D x H) | 13.39 x 16.54 x 22.17 inches / 340 x 420 x 563mm | 
| Dust bin volume (onboard) | 15.22oz / 450ml | 
| Water tank volume (onboard) | Not stated | 
| Dust bin volume (base) | 84.5oz / 2.5l | 
| Water tank volume (base) | 135.3oz / 4l | 
| Self-empty dust | Yes | 
| Self-empty / refill water | Yes | 
| Mop pad cleaning: | Yes | 
| Wi-Fi control | Yes | 
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max: design
- Raised LiDAR puck
- Extendable mop arm
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max isn’t pushing any boundaries when it comes to its overall design, but honestly that’s not such a bad thing.
It looks like your average robot vacuum, which is to say a big plastic disc with a chunky bumper at the front and a whole host of sensors. The most prominent of these is a big LiDAR sensor that sits in a little raised puck on the top, though there are others designed to spot obstacles or prevent the vacuum from falling off ledges.
Despite the basic look, the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max has a bunch of useful features including two mop pads, one of which can be extended on a little arm for edge cleaning. The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max is also capable of detecting which kind of surface it’s on, raising the mop pads when it goes over carpet to prevent any accidental stains.
Coming in at13.39 x 16.54 x 22.17 inches / 340 x 420 x 563mm, the docking station that it comes with is absolutely ginormous which could make it awkward to fit in smaller homes, but there are some good reasons for this size. Firstly, you’re getting a large 135.3oz / 4l clean water tank (removed for filling by simply popping up the lid on top of the dock) and a slightly smaller but still sizable 128.5oz / 3.8l tank for dirty water storage.
Xiaomi says that this is more than enough water to clean 2,152.8 square feet / 200 square meters on a single fill, and while my testing area was considerably smaller, I can say that it didn’t need refilling across multiple cleans.
The dock also has a hot water system to help wash both mop pads at 131F / 55C - a temperature that Xiaomi claims reduces odours more effectively. It dries the mop pads using hot air, a process that takes a few hours and produces a small level of sound akin to a desk fan.
There’s also a generous 84.5oz / 2.5l dust bag, which Xiaomi says only needs emptying once every 75 days in a three-person household with one pet. This seems like a very generous estimate to me, and your mileage will vary depending on your specific level of household mess. This bag size is on par with much of the competition, such as the aforementioned Eufy X10 Pro Omni, so you can expect similar performance to those models.
One feature that I particularly appreciate is the ability to remove parts of the dock for cleaning, including the little tray where the vacuum sits while charging. This isn't something that you will need to do regularly, but my previous robot vacuum tracked a decent layer of grime in its dock over the years and was comparatively pretty tricky to clean.
My only real complaint from a design standpoint is the vacuum’s incessant need to narrate what it's doing. By default it frequently declares 'start to dry the mop pad' and similar phrases in a loud, annoying voice. It's disruptive, though mercifully can be turned off in the app.
- Design score: 4/5
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max review: performance
- Good navigation
- Deals with multiple surfaces well
- Base station pump developed issues
I've been using the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max for a year now, and can say that it handles most daily cleaning tasks well. Its navigation capabilities are excellent and map that it generated of my cleaning area was spot on. I have the base station in the corner of an L-shape hallway and the robot never struggles to find it, even when it's been cleaning the handful of adjoining rooms.
Setting room boundaries works excellently too — if you want to restrict cleaning to a specific defined area, the vacuum won't stray beyond it. It also deals with unexpected obstacles like closed doors or moved furniture well, bumping into them once or twice and then adapting its path smartly. You don't need to worry about multiple surfaces, either. Every time I spot the vacuum going over the rug in the middle of a mop cycle, the pads are automatically raised as it detects the soft surface to prevent damage.
The vacuum picks up small debris and cleans up small spills with no sweat, and for a more intensive task I doused my kitchen floor with oats, cereal crumbs, flour, ketchup, and pretty much anything else that I could find in the cupboard.
How did the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max fare? I sent it out on the most intensive possible cleaning mode and it made a commendable dent in the mess. The oats, crumbs, and flour were masterfully hoovered up with the exception of a few survivors in the hardest to reach corners of the room.
The ketchup was more of a challenge, and at first I was pretty worried that it wouldn't be able to overcome it: the mop pads smeared it in a thin layer over the middle of the floor at first but, sure enough, after multiple visits to the base station in order to clean itself and to refill its water tanks, it was all gone after a few runs. I did spot some red residue in the grouting between tiles, but this took just a few seconds for me to wipe up.
It's the kind of performance you would want from a mid-range robot vacuum. It's not a total replacement for doing the cleaning, but it does decrease the need for big cleans.
That said, my unit has developed a major issue over long-term testing. Sometimes when the vacuum cleans its own mop pads (either at the start or during a cleaning task) the motor that's meant to suck away all the dirty water doesn't kick in. This means that dirty water starts to accumulate in the base station, eventually overflowing and spilling out onto the floor.
It's frustrating (and pretty gross), and I'm struggling to resolve the issue by cleaning the water sensors, fiddling with the base station, and so on. Anecdotally, a family member bought Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max a few weeks after seeing my one, and it developed a similar fault within just a couple of months. It was, after some back and forth, repaired by Xiaomi.
Looking online, it doesn't seem to be a widespread problem, though I've still been able to find at least a few others who report the same thing. Users on Facebook and Reddit also seem to have had luck getting their vacuums replaced via Xiaomi's support service, though I suspect I can't go through this route with a review sample.
For this reason, I would recommend buying from Xiaomi directly rather than through reseller if you do chose to pick one up, as you otherwise will likely have more trouble getting support if issues do arise.
- Performance score: 2.5/5
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max review: app
- Easy to use
- Scheduling features
- Different suction levels
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 is compatible with the Xiaomi Home app. It's easy to use and has plenty of features, including the ability to view the map generated by the robot, and its location real time. This is on top of the option to start cleans in specific rooms, schedule cleans, or clean the mop pads.
You can view the battery level, and change cleaning modes. These include basic vacuuming, mopping, vacuuming and mopping, or vacuuming before mopping. You can increase the water output too, with three levels to choose between, but bear in mind that this will increase how quickly you will need to refill everything.
I didn't encounter any bugs within the app, and it remained quick and responsive during my year of testing. The fact that you have to set up a Mi account is a bit annoying, but otherwise it offers everything you could from robot vacuum companion software.
- App score: 4.5/5
Should you buy the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max?
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Performance | Good at vacuuming up debris and cleaning up small spills... when it works as intended. | 2.5/5 | 
| Design | The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max doesn't defy any design conventions, but it's perfectly functional and packed with features. | 4/5 | 
| App | An easy to use app that offers every feature you could reasonably expect. | 4.5/5 | 
| Value | Decently positioned in the UK and regularly on sale, but far too expensive if you're in the US and no longer sold in Australia.. | 3/5 | 
Buy it if…
You want a robot vacuum capable of cleaning serious mess
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max did a good job dealing with some serious kitchen debris and spills. It requires multiple passes for some wet stains, but it is able to get through large amounts of grime.
You have a mix of hard flooring and carpet
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max does a great job differentiating between different flooring types.
You need a good app
The Xiaomi Robot Vacuum X20 Max's companion app has all the features you could reasonably expect. It's a great bit of software.
Don’t buy it if…
You need long term reliability
Although likely not widespread, it's hard to ignore the fact that my unit developed a fault after a year of use.
You can't fit a large base station
The base station here is pretty large, is an includes two water tanks in addition to the standard waste bag. Only pick this model if you know you have the space for it.

articles.title: Hace 55 años, este niño rodó su único papel en el cine. Hoy sigue cobrando (una ridícula miseria) por él
articles.text:
A Peter Ostrum lo sacaron con 12 años de un teatro infantil de Cleveland para ponerlo a las órdenes de Gene Wilder y protagonizar 'Willy Wonka y la fábrica de chocolate', la original, la de 1971. Fue su primera y última aparición en el cine, porque tras el rodaje de la peli rechazó un contrato de tres películas y se hizo veterinario. Lo más simpático es que todavía sigue cobrando por ese papel.
El cheque, literalmente, no da ni para la gasolina que gastaría en ir a cobrarlo, porque el monto asciende a la friolera de entre ocho y diez dólares cada tres meses.
El casting de Cleveland. Empecemos por el principio, que la historia tiene miga. Unos cazatalentos que buscaban por todo el país a su Charlie Bucket (el prota de la película) aterrizaron en el Cleveland Play House, donde Ostrum actuaba en el teatro infantil. Le hicieron unas fotos y lo grabaron leyendo el libro de Roald Dahl. Dos meses después llegó la llamada para una prueba en Nueva York (en la que cantó "My Country, Tis of Thee") y, un mes más tarde, la confirmación: el joven Ostrum tenía diez días para hacer las maletas rumbo a Múnich.
Cinco meses en Alemania. El rodaje de 'Charle y la Fábrica de Chocolate' duró cinco meses, tiempo durante el cual Ostrum estuvo a las órdenes de Wilder y de Jack Albertson (el abuelo Joe). Lo describió, años después, como "una especie de intercambio de estudiantes de cinco meses", según contó él mismo a la revista de la Asociación Americana de Medicina Veterinaria (AVMA). Lo de la revista de medicina veterinaria cobrará sentido en un momento.
El contrato que no firmó. Al terminar, el productor David L. Wolper le ofreció un contrato de tres películas. Ostrum se lo pensó una semana en California y volvió con un no. ¿El motivo? Nada que ver con Hollywood: a la vuelta de Alemania, su familia compró un caballo para celebrar el estreno. Ver trabajar al veterinario del anime fue lo que, realmente, despertó su vocación. "Recuerdo al veterinario viniendo a cuidar de los caballos, y me causó una impresión enorme", explicó, frente a un padre abogado del que, según reconoció, "no tenía ni idea de qué hacía todo el día".
De Charlie Bucket a las vacas de Lowville. Ostrum se doctoró en Medicina Veterinaria por la Universidad Cornell en 1984 y entró a trabajar al año siguiente en la Countryside Veterinary Clinic de Lowville (Nueva York), especializado en caballos y vacas lecheras. Tras dirigir una clínica veterinaria, Ostrum se jubiló en septiembre de 2023, después de casi 38 años de ejercicio.
Ocho dólares cada tres meses. Esa es la cifra que dio en 2018, durante una proyección en el Snowtown Film Festival, y SlashFilm la situaba en la misma horquilla en un texto de finales de 2024. No es ninguna anomalía suya: el sistema de regalías de SAG-AFTRA se calcula con fórmulas fijadas en el contrato de la época, y las películas de los 70 se firmaron sin pensar ni en streaming ni en inflación. Por lo que sea.
Esto mismo le pasa a Mandy Moore, que ha enseñado cheques de 81 centavos por las reposiciones de 'This Is Us' en streaming. A William Sanford Davis, de 'Abbott Elementary', le llegó uno de 3 centavos. Es decir, cuanto más viejo el contrato, más ridículo es el cheque, da igual lo que valga hoy la película: fue precisamente esa brecha uno de los motivos de la huelga de SAG-AFTRA de 2023, que terminó 118 días después con un acuerdo histórico sobre regalías y sobre el uso de la IA con la imagen de los actores.
El valor de la película original. 'Willy Wonka y la fábrica de chocolate' vale mucho hoy en día, aunque costó tres millones de dólares (unos 23 millones actuales, ajustando a la inflación) y recaudó solo cuatro en su estreno de 1971. Fue, a todas luces, un fracaso de taquilla según los estándares de la época. No se convirtió en clásico de culto hasta que la televisión la repuso sin parar durante los años 80 y el vídeo doméstico hizo el resto.
Wonka vuelve con la voz de un muerto. Netflix pagó unos 686 millones de dólares (500 millones de libras, según Financial Times, porque la propia Netflix nunca confirmó la cifra) en 2021 por los derechos de la obra de Roald Dahl, 'Charlie y la fábrica de chocolate' incluida, y cinco años después esa inversión no le ha dado ningún éxito comparable a 'Bridgerton' o 'Miércoles'.
Su última carta, a tiempo para el 55º aniversario, es 'Wonka's The Golden Ticket': un reality de competición de nueve episodios (los siete primeros de golpe el 23 de septiembre de 2026, el final en dos partes el 30) rodado en la Gold Coast australiana, con doce concursantes que se juegan su propio ticket dorado, cada uno con un acompañante, según detalla Deadline.
Rusty Goffe, uno de los Oompa Loompa originales de 1971, repite papel. Y la voz que narra el concurso es la de Gene Wilder, fallecido en 2016, recreada con inteligencia artificial por ElevenLabs (la misma compañía que ya vende clones de Judy Garland o James Dean) y autorizada por la viuda de Wilder, Karen Wilder, que lo resumió así: "Gene tenía una capacidad extraordinaria para llevar humor, asombro y corazón a la vida de la gente."
Ese permiso no es un trámite menor. La legislatura de California aprobó en agosto de 2024 la AB 1836, en vigor desde enero de 2026, que exige el consentimiento de los herederos para recrear digitalmente a un actor fallecido, precisamente después de que Disney acumulara demandas por casos parecidos (Peter Cushing en 'Rogue One' o Christopher Reeve en 'The Flash').

articles.title: Le Canada menace d'attaquer en justice le Français OVHcloud, qui refuse de lui fournir des données
articles.text:
Accusé de ne pas avoir respecté une ordonnance de communication canadienne datant de 2024, OVHcloud risque désormais des poursuites pénales. L'hébergeur français fait valoir la souveraineté juridique de ses filiales et prépare sa défense.
Ce week-end, l'hébergeur français OVHcloud a confirmé être visé par une menace de poursuites judiciaires au Canada, qui lui reproche de ne pas s'être conformé à une ordonnance de communication d'informations privées vieille de plus de deux ans. Dans le détail, il s'agit des données d'abonnés liées à des serveurs situés hors du territoire canadien, réclamées directement par les autorités, qui ne sont pas passées par les canaux diplomatiques habituels. Pour une entreprise qui bâti une bonne partie de son image sur la protection juridique de ses clients, c'est un vrai problème. OVHcloud, lancé dans un bras de fer, promet de se défendre « vigoureusement ».
Le bras de fer entre OVHcloud et le Canada autour de la protection des données
Avec l'affaire opposant OVHcloud au Canada, nous voilà avec un vrai cas d'école de souveraineté et de test de crédibilité de cette souveraineté. Le 19 avril 2024, en invoquant un article du Code criminel canadien, la justice locale avait exigé d'OVH France et de sa filiale OVH Canada la communication de données d'abonnés et de comptes. Le souci, c'est que ces informations concernent des adresses IP rattachées à des serveurs hébergés par d'autres filiales du groupe, situées hors du Canada, donc a priori hors de sa portée juridique directe. Un détail cocasse évidemment, puisqu'OVHcloud exploite justement deux datacenters sur le sol canadien, mais ce n'est pas là que se trouvent les données recherchées.
Deux ans plus tard, faute d'avoir obtenu ce qu'elles réclamaient, les autorités canadiennes ont décidé d'accélérer les choses. Elles menacent désormais d'attaquer OVH France et OVH Canada en justice, pour non-conformité à l'ordonnance de communication, et entrave à la justice, rien que ça.
L'hébergeur fondé et dirigé par Octave Klaba ne compte pas plier. Dans un communiqué publié ce week-end, le groupe affirme avoir « agi de bonne foi », dans le respect de ses obligations légales, aussi bien françaises que canadiennes. Son argument est que chaque filiale OVH est une entité juridique indépendante, régie par les lois du pays où elle opère, et non par celles de sa maison-mère.
La souveraineté numérique, le nerf de la guerre
OVHcloud ne faut pas contester d'ailleurs, puisque l'entreprise propose aussi une porte de sortie. Elle rappelle l'existence des traités d'entraide judiciaire internationale, les fameux MLAT, conçus précisément pour ce type de demande transfrontalière. D'après OVH, les autorités françaises ont fait savoir qu'une requête passée par ce canal serait traitée en quelques semaines seulement. Une voie plus longue qu'une simple ordonnance, certes, mais qui au moins respecte les prérogatives de chaque pays.
Octave Klaba rappelle que son entreprise s'est bâtie sur « une promesse de confiance, de transparence et de souveraineté des données ». Il ajoute que ses équipes ont agi de manière licite tout au long du dossier et qu'elles défendront le principe de séparation juridique des filiales avec la conviction qu'il sera reconnu. Cela donne une idée du positionnement commercial et du caractère de la société qui, depuis des années, cultive son image d'alternative européenne face aux géants américains du cloud, eux soumis au très controversé CLOUD Act.
Et essayons de voir plus loin. Si le Canada obtenait gain de cause en s'appuyant sur la présence locale d'une filiale pour accéder à des données stockées à l'étranger, l'argument de la « séparation des entités », brandi par de nombreux acteurs du cloud pour vanter leur indépendance vis-à-vis des lois extraterritoriales, en sortirait sérieusement fragilisé. Il n'est pas question ici de jouer la surenchère, mais il y a un vrai enjeu pour le groupe nordiste, qui revendique le titre de premier fournisseur de cloud en Europe.

articles.title: YouTube deja de funcionar en estos celulares Android: qué hacer para ver videos
articles.text:
Varios teléfonos Android han dejado de ejecutar la aplicación de YouTube. La decisión de Google de dejar fuera de soporte a ciertas versiones antiguas de Android es el factor central de esta problemática, que afecta la experiencia de millones de usuarios en todo el mundo.
Durante años, Google había mantenido una política de soporte extendido para sistemas operativos Android antiguos, permitiendo que dispositivos lanzados incluso hace más de una década continuaran accediendo a servicios clave.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué algunos celulares ya no pueden abrir YouTube
Google anunció oficialmente el fin del soporte para los Servicios de Google Play en dispositivos con Android 6.0 Marshmallow, versión lanzada en 2015. Esto implica que estos teléfonos ya no recibirán actualizaciones en segundo plano ni parches de seguridad, y pierden la capacidad de ejecutar correctamente aplicaciones que dependen de dichos servicios.
El núcleo del problema radica en que los Servicios de Google Play son responsables de la autenticación de cuentas, servicios de ubicación, notificaciones push y la seguridad a través de Google Play Protect. Además, permiten que aplicaciones de terceros utilicen funciones como Google Maps y gestionan la instalación y actualización de apps desde la Play Store.
PUBLICIDAD
Al dejar de funcionar estos servicios, las aplicaciones más utilizadas —como YouTube— pierden acceso a funciones críticas y pueden bloquearse por completo.
Actualmente, para mantener la compatibilidad con Google Play, un teléfono debe tener Android 7.0 Nougat o superior. Los celulares que aún funcionan con Android 6.0 Marshmallow han quedado oficialmente fuera del alcance de nuevas actualizaciones, inaugurando una nueva etapa en la que los dispositivos antiguos dejan de ser considerados en la evolución del ecosistema de Google.
PUBLICIDAD
La aplicación de YouTube, en particular, es una de las primeras en bloquear el acceso a versiones anteriores del sistema operativo. Al intentar abrirla en un teléfono afectado, aparece un mensaje que sugiere utilizar la versión web a través del navegador móvil.
El motivo principal de este cambio es la necesidad de garantizar la seguridad y estabilidad de las aplicaciones. Google Play Protect, que deja de actualizarse con el fin del soporte, era la última barrera contra malware y amenazas digitales. Sin este escudo, los teléfonos se vuelven más vulnerables, lo que lleva a Google a incentivar la actualización de los dispositivos o la migración a modelos más recientes.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué modelos y versiones quedan afectados por el bloqueo
Los teléfonos afectados son aquellos que aún utilizan Android 6.0 Marshmallow o versiones anteriores. Este sistema operativo, que llevaba casi 11 años disponible, representaba hacia fines de 2025 apenas el 0,4 % de los dispositivos activos conectados a los servidores de Google. Sin embargo, esa minoría aún cuenta con millones de usuarios en todo el mundo.
La retirada del soporte para Marshmallow marca el ciclo de vida más extenso que una versión de Android haya tenido, superando incluso el de Lollipop (Android 5), que se mantuvo activo durante más de nueve años.
PUBLICIDAD
Los fabricantes de dispositivos, como Google y Samsung, ya han anunciado que los modelos nuevos contarán con actualizaciones garantizadas por un máximo de siete años, pero una amplia gama de teléfonos lanzados antes de esa política queda excluida de esta cobertura.
Entre los dispositivos más afectados se encuentran modelos de gama media y baja de años anteriores a 2017, que por limitaciones técnicas o falta de soporte del fabricante nunca pudieron actualizarse a versiones superiores de Android. Además, algunos equipos de marcas menos conocidas tampoco recibieron actualizaciones oficiales más allá de Marshmallow.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué alternativas existen para ver videos de YouTube en estos dispositivos
Ante la imposibilidad de abrir la aplicación oficial de YouTube, los usuarios de teléfonos con Android 6.0 o inferior pueden recurrir a la versión web del servicio. Al ingresar a YouTube.com mediante el navegador móvil, se accede al contenido de la plataforma, aunque con una experiencia menos fluida y sin algunas funciones avanzadas presentes en la app.
El mensaje que aparece al intentar abrir YouTube en estos dispositivos invita expresamente a utilizar esta alternativa, que permanece disponible para navegadores compatibles. No obstante, la navegación puede verse entorpecida por la falta de optimización de algunos navegadores antiguos, la ausencia de notificaciones push y la imposibilidad de reproducir videos en segundo plano o descargar contenidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, la descarga de aplicaciones desde repositorios de terceros no soluciona el problema, ya que la mayoría de las versiones actuales de YouTube y otras apps clave requieren versiones de Android más recientes. Incluso si se logra instalar una versión antigua, la falta de actualizaciones y soporte expone al usuario a fallos de funcionamiento y a riesgos de seguridad, como la presencia de malware o fuga de datos personales.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Les astronomes ont mesuré “la plus grande galaxie connue” : le résultat dépasse l’imagination
articles.text:
Les astronomes ont mesuré “la plus grande galaxie connue” : le résultat dépasse l’imagination
Longue de 1,7 million d'années-lumière, IC 1101 est la plus gigantesque galaxie jamais observée. Grâce à de nouvelles images d'une profondeur inédite, des astronomes ont pu mesurer ses dimensions avec une précision inégalée et découvrir qu'elle continue de dévorer les galaxies qui l'entourent.
Il fallait aller chercher la lumière la plus faible de l'Univers pour découvrir l'ampleur réelle du monstre. Une équipe internationale vient en effet de réaliser les images les plus profondes jamais obtenues d'IC 1101, la plus grande galaxie connue à ce jour. Verdict : ce colosse cosmique s'étend sur près de 520 kiloparsecs, soit environ 1,7 million d'années-lumière. Et son expansion n'est manifestement pas terminée.
Située au centre de l'amas de galaxies Abell 2029, à un peu plus d'un milliard d'années-lumière de la Terre, IC 1101 est une galaxie elliptique géante. À titre de comparaison, notre Voie lactée mesure environ 100 000 années-lumière de diamètre. La nouvelle championne est donc 17 fois plus vaste.
Mais comment mesurer un objet aussi gigantesque ?
Le défi est considérable, car les régions périphériques d'IC 1101 sont si ténues qu'elles se confondent presque avec le fond du ciel. Pour les distinguer, les chercheurs ont utilisé le télescope Isaac Newton, installé aux Canaries, et développé une méthode capable d'éliminer la lumière parasite provenant des étoiles voisines et de l'instrument lui-même.
Les scientifiques ont ensuite analysé la luminosité et la répartition des étoiles afin de déterminer l'endroit où la galaxie s'arrête réellement. Ils estiment que son corps principal s'étend jusqu'à environ 260 kiloparsecs de son centre, soit un diamètre total d'environ 520 kiloparsecs. Un kiloparsec correspond à 3200 années-lumière.
Cette taille hors norme s'accompagne d'une masse tout aussi spectaculaire. IC 1101 renferme près de 3 400 milliards de fois la masse du Soleil sous forme d'étoiles, soit plusieurs dizaines de fois la masse stellaire de notre propre galaxie, estimée elle autour de 200 milliards de masse solaire.
17 fois plus grand, c'est la différence entre la France et la Chine
Il faut imaginer la France et la Chine pour avoir une idée du mastodonte que représente IC 1101. Si le Système solaire était vers son centre, il y a fort à parier que la densité d'étoiles - donc de soleils - nous offrirait des nuits presque aussi claires que le jour.
Un autre exemple parlant est que le diamètre de IC 1101 représente plus de la moitié de la distance qui sépare la Voie lactée de notre voisine galactique Andromède.
Et elle continue de grandir en absorbant des galaxies plus petites
Les observations révèlent également des structures diffuses et asymétriques autour de la galaxie. Elles témoignent probablement de la lente absorption de galaxies plus petites, un phénomène parfois qualifié de “cannibalisme galactique”. Autrement dit, IC 1101 continue de grandir en engloutissant progressivement son voisinage. L'équipe le précise clairement : IC 1101 “montre des signatures claires de l'assemblage de masse en cours”.
Malgré ses dimensions vertigineuses, IC 1101 n'a sans doute pas atteint sa taille définitive. Même à l'échelle de l'Univers, certains géants continuent de prendre du poids.

articles.title: Piratage massif de bitcoins : un hacker a dépouillé des milliers d'investisseurs, 88 millions de dollars de cryptos volées
articles.text:
Dans la nuit du 30 juillet 2026, un cybercriminel a mené une attaque d’envergure contre 500 portefeuilles Bitcoin. En l’espace de seulement 25 minutes, l’attaquant siphonne environ 594 bitcoins, soit près de 38 millions de dollars. L’opération cible spécifiquement des adresses détenant plus de 0,15 BTC, dont des adresses dormantes depuis plusieurs années.
Peu après cette première offensive, les analystes de Galaxy Research, qui documentent l’affaire en temps réel, se rendent compte que d’autres vols sont en cours. Deux autres vagues d’attaques sont recensées dans la journée du 31 juillet. Au total, ce sont 4 500 adresses différentes qui se font dépouiller. Plus de 1 367,05 BTC, soit environ 88,6 millions de dollars, ont été volés au cours de la cyberattaque.
À lire aussi : Un Bitcoin à seulement 5000 dollars – ce pirate a berné le système pour dérober 23,7 millions de dollars
Une faille de sécurité à l’origine de l’attaque
Toutes les attaques reposent sur une faille de sécurité dans Coldcard, les portefeuilles physiques développés par la société canadienne Coinkite. Toutes les adresses qui ont été siphonnées étaient liées à des hardwares wallets de la marque. Il s’agit d’une vulnérabilité dans le firmware de Coldcard, qui remonte à 2021. Elle est passée inaperçue pendant des années avant que des pirates n’exploitent la défaillance pour mener une cyberattaque. Normalement, ces portefeuilles Coldcard devaient générer leurs clés secrètes grâce à une puce de sécurité, spécialement conçue pour produire des mots de façon aléatoire. De cette façon, il est impossible qu’un tiers devine la clé secrète qui permet d’accéder au portefeuille.
Malheureusement, une erreur d’intégration a poussé les portefeuilles touchés à générer une clé secrète en s’appuyant sur des informations qui ne varient pas, comme le numéro de série de la puce et l’heure approximative de fabrication. De facto, il a été possible de deviner la clé secrète qui a pourtant été générée comme il se doit par le wallet. En mettant la main sur quelques informatiques, le pirate est parvenu à deviner la phrase de sécurité de nombreux détenteurs de cryptos.
 COLDCARD Mk3 Security Advisory
If you generated a seed on a Mk3 after firmware 4.0.1, your funds may be at risk.
Mk4, Q and Mk5 are not affected based on our early analysis.
Read the advisory and migrate carefully:https://t.co/3vgPHOjMS7
— COLDCARD (@COLDCARDwallet) July 30, 2026
À lire aussi : La France annonce le blocage de Polymarket, le site de paris crypto qui fait un carton
Mise à jour d’urgence
Face à la vague d’attaques contre ses clients, Coinkite a déployé un firmware d’urgence pour tous les modèles et toutes les versions concernées. La société canadienne précise qu’il ne suffit pas d’installer la mise à jour pour se protéger. Si les truands ont déjà généré une phrase de récupération en exploitant la faille, ils conservent un accès à l’adresse. Les utilisateurs exposés doivent créer une toute nouvelle phrase de récupération sur un appareil qui a été mis à jour. Ensuite, ils doivent transférer l’intégralité de leurs fonds vers les nouvelles adresses générées à l’occasion.
« La version 4.2.0 corrige la génération de nouvelles clés de récupération. Elle ne peut pas réparer une clé de récupération déjà générée par un firmware affecté », explique bien Coinkite, qui souligne que le fait de « précipiter la migration d’un portefeuille peut engendrer un risque plus immédiat que le problème que vous tentez de résoudre ».
 Even hardware wallets can have bugs. Even old wallets (with long history) can have bugs.
How to mitigate? Split your funds in a few wallets maybe? This has a different set of risks. Nothing is 100%.
Stay informed. Stay SAFU! https://t.co/9CHiNlbJbz
— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) August 1, 2026
 🚨 UPDATE: We halted COLDCARD shipments as soon as we confirmed the vulnerability. All remaining units at our facilities with affected firmware installed were destroyed.
Some orders had already shipped. We contacted those customers directly by email with the advisory and…
— COLDCARD (@COLDCARDwallet) August 2, 2026
Cette cyberattaque d’ampleur relance le débat sur les limites des portefeuilles physiques, qu’on présente souvent comme l’ultime rempart contre les vols de cryptomonnaies. Changpeng Zhao, fondateur de Binance, a d’ailleurs rappelé que même les portefeuilles les plus anciens et réputés peuvent comporter des failles. L’entrepreneur conseille donc aux investisseurs de systématiquement répartir leurs cryptomonnaies « sur plusieurs portefeuilles ».

articles.title: World’s smallest GPU silicon passes real-world testing — 240,000-transistor TinyGPU v2.0 renders 3D graphics at up to 15 FPS while v3.0 prepares for 2026 release
articles.text:
World’s smallest GPU silicon passes real-world testing — 240,000-transistor TinyGPU v2.0 renders 3D graphics at up to 15 FPS while v3.0 prepares for 2026 release
TinyGPU v3.0 will feature a programmable pixel shader.
We wrote about the world’s tiniest GPU heading to production last November. Its developer, Pongsagon Vichit, has now received the finished silicon back from the Tiny Tapeout community, where it was part of the SKY 25b shuttle. “ASIC TinyGPU v2.0 is alive and working!!!” cheered the amateur ASIC/FPGA designer on social media. That’s definitely worth celebrating, and we are also happy to hear that TinyGPU v3.0 will arrive towards the end of this year.
Above you can see the TinyGPU v2.0 SKY 25d “standalone GPU” silicon in action. At the beginning of the embedded video, Vichit has a rather low-polygon model on screen that is being manipulated by a game controller in real time. The second demo, showing a colorful zooming and rotating globe representing the Earth, is more impressive.
According to the TinyGPU v2.0 GitHub, this GPU can perform transformation & lighting plus rasterization with a maximum of 1,000 triangles on screen. It also features one dynamic directional light, flat shading, backface culling, and affine texture mapping. This finished sliver of silicon, packing around 240,000 transistors, also offers a 4-bit double buffer and an 8-bit depth buffer stored on QSPI RAM, according to its designer.
In our earlier reporting, we noted that TinyGPU v2.0 was tested using a Basys3 FPGA host. This test only managed frame rates in the demo of between 7.5 and 15 FPS. The Tiny Tapeout silicon won’t run any faster than the FPGA, Vichit previously indicated, and indeed, the on-screen action doesn’t look any more fluid.
TinyGPU v3.0 ASIC details and delivery schedule
No sooner has TinyGPU v2.0 materialized than the excitement over TinyGPU v3.0 begins to build. The next-gen TinyGPU had already been submitted to Tiny Tapeout’s upcoming run before TinyGPU v2.0 was actually received and tested by Vichit. “But we all know that GPU is a cut-throat business — must release new models fast,” joked the enthusiast.
New and significant in TinyGPU v3.0 is the programmable pixel shader. In other social media posts about this upcoming GPU, Vichit reveals that it will boast the following pixel shader specs:
- Lightweight DirectX 8 PS 1.1–inspired design
- SIMD (4 pixels in parallel)
- 31 instructions per shader (tweaking)
- 26-op instruction set
- Branching via masked execution
- 4x 8-bit temp registers
With the new pixel shader in parallel with Z-buffer access, and near/far plane culling plus guard band clipping, big fidelity gains are teased. A far more detailed, textured, and animated model should be the result with little to no performance impact.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
One of the earliest TinyGPU v3 demos featured a chameleon to pay tribute to the Nvidia GeForce 3, reputed to be the first programmable shader GPU for consumers. That milestone was achieved in a PC graphics card that launched a quarter of a century ago (Feb 2001).
The latest information about TinyGPU v3 mentions that the finished ASIC should be delivered in December 2026 or January 2027.

Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: 7 Books that make you realise you can't control everything
articles.text:
7 Books that make you realise you can't control everything
Discover seven insightful books that explore uncertainty, acceptance, and the freedom that comes from letting go of control.
Many of us spend a surprising amount of time trying to control life. We plan every detail, worry about future outcomes, replay past mistakes, and attempt to manage how others think, feel, or behave. Yet despite our best efforts, life remains unpredictable. People change. Plans fall apart. Opportunities appear unexpectedly. Challenges arrive without warning.
The more we try to control every outcome, the more frustrated and anxious we often become. Some of the most powerful books on personal growth, philosophy, and psychology remind us of a difficult but liberating truth: we cannot control everything. What we can control is how we respond.
7 books that explore the wisdom of letting go
1. The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck by Mark Manson
Many struggles come from trying to control things that were never meant to be controlled. Mark Manson challenges the idea that a perfect life comes from avoiding problems or constantly chasing approval. Instead, he explains that peace comes from accepting difficulties, choosing what truly matters, and letting go of the things outside our influence.
The book teaches readers that they cannot control every outcome, other people's opinions, or every challenge they face. What they can control is how they respond and where they choose to direct their energy. For anyone learning to accept uncertainty and stop fighting against reality, The Subtle Art of Not Giving a Fck* offers a practical perspective on focusing only on what truly matters.
2. The Wisdom of Insecurity by Alan Watts
Alan Watts argues that much of human anxiety comes from our desire for certainty. We want guarantees about careers, relationships, health, and the future. But life offers very few guarantees. Watts suggests that attempting to eliminate uncertainty only increases stress because uncertainty is woven into existence itself. The book encourages readers to embrace the present moment rather than constantly seeking control over what comes next. Its message is both challenging and deeply freeing.
3. When Things Fall Apart by Pema Chödrön
Life inevitably includes disappointment, loss, and unexpected change. In this compassionate and insightful book, Pema Chödrön explores what happens when our carefully constructed plans collapse. Instead of resisting uncertainty, she encourages readers to remain open to it.
The book teaches that suffering often increases when we insist that reality conform to our expectations. Acceptance, on the other hand, allows us to move through difficulties with greater resilience and wisdom.
4. The Black Swan by Nassim Nicholas Taleb
Many people believe the world is more predictable than it actually is. Taleb explores how rare and unexpected events, what he calls "Black Swans", often have enormous consequences. These events frequently shape history, careers, economies, and personal lives in ways that no one could have predicted.
The book challenges the illusion of control and highlights the limits of forecasting and planning. Readers come away with a deeper appreciation for uncertainty and adaptability.
5. Man's Search for Meaning by Viktor E. Frankl
Frankl's experiences in Nazi concentration camps led him to a profound realisation about control.
Even when nearly every external freedom had been taken away, individuals retained the ability to choose their attitude and response. This insight became the foundation of his philosophy.
The book demonstrates that while circumstances may be beyond our control, meaning and dignity can still be found through our choices. It remains one of the most powerful explorations of human resilience ever written.
6. The Book of Joy by the Dalai Lama and Desmond Tutu
Through conversations about happiness, suffering, and human experience, the Dalai Lama and Desmond Tutu repeatedly return to the theme of acceptance. The book acknowledges that pain, uncertainty, and disappointment are unavoidable parts of life.
Rather than trying to control every circumstance, the authors encourage cultivating gratitude, compassion, and perspective. Their approach offers a more sustainable path to peace than the endless pursuit of control.
7. Everything Is F*cked: A Book About Hope by Mark Manson
In this philosophical and often provocative book, Mark Manson examines humanity's desire for certainty, control, and predictability. He argues that many people struggle because they expect life to be controllable and fair. When reality fails to meet those expectations, frustration follows.
The book encourages readers to focus less on controlling outcomes and more on developing values, resilience, and perspective. Its message aligns with a timeless truth: life is unpredictable, but our response to it matters enormously.
What stays with us
Letting go of control can feel uncomfortable because it requires accepting that some questions will remain unanswered and some outcomes will remain uncertain. Yet it can also be incredibly liberating. Whether it's the Stoic wisdom of Meditations, the philosophical insights of The Wisdom of Insecurity, the compassionate guidance of When Things Fall Apart, the unpredictability explored in The Black Swan, the resilience of Man's Search for Meaning, the perspective of The Book of Joy, or the modern reflections of Everything Is Fcked*, these books remind us of an important truth: You do not need to control everything to live a meaningful life.
Sometimes peace begins when you stop fighting uncertainty and start learning how to live alongside it.

articles.title: Bolsa del trabajo de CSIC: qué es, requisitos y cómo presentar tu solicitud para acceder a ella
articles.text:
Vamos a decirte qué es y cómo acceder a la bolsa de trabajo del CSIC, el Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas de España. Se trata de una institución pública a la que pueden intentar acceder los científicos cualificados.
Vamos a empezar diciéndote qué es y qué requisitos se piden para poder acceder a las ofertas laborales del CSIC. Luego, te diremos el proceso con el que puedes acceder a esta bolsa y realizar tu solicitud para acceder a un empleo.
Índice de Contenidos (3)
CSIC y su bolsa de trabajo
El CSIC es la mayor institución pública dedicada a la investigación científica en España. Es un organismo público adscrito al Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades, y ocupa el tercer lugar entre los organismos públicos de investigación de Europa.
Con todo esto, es normal que haya muchos científicos que quieran intentar entrar a trabajar en esta institución. Para facilitar el proceso, el CSIC tiene una bolsa de trabajo online, a la que cualquiera puede inscribirse para intentar acceder a alguna de sus vacantes.
En cuanto a las vacantes, las convocatorias que suele realizar el CSIC en su bolsa de trabajo van dirigidas a la contratación de investigadores y personal técnico. Estas personas tendrán que encargarse de contratos de investigación, proyectos y convenios.
En esta bolsa de empleo del CSIC podrás optar a acceder a trabajos que engloban todas las áreas relacionadas con el organismo, que son las siguientes:
- Biología y Biomedicina
- Humanidades y Ciencias Sociales
- Ciencias Agrarias
- Ciencias y Tecnologías de Alimentos
- Recursos Naturales
- Ciencias y Tecnologías Físicas
- Ciencias y Tecnologías de Materiales
- Ciencias y Tecnologías Químicas
Requisitos para acceder a la bolsa de trabajo
Para poder acceder a las ofertas del trabajo publicadas por el CSIC, debes cumplir con una serie de requisitos. Algunos de ellos son iguales para todos, mientras que otros dependen del grupo al que pertenezcan las ofertas. Esta es la lista de requisitos:
- Nacionalidad Europea: Los candidatos deben tener nacionalidad española o de un estado miembro de la Unión Europea.
- Titulación requerida: Obviamente, es imprescindible tener la titulación requerida para cada tipo de vacante. Aquí, las titulaciones se dividen en dos grupos diferentes:
- Titulación para Grupo 1: Máster, Licenciatura, Ingeniería, Doctorado o Arquitecto.
- Titulación para Grupo 2: Titulación de diplomado, Ingeniería Técnica, Arquitectura Técnica o equivalente.
- Tener las capacidades: Además de la titulación, es importante tener las capacidades para desempeñar las funciones propias de los puestos de trabajo ofertados.
- Sin expedientes disciplinarios: La persona candidata no debe haberse separado de administraciones públicas mediante expedientes disciplinarios.
Accede a la bolsa de trabajo
Para acceder a la bolsa de trabajo del CSIC, tienes que entrar en la web de su sede electrónica. La dirección es sede.csic.gob.es/tramites/bolsa-de-trabajo. Esto te llevará a la página principal, donde tienes que pulsar en Acceso a la aplicación de Bolsa de trabajo del CSIC. Esto lo tienes en un botón granate a la derecha de la página.
Esto te llevará a la página donde tienes que identificarte para acceder al sistema. Puedes hacerlo con tu nombre de usuario y clave en el caso de que te hayas registrado, pero también con el sistema Cl@ve.
Esto te llevará a la página principal. En ella, puedes crear solicitudes de acceso a las distintas bolsas de trabajo que tiene disponibles el CSIC. Simplemente, mira la bolsa de la lista a la que quieres entrar, y pulsa en Crear Solicitud.
Y esto te llevará a la página donde tienes que configurar detalladamente tus datos para la solicitud. Tendrás que poner tus datos personales, pero también los académicos, tus áreas científicas, tu experiencia laboral en investigación, las becas que has tenido, y en definitiva todo con lo que desde el CSIC puedan saber si eres la persona adecuada para los puestos que se oferten.

articles.title: MENA startups raise $173 million in July 2026 as Saudi Arabia regains the lead
articles.text:
MENA startups raise $173 million in July 2026 as Saudi Arabia regains the lead
MENA startup funding rose modestly in July 2026, but the rebound was largely debt-driven, with equity investment remaining subdued.
Startups across the Middle East and North Africa raised $172.6 million across 45 deals during the first month of the second half of 2026, up 16% from June but still 78% below the amount recorded in July last year.
The monthly increase therefore offers only a partial improvement. Debt accounted for 56% of total funding in July, compared with 11.5% in June and just 2% in July 2025.
Saudi Arabia returns to the lead
Saudi Arabia reclaimed the top position in July after failing to lead the regional rankings throughout the first half of the year. Startups based in the kingdom raised $106.6 million across 16 transactions, accounting for nearly 62% of the month’s total funding.
The UAE matched Saudi Arabia’s deal count, with 16 transactions, but ranked second by value after attracting $46.6 million.
Syria emerged as an unexpected third-place market, overtaking Egypt after three startups collectively secured $10.16 million. Egypt, which frequently ranks among the region’s three largest startup markets, raised $7.25 million across eight deals.
Morocco ranked fifth after one startup raised $2 million, while Qatar recorded a single transaction worth an estimated $100,000.
The country distribution, however, remained highly concentrated. Saudi Arabia and the UAE together accounted for almost 89% of all capital raised during the month, leaving the rest of the region with just over $19 million.
E-commerce takes the largest share
E-commerce returned to the top of the sector rankings in July, attracting 55% of total investment. The result, however, was driven by a limited number of sizeable transactions rather than broad-based activity across the sector.
Govtech ranked second following a $15 million round raised by Whiteshield.
Super apps came third after two startups, one based in Syria and the other in Morocco, collectively raised $12 million.
Despite falling out of the top three sectors by funding value, fintech remained the most active sector by deal count. The sector recorded nine transactions worth a combined $10.9 million, highlighting continued investor appetite for fintech startups despite smaller cheque sizes. Proptech followed closely in terms of deal count, with eight deals that collectively raised $11.9 million.
The sector rankings underline the concentration of July’s investment activity. A small number of transactions shaped the overall picture, while most other sectors attracted comparatively limited capital.
Early-stage rounds dominate
No mega deals or late-stage rounds were announced in July, leaving early-stage startups to dominate both deal value and volume.
A total of 33 early-stage startups raised $49 million, reflecting continued investor preference for smaller cheques and earlier entry points.
Another nine startups did not disclose their funding stages, accounting for $27.5 million that could not be assigned to a specific stage.
While the absence of large late-stage transactions reduced the headline total, the number of early-stage deals suggests that investors remain active at the lower end of the market, albeit with more limited capital commitments.
B2B startups capture most funding
B2B startups maintained their lead over other business models, raising $136 million across 33 transactions. They accounted for nearly 79% of all capital deployed during the month.
Consumer-facing startups secured $13.3 million across five deals, while companies serving both businesses and consumers raised $23.3 million through seven transactions.
The gap reflects investors’ continued preference for business-focused models, which are often perceived as offering clearer revenue visibility and more predictable customer economics during uncertain market conditions.
Female founders remain underfunded
Funding for female-founded startups remained marginal in July.
Startups founded solely by women raised $1.7 million across four transactions, equivalent to less than 1% of the month’s total investment.
Male-founded startups received 97% of all funding, while four companies founded by mixed-gender teams collectively raised $3 million.
The imbalance remains one of the most persistent structural gaps in the regional ecosystem. Although female-founded companies continue to appear in the deal count, the capital allocated to them remains disproportionately small.
July’s figures point to a market that improved slightly in headline terms but remained dependent on debt and a narrow group of transactions. Saudi Arabia’s return to the top and the rise of e-commerce reshaped the monthly rankings, yet the absence of mega deals and late-stage rounds shows that investors are still exercising caution.
The second half of 2026 has therefore begun with higher funding than June but not yet with a meaningful recovery in equity investment. Whether the improvement gains momentum will depend on the return of larger rounds and a broader distribution of capital across countries, sectors and founder profiles.
These monthly reports are a collaboration between Wamda and Digital Digest.

articles.title: Lista de celulares que se quedan sin Netflix desde el 3 de agosto de 2026
articles.text:
Desde el 3 de agosto de 2026, la aplicación nativa de Netflix dejará de funcionar en una amplia gama de celulares antiguos. Esta decisión afecta tanto a usuarios de Android como de iPhone cuyos dispositivos ya no pueden instalar las versiones más recientes de sus sistemas operativos.
La plataforma streaming ya no permitirá abrir, actualizar ni instalar la app en los celulares afectados. Los usuarios deberán buscar alternativas para acceder a contenidos, porque la interrupción impacta tanto en el acceso a películas y series como en la disponibilidad de nuevas funciones y actualizaciones de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué celulares Android se quedan sin la app de Netflix
Entre los dispositivos Android que pierden acceso a Netflix se encuentran modelos lanzados entre 2011 y 2014. Entre los celulares afectados figuran el Samsung Galaxy S3, Galaxy Note 2, Galaxy Grand Prime, LG Optimus L5, Optimus L7, LG G2 y los Sony Xperia Z, Xperia Z1 y Xperia E3.
Estos teléfonos no pueden ejecutar versiones recientes del sistema operativo Android, lo que los deja sin posibilidad de recibir futuras actualizaciones de seguridad y funciones.
PUBLICIDAD
La imposibilidad de actualizar el sistema operativo limita el funcionamiento de la aplicación y expone a los usuarios a riesgos de seguridad, sumado a impactar en el uso de servicios críticos como mensajería y banca digital.
Cuáles modelos de iPhone no podrán acceder a la aplicación de Netflix
La restricción alcanza a modelos iPhone que no sean compatibles con iOS 18.0 o versiones superiores. Entre los modelos afectados se encuentran el iPhone X, iPhone 8 y 8 Plus, iPhone 7 y 7 Plus, iPhone 6s y 6s Plus, el iPhone SE de primera generación y cualquier modelo anterior.
PUBLICIDAD
Quienes continúan utilizando estos dispositivos tendrán que considerar una actualización para mantener el acceso a Netflix y a otras aplicaciones esenciales para la vida diaria. El cese del soporte implica el fin de futuras actualizaciones, lo que incrementa las vulnerabilidades.
Cómo saber si un dispositivo es compatible con Netflix y otras aplicaciones
Para determinar si un celular podrá seguir usando Netflix u otras aplicaciones, es fundamental verificar la versión del sistema operativo. En Android, se debe ingresar al menú ‘Configuración’ o ‘Ajustes’, seleccionar la opción ‘Acerca del teléfono’ y consultar ‘Información del software’, donde aparece la versión de Android y el nivel de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
En el caso de los iPhone, esta información se encuentra en ‘Configuración’, sección ‘General’ y luego en ‘Información’. Comprobar estos datos permite anticipar tanto la exclusión del servicio streaming como la de otras aplicaciones que requieren sistemas actualizados para operar correctamente y proteger la información personal.
Qué otros dispositivos pierden acceso a la aplicación de Netflix
La decisión de Netflix alcanza a dispositivos como los Apple TV de primera, segunda y tercera generación, así como a televisores inteligentes fabricados antes de 2015 por marcas como Panasonic, LG y la línea Samsung Smart TV serie EOS (2012-2015).
PUBLICIDAD
El cambio afecta a varios televisores, reproductores multimedia y dispositivos de streaming, modificando la experiencia de usuario y aumentando la exposición a riesgos de seguridad.
Por qué las aplicaciones dejan por fuera de soporte a dispositivos antiguos
La principal razón detrás de la restricción es la seguridad. Los dispositivos sin soporte de actualizaciones ni parches quedan expuestos a vulnerabilidades que incrementan el riesgo de malware, robo de datos y ataques informáticos.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, cuando un dispositivo queda obsoleto, aplicaciones esenciales como mensajería, banca, compras y autenticación pueden dejar de funcionar correctamente.
Netflix explicó que la falta de compatibilidad genera bloqueos, lentitud y fallas en procesos cotidianos, afectando desde la recepción de mensajes hasta la protección de cuentas personales. Todos los fabricantes sugieren actualizar los dispositivos para mantener la seguridad y el acceso a todas las funciones de la plataforma.

articles.title: Xbox : Microsoft augmente encore les prix en Europe, la Series S désormais au prix de lancement de la Series X
articles.text:
Que nous ayons été prévenus en amont ne change rien à l'affaire : la nouvelle augmentation des consoles Microsoft fait très mal.
La politique tarifaire de Microsoft continue de faire grincer des dents. Après plusieurs hausses successives, les consoles Xbox Series voient une nouvelle fois leurs prix grimper en Europe. Résultat : la Xbox Series S d'entrée de gamme est désormais vendue 499,99 €, soit le prix auquel la Xbox Series X avait été lancée en 2020.
Sponsorisé
Vous conservez l’électricité solaire produite en trop pendant la journée pour la réutiliser lorsque vos besoins augmentent.
Sponsorisé
Une inflation qui ne s'arrête plus
Les joueurs européens devront une nouvelle fois mettre la main au portefeuille. Microsoft a officialisé la nouvelle augmentation des prix de l'ensemble de sa gamme Xbox Series qui avait déjà été évoquée en juin dernier.
Comme prévu, cette augmentation concerne toutes les consoles Xbox Series et tous les marchés européens, que ce soit l'Allemagne, la France ou le Royaume-Uni, pour n'en citer que certains des plus importants. La hausse est plus particulièrement observable sur les modèles considérés comme les plus accessibles, traditionnellement présentés comme la porte d'entrée vers l'écosystème Xbox.
Le cas de la Xbox Series S 512 Go illustre parfaitement cette évolution. Commercialisée à 299,99 € lors de son lancement en novembre 2020, puis progressivement revalorisée au fil des années, elle atteint désormais les 499,99 €. Un montant symbolique puisqu'il correspond exactement au prix de lancement de la Xbox Series X – la console haut de gamme de Microsoft – il y a près de six ans. Avouez que le symbole est fort.
Microsoft invoque le coût des composants
Cette Xbox Series X augmente pour sa part de 200 € par rapport à ce prix de lancement. Elle se trouve aujourd'hui facturée 749,99 € dans sa version sans lecteur optique et 799,99 € avec lecteur optique.
Pour justifier cette nouvelle révision tarifaire, Microsoft met en avant la flambée persistante des coûts des composants, notamment de la mémoire vive et du stockage en mémoire flash. Une pression qui touche l'ensemble de l'industrie électronique, portée par une demande toujours plus forte en puces destinées aux infrastructures dédiées à l'intelligence artificielle.
Cette nouvelle hausse intervient alors que les consoles de salon suivent une trajectoire inhabituelle. Là où les prix avaient historiquement tendance à diminuer au fil des années, les PlayStation et autres Xbox Series enchaînent au contraire les revalorisations. Les consoles de Sony ont déjà connu des augmentations assez similaires et le prix de la Switch 2 de Nintendo devrait être réévalué en septembre prochain.

articles.title: Everyday IT Support For Uninterrupted Team Productivity - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Critical Role of IT Support in Modern Workplaces
In today’s fast-paced business environment, uninterrupted productivity is essential for maintaining a competitive edge. Teams rely heavily on technology to communicate, collaborate, and execute daily tasks efficiently. However, even minor IT disruptions can cascade into significant downtime, lost revenue, and decreased employee morale. This is where everyday IT support becomes a vital component of organizational success.
Effective IT support ensures that systems remain operational, software runs smoothly, and employees receive timely assistance whenever technical issues arise. With businesses increasingly adopting digital tools and remote work models, the demand for reliable IT support has escalated dramatically. According to a study by Gartner, businesses that implement robust IT support frameworks experience up to a 30% reduction in downtime, directly enhancing productivity and profitability.
Moreover, the integration of IT support into everyday business operations leads to improved employee satisfaction. When teams know that technical problems will be resolved quickly and efficiently, they remain focused on their core tasks without the anxiety of prolonged disruptions. This reliable support infrastructure is no longer a luxury but a necessity in the digital age.
Onsite Support: Enhancing Immediate Problem Resolution
One of the most effective ways to maintain seamless IT operations is through onsite support services. Unlike remote assistance, onsite support provides hands-on intervention, enabling technicians to diagnose and resolve issues directly at the workplace. This approach minimizes delays and ensures that hardware or network problems are addressed swiftly.
Businesses looking for reliable onsite support by WPG can benefit significantly from the immediate presence of skilled professionals who understand the local infrastructure and can tailor solutions accordingly. Onsite support often includes routine maintenance, system upgrades, and emergency repairs, all of which contribute to reducing unplanned downtime.
Industry research suggests that companies utilizing onsite support experience a 25% faster resolution time for critical IT issues compared to those relying solely on remote help desks. This speed in addressing problems translates to less disruption and smoother workflows, keeping teams focused on their core responsibilities.
Furthermore, onsite support fosters better communication between IT professionals and end users. Technicians can observe the work environment firsthand, identify potential risks, and provide personalized training or advice to prevent future issues. This direct interaction builds trust and encourages a proactive approach to IT management within the organization.
Cloud and Network Support: The Backbone of Productivity
Beyond physical hardware, much of today’s business activity depends on cloud services and robust network infrastructure. Ensuring these systems are consistently monitored and maintained is crucial for uninterrupted productivity. IT providers offer comprehensive network management and cloud support services, which include security updates, performance optimization, and data backup solutions.
Organizations that explore XL.net’s offerings gain access to tailored IT support plans designed to safeguard data integrity and optimize connectivity. With cyber threats on the rise, maintaining secure and reliable networks is non-negotiable. According to a recent report by Cybersecurity Ventures, cybercrime damages are expected to reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, highlighting the importance of proactive IT security measures.
Cloud computing not only offers scalability and flexibility but also demands vigilant monitoring to prevent service interruptions. Network support ensures that bandwidth is sufficient, latency is minimized, and systems are configured to handle peak loads without faltering. Regular audits and penetration testing are also part of comprehensive cloud and network support, helping organizations identify vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.
By integrating cloud and network management into everyday IT support, businesses can reduce the risk of outages and data breaches, ensuring that team productivity remains uninterrupted. This integration also supports remote workforces by providing secure, reliable access to company resources from any location, further contributing to operational continuity.
Proactive Maintenance and Support: Preventing Issues Before They Occur
Proactive IT support involves continuous monitoring and regular maintenance to detect and resolve potential issues before they impact operations. This preventive strategy minimizes unexpected downtime and extends the lifespan of IT assets.
Routine tasks such as software updates, patch management, hardware diagnostics, and system health checks are essential components of proactive support. These activities help identify vulnerabilities, optimize system performance, and prevent failures that could halt business activities.
Statistics show that companies investing in proactive IT support reduce their unplanned downtime by nearly 50%, significantly improving operational efficiency. This approach not only safeguards productivity but also contributes to better budget management by avoiding costly emergency repairs.
In addition to technical benefits, proactive maintenance fosters a culture of continuous improvement within IT teams. By analyzing trends and recurring issues, organizations can implement strategic upgrades and refine their IT infrastructure to better support evolving business needs. This foresight is especially valuable as companies scale or adopt new technologies.
Empowering Employees Through IT Support
Another critical aspect of everyday IT support is empowering employees with the tools and knowledge they need to troubleshoot minor issues independently. IT support teams often provide training sessions, user guides, interactive FAQs, and quick-response help desks to assist staff promptly.
When employees feel confident in managing basic technical problems, the overall burden on IT personnel decreases, allowing them to focus on more complex challenges. This empowerment fosters a more resilient and agile workforce capable of maintaining productivity even during minor disruptions.
Moreover, employee empowerment through IT support enhances job satisfaction and reduces frustration. When users understand how to use their devices and applications effectively, they are more productive and less likely to encounter preventable errors. Many organizations have seen a 20% increase in employee productivity after implementing comprehensive IT training programs.
IT support teams also benefit from this strategy by building stronger relationships with end users. By serving as educators and problem solvers, support staff become trusted partners rather than mere troubleshooters, which improves overall organizational communication and collaboration.
Choosing the Right IT Support Partner
Selecting an experienced and responsive IT support provider is crucial for maximizing the benefits of everyday IT assistance. Companies should look for partners offering comprehensive services, including onsite support, cloud management, cybersecurity, and proactive maintenance.
Additionally, providers with strong local presence and industry-specific expertise can tailor their offerings to meet unique business needs. Transparent communication, rapid response times, and scalable solutions are also key factors to consider.
It is also important to evaluate an IT support partner’s ability to align with your company’s growth plans. As businesses evolve, IT demands increase and change. A flexible partner who can adapt services accordingly prevents future bottlenecks and ensures continued productivity.
Many organizations report that partnering with a reliable IT support provider leads to a 40% reduction in IT-related downtime and a corresponding increase in employee satisfaction. This partnership becomes an investment in operational excellence, not just a cost center.
Conclusion
In conclusion, everyday IT support is indispensable for ensuring continuous team productivity in today’s technology-driven workplace. By investing in reliable onsite support, robust network and cloud management, proactive maintenance, and employee empowerment, businesses can minimize downtime, enhance operational efficiency, and maintain a competitive advantage.
The complexity of modern IT environments demands a strategic approach that combines immediate problem resolution with long-term prevention. Organizations that embrace comprehensive IT support frameworks not only safeguard their daily operations but also position themselves for sustainable growth and innovation.
In an era where technology underpins nearly every aspect of business, uninterrupted productivity is no longer optional-it is essential. Prioritizing everyday IT support is the key to unlocking your team’s full potential and driving success in a constantly evolving digital landscape.

articles.title: The InkLeaf is a dual-screen e-paper tablet that folds like a notebook, so you can hold it like a hardback
articles.text:
The InkLeaf is a dual-screen e-paper tablet that lets you read on one display and take notes on the other
Updating the notebook for 2026
- The InkLeaf is a notebook-like dual-screen ereader
- It opens like a book and lets you read on one screen while making notes on the other, using a stylus
- It's shipping to early buyers this month at a hefty discount
In recent years we’ve seen all sorts of e-paper innovations, from e-paper phones like the Hisense A10 to absolutely tiny ereaders like the Xteink X4 Pro, and now another unusual device is on the way, dubbed the InkLeaf.
This is a dual-screen ereader that folds open like a notebook. So the design is a bit like that of the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and other foldable phones, except it’s using E Ink for its displays, and it’s not using foldable screens.
Instead, you get a pair of 10.3-inch E Ink Carta displays, and an aluminum frame between them. That also means the screens are much bigger than on Samsung's foldable, putting each display more in line with a tablet.
The idea here is that you can hold and fold it like a notebook, and that, thanks to having two screens, you can read from one and take notes on the other. For example, you might have a textbook open on one display and note paper on the other — though you can also directly annotate whatever text you’re viewing too.
The InkLeaf, then, is designed primarily for work, study, and research, though given that it opens and folds like a book, it could also be appealing to read novels on for anyone who otherwise prefers hardbacks.
The InkLeaf is also just 4.2mm thick when open and 8.4mm thick when closed, so it’s no thicker than a notebook, and it weighs just 480g. Plus it has a speaker, microphones, 64GB of storage, and a battery that promises weeks of life per charge.
Unclear software and a high price
The InkLeaf runs Android under the hood, though it’s not clear what version of Android this is, or whether it includes access to the Google Play Store. It also supports PDF, EPUB, MOBI, TXT, and HTML files.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The InkLeaf comes with a stylus for all your note-taking needs, supporting 4096 levels of pressure, and this supposedly provides the friction of real paper, so it won’t feel like you’re writing on a screen.
And, of course, this being 2026, the InkLeaf also includes AI, allowing you to search for handwritten phrases across all of your notes, and with summaries and an outline assist planned post-launch.
At full price, this ereader isn’t cheap, with an MSRP of $999 (around £740 / AU$1,425), but you can reserve one now for delivery worldwide on InkLeaf's site for just $489 (roughly £365 / AU$700) — that’s the ‘founder price’, and requires paying a refundable $9.99 (approximately £7.50 / AU$14) deposit ahead of when it ships sometime this month.
As well as getting you a big discount, this is also an early access launch — following that, it will land on Kickstarter, with most units not shipping until 2027.
So if you want the InkLeaf early and affordably, you should reserve one soon. Of course, doing so comes with all the perils of being an early adopter, and means you won’t get a chance to read reviews before making a purchase decision.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds. Make sure to click the Follow button!
And of course you can also follow TechRadar on TikTok for news, reviews, unboxings in video form, and get regular updates from us on WhatsApp too.
James is a freelance phones, tablets and wearables writer and sub-editor at TechRadar. He has a love for everything ‘smart’, from watches to lights, and can often be found arguing with AI assistants or drowning in the latest apps. James also contributes to 3G.co.uk, 4G.co.uk and 5G.co.uk and has written for T3, Digital Camera World, Clarity Media and others, with work on the web, in print and on TV.
