articles.title: How IT Consulting Optimizes Everyday Technology Decisions - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Complexity of Technology in Business
In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, businesses face an ever-growing array of technology choices. From cloud computing and cybersecurity to software integration and data analytics, technology decisions have become increasingly complex and critical to operational success. While many companies strive to manage these decisions internally, the specialized knowledge required often exceeds the capacity of in-house teams. This is where IT consulting emerges as a vital asset, offering expert guidance to optimize technology choices that align with business goals.
According to a recent survey, 70% of organizations reported that they struggle to keep up with the pace of technology change, highlighting a significant challenge for businesses striving to stay competitive. This statistic underscores the urgency for companies to seek external expertise to navigate the complex technology landscape effectively.
Moreover, the rapid advancement of technologies means that what is cutting-edge today may become obsolete tomorrow. This pace of change necessitates continuous learning and adaptation, which can strain internal resources. IT consultants not only bring current knowledge but also anticipate future trends, enabling businesses to make proactive, rather than reactive, technology decisions. This foresight is essential in maintaining a competitive edge and avoiding costly missteps.
The Role of IT Consulting in Everyday Technology Decisions
IT consulting firms specialize in analyzing a company’s current IT environment and future needs to recommend the most suitable technology solutions. These consultants bring a wealth of experience across various industries, enabling them to identify pitfalls and opportunities that may not be apparent to internal teams. By leveraging their expertise, businesses can make informed decisions about technology investments, implementation, and management.
An excellent example of this expertise can be found through Protek’s IT professionals. Their IT professionals provide comprehensive assessments that help organizations understand the implications of adopting new technologies, ensuring alignment with business objectives and compliance requirements.
Beyond initial technology selection, IT consultants play a crucial role in the ongoing management and optimization of IT systems. They assist with change management, staff training, and establishing governance frameworks that ensure technologies continue to deliver value over time. This ongoing support helps organizations adapt to shifting business needs and evolving technological landscapes without disruption.
Furthermore, IT consulting can help bridge the gap between technical teams and business leadership. Consultants often act as translators, converting complex technical jargon into understandable insights that inform strategic decision-making. This communication facilitates better collaboration across departments, aligning technology initiatives with broader business goals.
Streamlining IT Strategy with Proven Methodologies
Adopting a structured methodology is crucial for effective IT consulting engagements. Frameworks that emphasize assessment, planning, implementation, and review allow consultants to deliver consistent and measurable results.
Prototype IT’s methodology exemplifies this approach by employing a methodology designed to tailor IT solutions precisely to their clients’ operational and strategic needs.
The structured nature of such methodologies helps businesses avoid common pitfalls, such as underestimating resource requirements or overlooking security vulnerabilities. Research shows that 63% of IT projects exceed their budget or timeline due to poor planning and management. Utilizing a proven IT consulting methodology can significantly reduce these risks, leading to more successful project outcomes.
In addition, these methodologies often incorporate best practices for risk assessment and mitigation, ensuring that potential challenges are identified early and addressed proactively. This approach not only safeguards project timelines and budgets but also enhances the overall quality and effectiveness of technology implementations.
By following a disciplined process, IT consulting firms can also facilitate better stakeholder engagement and transparency throughout the project lifecycle. Regular progress reviews and clear communication channels help maintain alignment and build trust, which are critical factors in the success of any technology initiative.
Enhancing Cybersecurity and Risk Management
One of the most critical aspects of everyday technology decisions is cybersecurity. With cyberattacks increasing in frequency and sophistication, organizations must prioritize robust security measures. IT consultants evaluate current security postures and recommend enhancements that protect sensitive data and ensure regulatory compliance.
Data from Cybersecurity Ventures predicts that global cybercrime costs will reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, underscoring the urgency of effective security strategies. This staggering figure highlights the growing financial risks associated with inadequate cybersecurity.
IT consultants help organizations adopt a multi-layered defense strategy, incorporating technologies such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, encryption, and endpoint protection. They also assist in developing comprehensive security policies and incident response plans, which are vital for minimizing damage in the event of a breach.
Moreover, consultants stay abreast of evolving regulatory requirements, such as GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA, ensuring that businesses maintain compliance and avoid costly penalties. By integrating cybersecurity into the broader IT strategy, consultants help businesses mitigate risks and foster trust with customers and partners.
Regular security assessments and penetration testing conducted by IT consultants can uncover vulnerabilities before malicious actors exploit them. This proactive stance is essential in today’s threat landscape, where attackers continuously develop new tactics.
Cost Efficiency and ROI Through Expert Advice
Making informed technology decisions can lead to significant cost savings and improved return on investment (ROI). IT consultants analyze the total cost of ownership (TCO) for various technology options, factoring in acquisition, maintenance, training, and potential downtime costs. This comprehensive perspective enables businesses to prioritize investments that deliver the greatest value.
Studies indicate that companies engaging IT consultants are 30% more likely to complete technology projects on time and within budget. This increased efficiency not only reduces unnecessary expenditures but also accelerates the realization of business benefits from new technologies.
Additionally, IT consulting can help organizations identify opportunities to consolidate systems, eliminate redundancies, and leverage cloud services to reduce infrastructure costs. For example, migrating to cloud platforms often results in lower upfront capital expenses and more flexible scalability, which can be optimized with expert guidance.
Consultants also assist in negotiating vendor contracts and service-level agreements (SLAs), ensuring that businesses receive favorable terms and reliable support. This expertise helps prevent hidden costs and service disruptions that can impact operations.
By focusing on strategic investments aligned with business priorities, IT consulting maximizes ROI and ensures that technology expenditures contribute directly to organizational growth and efficiency.
Facilitating Digital Transformation and Innovation
Beyond immediate technology decisions, IT consulting plays a strategic role in digital transformation initiatives. Consultants help organizations adopt emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which can drive innovation and competitive advantage.
By aligning technology adoption with business vision, IT consultants ensure that digital transformation efforts are purposeful and sustainable rather than reactive and fragmented. This foresight is essential in a business environment where 87% of executives believe digital transformation is a priority but only 40% feel their organization is fully prepared to execute it.
IT consultants guide companies through the complex process of integrating new technologies with existing systems, minimizing disruption while maximizing benefits. They also help establish metrics to measure the impact of digital initiatives, enabling continuous improvement and accountability.
Furthermore, consultants facilitate cultural change within organizations, encouraging innovation mindsets and agility. This human element is often overlooked but is critical for successful digital transformation, as technology alone cannot drive change without engaged and adaptable people.
By fostering innovation ecosystems, IT consulting supports businesses in exploring new business models, enhancing customer experiences, and creating data-driven decision-making capabilities that position them for long-term success.
Conclusion
In an era marked by technological complexity and rapid change, IT consulting stands out as a critical enabler of sound technology decision-making. By leveraging the expertise of specialized professionals like and adopting structured approaches exemplified by, businesses can optimize their technology investments, enhance cybersecurity, improve operational efficiency, and drive innovation.
The impact of these contributions is measurable: from reducing project overruns to mitigating cyber risks and accelerating digital transformation, IT consulting offers tangible benefits that empower organizations to thrive in a competitive marketplace. As technology continues to evolve, partnering with trusted IT consultants is not just a strategic advantage-it is a necessity for sustainable business success.
Through comprehensive assessments, proven methodologies, and a focus on both technology and people, IT consulting transforms complex technology landscapes into clear, manageable pathways that support business growth and resilience. This holistic approach ensures that technology decisions are not only optimized for today’s challenges but also future-proofed for tomorrow’s opportunities.

articles.title: Dieses Tool macht dein Smartphone zur Maus
articles.text:
Für Windows und macOS: Dieses Tool macht dein Smartphone zur Maus
Wenn der Akku der kabellosen Maus leer ist oder die kabelgebundene Peripherie aus unerfindlichen Gründen streikt, ist der Frust schnell groß. Schließlich gibt es dann keine schnelle Alternative, um den Computer zu steuern. Abhilfe schafft dabei ein kleines Tool, das du dir für Notfälle installieren kannst, um so die Maus mit deinem Smartphone ersetzen zu können.
Unified Remote: So wird das Smartphone zum Mausersatz
Das Tool mit dem Namen Unified Remote ist dabei für eine Vielzahl von Systemen und Geräten verfügbar. Auf der Smartphone-Seite werden Android- und iOS-Geräte und sogar Windows Phones unterstützt. Zudem kannst du die vereinheitlichte Fernbedienung auf Windows-PCs, unter macOS sowie für Linux und auf einem Raspberry Pi oder Arduino Yún installieren.
Sobald die App auf beiden Endgeräten installiert wurde, musst du nur noch sicherstellen, dass sie sich im selben Netzwerk befinden. Die Steuerung erfolgt über dein Wifi. Sind die Geräte miteinander verbunden, kannst du aus einer Reihe von vorgefertigten Fernbedienungen für diverse Apps auswählen. So gibt es etwa eine Fernbedienung, die Maus und Tastatur ersetzt, sowie eine spezialisierte Steuerung für Datei-Browser und die Medienwiedergabe.
Neben der kostenlosen Grundversion bietet Unified Remote aber noch eine Bezahlversion. Diese kostet einmalig 4,99 Euro und wird über die Smartphone-Version der Anwendung in den jeweiligen Stores freigeschaltet. Dadurch erhältst du Zugriff auf deutlich mehr Fernbedienungen, die dann auch für einzelne Dienste angepasst sind. Dazu zählen etwa Streaming-Dienste wie Disney Plus und Netflix, aber auch Browser wie Chrome und Firefox oder Anwendungen wie Blender.
In der Bezahlversion kannst du dir darüber hinaus auch eigene Fernbedienungen erstellen. Ebenfalls praktisch: Nachdem du bezahlt hast, kann Unified Remote nicht nur den Input vom Smartphone an deinen Computer, sondern auch das Bild von deinem Computer an dein Smartphone schicken. So kannst du jederzeit sehen, was passiert, auch ohne vor dem Rechner zu sitzen. In Kombination mit den Fernbedienungen, die sich schwebend über der App anpinnen lassen, kannst du die Inhalte sehen und gleichzeitig steuern.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro : 3 capteurs hyper hauts de gamme au programme
articles.text:
Attendue pour la génération précédente des Galaxy S26, l‘introduction d’un modèle pro au sein de la gamme des smartphones haut de gamme de Samsung revient à nouveau au cœur des rumeurs pour les futurs S27. Mais son positionnement n’a rien à voir avec ce que le Galaxy S26 Pro aurait pu être.
Contrairement à la dernière fois, le Galaxy S27 Pro ne viendrait pas remplacer le S27, mais il viendrait se glisser juste en dessous du S27 Ultra. Pour l’heure, il n’est pas clair s’il viendra remplacer ou non un Galaxy S27 Plus ou s’il s’ajoutera à l’ensemble de la gamme, la faisant passer de trois à quatre modèles.
Une configuration photo qui se précise pour le Galaxy S27 Pro
Toujours est-il que sa configuration photo commence à se préciser fortement. Un article du journal coréen ETNews table en effet sur l’introduction d’un capteur de 200 Mpx pour le grand angle, d’un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx et, élément tout à fait nouveau, de l’existence d’un téléobjectif équivalent X3 sur ce modèle, avec capteur de 12 Mpx.
Concrètement, cela voudrait dire qu’il proposerait une expérience similaire au Galaxy S27 en matière de téléobjectif, et se rapprocherait du Ultra sur les grand-angle et ultra-grand angle.
Un S27 Ultra bien différent
Pour rappel, le Galaxy S27 Ultra, le modèle au-dessus dans la gamme, devrait pour sa part, selon des rumeurs précédentes propagées par Ice Universe, passer de quatre à trois appareils photo. Il se débarrasserait en effet du moins musclé du lot, le téléobjectif X3, pour miser simplement sur un grand angle de 200 Mpx, un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx et un téléobjectif de 50 Mpx en équivalent X5. L’idée étant que l’espace entre le X1 et le X5 pourrait être couvert par le zoom numérique du grand angle offert par ses 200 Mpx, garantissant une perte pas trop importante.

articles.title: Atlético Nacional vs. Jaguares: por qué debes evitar Roja Directa, Pirlo TV y Fútbol Libre para ver el partido online
articles.text:
Atlético Nacional inicia su camino en la Liga BetPlay 2026-2 este domingo 2 de agosto, enfrentando a Jaguares en el estadio Jaraguay de Montería. El encuentro, programado para las 3:45 p.m. (hora de Colombia), despierta gran expectativa entre los hinchas, que buscan seguir en vivo todos los detalles del debut del equipo verdolaga, especialmente después de la postergación de su primer partido ante Boyacá Chicó.
Si bien la transmisión oficial corre por cuenta de Win Sports Premium, el auge de búsquedas en internet para “ver gratis” y la proliferación de portales como Roja Directa, Pirlo TV y Fútbol Libre plantean una pregunta crucial sobre los riesgos de recurrir a sitios no autorizados para seguir el fútbol online.
PUBLICIDAD
El atractivo y los riesgos del streaming no oficial
Los partidos de alto impacto son un imán para plataformas de streaming ilegal que prometen acceso gratuito, sin registro y en calidad supuestamente premium. La propuesta resulta tentadora para quienes no cuentan con una suscripción, pero esconde múltiples riesgos. Estos portales operan bajo dominios cambiantes, administradores anónimos y sin ningún canal de soporte.
Tras cada cierre judicial, reaparecen rápidamente copias que emulan el diseño y nombre del sitio original, confundiendo a los usuarios y dificultando la identificación de una fuente legítima.
PUBLICIDAD
El verdadero problema radica en la opacidad de estos servicios: no hay una empresa responsable detrás, ni garantías de privacidad o mecanismos para reclamar en caso de robo de datos, fraude o daños al dispositivo. Además, la ausencia de derechos oficiales implica que cualquier promesa de “señal HD” o “transmisión premium” debe tomarse con extrema cautela.
Trampas digitales y amenazas ocultas
Acceder a partidos por medio de páginas como Roja Directa, Pirlo TV o Fútbol Libre suele implicar un recorrido plagado de trampas tecnológicas. El proceso está lleno de ventanas emergentes, anuncios agresivos, botones de “play” falsos y solicitudes de registro que, lejos de ofrecer acceso directo al partido, dirigen al usuario a descargas de software potencialmente malicioso o a formularios que piden datos personales y bancarios.
PUBLICIDAD
Los especialistas en ciberseguridad advierten que estos días de alta demanda deportiva son aprovechados por los ciberdelincuentes para multiplicar páginas clonadas, aumentar la presión con mensajes urgentes y propiciar la descarga inadvertida de malware. Entre los riesgos más graves se encuentran la instalación de archivos dañinos capaces de robar contraseñas, secuestrar sesiones de apps financieras, acceder a fotos y documentos privados, o incluso tomar el control total del dispositivo.
En dispositivos móviles, el peligro crece si se conceden permisos como acceso a almacenamiento, notificaciones o accesibilidad. El malware puede propagarse a otros equipos conectados a la misma red WiFi, comprometiendo la seguridad de todos los dispositivos del hogar.
PUBLICIDAD
No todos los ataques requieren sofisticación técnica. Muchas de estas plataformas emplean estrategias de ingeniería social, diseñadas para que el usuario, apurado por no perderse el partido, termine entregando datos sensibles.
Es común encontrar mensajes que solicitan registrar una tarjeta bancaria para “verificar identidad”, completar formularios de validación sospechosos o prometer “acceso premium gratis” a cambio de información confidencial, lo que puede derivar en suplantación de identidad o cargos no autorizados.
PUBLICIDAD
Señales de alerta y recomendaciones
Entre los signos más frecuentes que deben levantar sospechas al navegar por estos portales destacan:
- Solicitudes para ingresar datos bancarios o personales.
- Formularios de registro y “validaciones” sin sentido.
- Mensajes sobre acceso inmediato solo tras compartir información confidencial.
Los expertos recomiendan evitar cualquier interacción con estos sitios, no instalar aplicaciones o extensiones ajenas a las tiendas oficiales y recurrir únicamente a las señales oficiales para ver partidos en línea. Optar por plataformas legales, aunque implique un costo, protege tanto la seguridad digital como la integridad financiera y la privacidad de los usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
En la era digital, la mejor jugada es siempre priorizar la seguridad y la protección de la información personal, evitando atajos que pueden salir muy caros.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: The infrastructure debt AI creates isn't in the code. It's in the operations
articles.text:
The infrastructure debt AI creates isn't in the code. It's in the operations
Enterprise AI success depends on operational discipline
Enterprise DevOps teams have adopted AI faster than they have adapted the operational systems that support it. Large language models generate Infrastructure as Code, deployment pipelines, and configuration files in seconds.
Development teams are delivering infrastructure changes at a pace that would have been implausible five years ago. Production environments have simultaneously become harder to reproduce, more difficult to govern, and more expensive to operate.
CEO at Quali.
The problem is easy to miss at first, because AI looks like a clear win in the early stages. A team asks an AI tool to set up some infrastructure. It works. The team expands how much they rely on it. More teams follow. More infrastructure gets created for testing, demos, experiments, and development. The organization ends up with far more moving parts than it had before, but far less ability to track them.
Not the full picture
The tools generating this infrastructure are good at describing what something should look like at the moment it's created. They're not built to watch what happens to it afterward, decide whether it's safe to make another change while one is already in progress, or notice when something has quietly drifted out of its intended state over the following weeks.
That kind of oversight used to come from experienced operations people making changes one at a time, in a predictable order, with a clear sense of what else was happening around them. AI removed the slow part of that process without replacing the judgment that made it manageable.
Now there are multiple people and multiple AI tools all making changes to the same systems around the same time, each one doing its job correctly in isolation, none of them able to see the full picture of what's happening across the environment as a whole.
The result looks familiar to anyone running infrastructure today. Environments that worked perfectly last week suddenly don't, and nobody can say exactly why. Cloud costs creep up steadily because nobody remembered to shut something down once it was no longer needed. Teams spend real, billable hours figuring out why two environments that were supposed to be identical have quietly diverged.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Security settings that were correct at launch slowly fall out of sync as everything around them keeps evolving independently. None of these are dramatic failures on their own. They're slow leaks, and slow leaks are much harder to notice and much more expensive to fix than sudden breaks.
Too much fragmentation
The teams responsible for infrastructure have been adjusting to this reality in real time. A few years ago, their main job was making things easy for developers, such as removing friction, giving people self-service access to what they needed, getting out of the way. That's still part of the job, but the role has expanded considerably.
Now they're expected to enforce rules across the organization, manage costs on increasingly expensive compute, track what's actually running where, and keep things consistent across a far more complicated set of environments than existed even two or three years ago. Bolting on another automated tool to handle some piece of that doesn't solve the underlying issue.
More often than not, it just adds another piece to a pile that's already too fragmented to manage well.
An environment isn't just the infrastructure sitting inside it. It's also everything connected to that infrastructure: who has access to what, what depends on what else, how much it actually costs to keep running, and how long it's supposed to stick around before someone should be cleaning it up.
Getting ahead of problems means building that kind of awareness directly into how infrastructure gets deployed and maintained, rather than discovering issues after the fact through documentation nobody reads regularly or incidents nobody wanted to have in the first place.
Processes should be built in
This becomes even more important as companies pour money into AI-specific hardware. Setting up GPU-powered environments isn't simply a matter of securing the hardware, it requires everything around that hardware, including networking, storage, security, and software, to come together correctly and stay that way.
Having the hardware on hand doesn't make that coordination problem any smaller. Only better processes do, and that process has to be built deliberately rather than assembled from whatever tools happened to be lying around.
The questions worth asking have changed as a result, even if a lot of organizations haven't caught up to that yet. How fast a team can generate infrastructure isn't the most useful thing to measure anymore and it was never really the hard part.
A better gauge is whether environments stay consistent over time, how often things drift without anyone noticing, how long unused environments sit around quietly costing money, and whether anyone in the organization can actually describe with confidence what's running in production at any given moment.
The companies that get the most lasting value out of AI won't necessarily be the ones using the most advanced or most numerous tools.
They'll be the ones that put just as much disciplined effort into managing what AI produces as they did into producing it in the first place and treating governance not as an afterthought, but as the thing that determines whether all that speed actually turns into something worth having.

articles.title: Enceinte portable JBL Flip Essential 2 à 79,99 € au lieu de 109,99 €
articles.text:
Pour les sorties en extérieur ou les fins d'après-midi au bord de l'eau, une enceinte portable robuste et étanche fait souvent la différence. La JBL Flip Essential 2, régulièrement citée parmi les meilleures enceintes à moins de 100 €, profite justement d'une remise chez Boulanger : 79,99 € au lieu de 109,99 €.
Positionnée dans la gamme d'entrée de JBL, cette enceinte mise sur la robustesse et la simplicité plutôt que sur des fonctionnalités avancées. Elle embarque une puissance RMS de 16 à 20 W selon les sources, avec deux haut-parleurs en configuration stéréo 2.0 couvrant une plage de fréquence de 65 Hz à 20 kHz. Certifiée IPX7, elle résiste à une immersion dans l'eau jusqu'à un mètre de profondeur pendant 30 minutes, un argument de poids pour une utilisation en bord de piscine ou à la plage.
Enceinte JBL Flip Essential 2 à 79,99 € au lieu de 109,99 €
Pourquoi choisir cette enceinte JBL Flip Essential 2 ?
- Une certification IPX7 qui autorise une immersion complète, pas seulement des éclaboussures
- Un format compact de 17,5 cm de long qui se glisse facilement dans un sac pour l'extérieur
- Un prix qui redescend sous les 80 €, en dessous du tarif moyen habituellement constaté autour de 99 €
Une autonomie qui dépend fortement du volume d'écoute
Plusieurs tests indépendants confirment que l'autonomie réelle de 10 heures annoncée par JBL se vérifie surtout à volume modéré, autour de 30% du potentiel maximal de l'enceinte. À volume élevé, cette même autonomie peut chuter à 5 ou 6 heures selon les mesures effectuées, un écart à connaître avant de partir en balade toute la journée sans prise de courant à proximité. D'autres tests plus favorables relèvent toutefois une autonomie oscillant entre 8 et 10 heures en usage courant, ce qui reste correct pour une utilisation quotidienne ou une sortie en extérieur classique.
Le compromis logique d'une enceinte d'entrée de gamme
Cette Flip Essential 2 se positionne clairement en dessous de la JBL Flip 6, sa grande sœur, avec une autonomie légèrement inférieure (10 heures contre 12 heures maximum) et l'absence de certaines fonctions avancées comme le mode PartyBoost pour connecter plusieurs enceintes entre elles. Le codec Bluetooth se limite au SBC, sans AAC ni aptX, ce qui peut légèrement affecter la qualité de streaming audio sur certains appareils compatibles avec des codecs plus avancés. Ces limitations restent cohérentes avec son positionnement tarifaire, la plupart des tests saluant un excellent compromis pour une enceinte nomade du quotidien plutôt qu'un modèle pour audiophiles exigeants.
✅ Les points forts
- Certification IPX7, résistance complète à l'immersion jusqu'à un mètre pendant 30 minutes
- Format compact et léger, facile à transporter en extérieur
- Charge rapide via USB-C, environ 3 heures pour une charge complète
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie réelle très dépendante du volume, pouvant chuter à 5-6 heures à fort volume contre 10 heures annoncées
- Codec Bluetooth limité au SBC, sans AAC ni aptX
- Absence de fonction PartyBoost pour connecter plusieurs enceintes JBL entre elles, contrairement à des modèles plus haut de gamme
Enceinte JBL Flip Essential 2 à 79,99 € au lieu de 109,99 €
À 79,99 €, la JBL Flip Essential 2 reste un choix pertinent pour une enceinte nomade robuste et étanche à petit prix, à condition de garder en tête que l'autonomie réelle dépendra fortement du volume d'écoute choisi. Une remise qui positionne ce modèle sous son prix moyen habituel, déjà considéré comme abordable sur le marché.

articles.title: Beltone Venture Capital exits BirdNest investment with 3.5x return
articles.text:
Beltone Venture Capital exits BirdNest investment with 3.5x return
- Egypt-based Beltone Venture Capital has completed a partial exit from Egyptian proptech BirdNest, generating a 3.5x return on invested capital and an 80% internal rate of return (IRR) over a two-year investment period.
- The transaction covered both Beltone Venture Capital's direct investment and its indirect stake through its joint fund with UAE-based Citadel International Holdings, while the firm retained a strategic stake in BirdNest.
- According to Ali Mokhtar, CEO and Managing Partner of Beltone Venture Capital, the partial exit reflects the firm's disciplined investment strategy while allowing it to return capital to investors and continue supporting BirdNest's next growth phase.
- Founded in 2019 by Mostafa Elnahawy, BirdNest offers a technology-powered marketplace for curated boutique hotels and holiday homes centred on art, wellness, and local experiences.
Press release:
Beltone Venture Capital has announced the successful partial exit from BirdNest, delivering a 3.5x return on invested capital and an 80% internal rate of return (IRR) over a two-year holding period.
The partial exit was executed across Beltone Venture Capital's direct stake and its indirect stake through the joint fund with UAE-based Citadel International Holdings, while Beltone Venture Capital continues to retain a strategic stake in BirdNest, reinforcing its confidence in the company's long-term growth potential.
Commenting on the milestone, Ali Mokhtar, CEO & Managing Partner of Beltone Venture Capital, said: "This outcome reflects the discipline of Beltone Venture Capital's investment approach from rigorous underwriting and active portfolio support to disciplined capital realization. This partial exit enables us to return capital to our investors while retaining a strategic stake in BirdNest. We remain committed to supporting the company's next phase of growth through Beltone's financial ecosystem and capabilities."
Mostafa Elnahawy, Co-Founder & CEO of BirdNest, added: “This milestone reflects the strength of BirdNest’s business model and the dedication of our team, partners, and investors. Over the past two years, we have achieved more than 10x growth in U.S. dollar revenue while reaching profitability. As we enter our next phase, we remain focused on creating sustainable long-term value and redefining hospitality through technology and exceptional guest experiences.”

articles.title: Google recibió 800.000 reservas para una app en 168 países. Su respuesta ha sido cancelarla
articles.text:
Google tiene en su haber un cementerio de aplicaciones y servicios donde fueron algunos de sus proyectos más conocidos. Google Reader es de los que recuerdo con más cariño, también el cliente de correo Inbox. A la empresa no le tiembla el pulso a la hora de matar servicios, el Chromecast es una buena muestra de ello. Ahora ha llevado su afán por las tijeras a una aplicación que aún no había salido: AI Studio para Android. La plataforma web sigue como hasta ahora.
Un adiós sin decir antes hola. El cementerio de Google es un lugar cargado de melancolía, de grandes ideas que no llegaron en el momento adecuado. Y de algunas que merecieron el final aunque Google se empeñase en mantenerlas con oxígeno, como Google+. El problema con AI Studio es que la aplicación no había salido aún al mercado. No solo eso: el número de reservas era altísimo, reconocido por la propia Google. Unas 800.000 en 168 países. Ahí estaba también la mía.
La app móvil de Google AI Studio se anunció en el pasado I/O como una herramienta para crear aplicaciones mediante inteligencia artificial y sin abandonar el teléfono. Iba a permitir la creación de software a golpe de prompt, instalarlo en el teléfono y usarlo directamente desde allí, todo de manera sencilla. La app ya aparecía en Google Play para el registro previo, pero ha desaparecido. Google asegura que tiene un plan B.
Un problema de coordinación. Google mantiene un equipo ingente de trabajadores, cada uno en su propia división. La comunicación entre departamentos no tiene fama de ser fluida, por eso Sundar Pichai ha ido reorganizando los equipos para mejorar la interacción entre ellos. Que una app de éxito anticipado se cancele podría explicarse por cierta desorganización entre los equipos de AI Studio, Android y Gemini, porque el giro ha sido hacia este último.
AI Studio aclara que la cancelación de la app no se debe a las bajas expectativas, solo a una reorganización. La app no verá la luz porque Gemini va a adquirir las habilidades planteadas de creación de aplicaciones Android y prueba directa en el dispositivo. Suena como un “mejor dejad a los que ya tienen una buena aplicación” dirigido al equipo de AI Studio, porque la idea tenía todo el sentido dentro del marco del vibe coding.
Gemini, la superapp. Google siempre se ha caracterizado por no tener miedo a desarrollar aplicaciones experimentales. De hecho, fomenta el desarrollo indie entre sus trabajadores, como con Android Experiments (que también está a un paso del cementerio, por cierto). Ahora parece que camina en sentido contrario, al de reducir el catálogo de software a la mínima expresión.
Gemini para Android se está convirtiendo en una superapp. No solo es un buscador, también un generador de texto, de imágenes, crea código, hace canciones, es una app de notas, de recordatorios… Y aspira a convertirse en el agente de Android. Con la cancelación de AI Studio para Android, Gemini puede convertirse en la llave maestra con la que crear nuestro propio software en el teléfono y para el teléfono. Ahora falta saber cuándo será eso, porque la app de AI Studio estaba a punto.
Una nueva promesa. El cementerio de Google está lleno de lápidas con fecha de nacimiento y fecha de defunción. La de AI Studio para Android solo tendrá la segunda. Y una cifra incómoda: 800.000 personas esperando una app que nunca existió, yo entre ellas. Ahora espero el equipo de Gemini cumpla lo que otro departamento de Google prometió.

articles.title: Ten years later, the iconic GTX 1080 Ti still holds up in 1080p gaming, but not without showing its age — Redux testing highlights the wonders of 11GB VRAM & the woes of time
articles.text:
Ten years later, the iconic GTX 1080 Ti still holds up in 1080p gaming, but not without showing its age — Redux testing highlights the wonders of 11GB VRAM & the woes of time
A card worthy of the GOAT status.
Few names echo in the aisles of tech cathedrals like the legendary GTX 1080 Ti, released by Nvidia all the way back in 2017. The GPU it's based on, GP102, actually debuted a year earlier, in 2016, which is why this story is titled as a decade-old hindsight. German outlet PC Games Hardware just retested all three cards based on the GP102, pitting them against far more efficient modern offerings to answer a simple question: how well does the 1080 Ti hold up in 2026?
At its launch, the GTX 1080 Ti cost $700 and used a cut-down version of the GP102 called "GP102-400," while the Titan Xp that released a month later enjoyed the full-fat GP102-450 silicon. Built on the Pascal architecture, the 1080 Ti featured 3,584 CUDA cores that could boost up to 1.58 GHz, 11GB of GDDR5X memory saturated across a 352-bit wide bus, and a 250W TDP. It was the last (consumer) flagship Nvidia made with pure rasterization in mind.
Jumping to the results, we see the 1080 Ti still pushes close to 60 FPS in modern titles at 1080p resolution. However, it's slower than even the current-gen RTX 5050, and it's unable to beat any recent 60-series GPU as well. You'd have to go as far back as the RX 6600 or the RTX 3060 8GB to find something that the 1080 Ti edges out. Speaking of which, it is still faster than the Radeon VIII that came out two years later and matches the relative performance of the Titan X, while the Titan Xp clears it comfortably.
As you'd expect, the older the game, the better the 1080 Ti performs. Though its large VRAM buffer helps it win in some areas. For instance, it's barely faster than the aforementioned RTX 3060 in Assassin's Creed Shadows, Battlefield 6, Days Gone, and Baldur's Gate 3. X4 Timelines and Spider-Man 2 are surprise cases where it's faster than even the RTX 4060 and RX 7600. Stalker 2 was the only game where the 1080 Ti managed to beat the RTX 5060 as well, once again because of that extra memory.
In recent titles, reliance on technologies like upscaling and ray tracing severely hurts the king of a bygone raster-only era. DLSS and ray tracing were both mocked at the time they debuted, but have become integral parts of the industry now. Pascal lacks any Tensor or dedicated RT cores, forcing it to fall back to software emulation, which is basically unplayable. DOOM: The Dark Ages and the new Indiana Jones game wouldn't even boot on this GPU.
Averaged across all resolutions and 20 different games, testing shows the RX 5700 XT and RTX 2070 as its closest contemporaries. At 1080p, the resolution you'll actually play at, it's slightly more performant than the RX 6600 and RTX 2060 6GB, while being smoked by almost every midrange card from the last five years. Not to mention, even this performance requires an absurd amount of power by today's standards.
The GTX 1080 Ti posted the worst efficiency numbers on the chart, second only to the Radeon VII. The aging architecture mixed with the 16nm process node combines to give it a rating of 0.085 FPS per watt. In comparison, the current-gen RTX 5060 achieved 0.202 FPS per watt, meaning the 1080 Ti wastes 58% more energy under load, while the RTX 5080 had the best results at 0.253 FPS per watt.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Today, cards like the RTX 5070 have 250W TDPs, and they're almost three times as fast with that kind of power consumption. Not to mention, they're significantly cheaper compared to the 1080 Ti when adjusted for inflation. So, you're paying more for less performance, fewer features, and less efficiency, but maybe not less longevity, since the card is almost a decade old already. Keep in mind that Nvidia has stopped pushing driver optimizations for Pascal at this point as well.
If you want to check out all the benchmarks in detail, make sure to give our friends at PC Games Hardware a visit. Their excellent testing originally included comparisons against the Titan X and Titan Xp, since both use the same GPU, but neither of them is as illustrious as the 1080 Ti. The outlet actually argues its GOAT status and crowns the 2080 Ti as the true visionary, and the charts certainly back that up.
The answer to the question asked at the start is rather straightforward. If you already own the 1080 Ti and only have a 1080p monitor, you can still just about get by, though you're missing out on a lot. However, given the state of the PC hardware industry right now, it would be sacrilegious to recommend upgrading from an icon that championed the people's voice for so long. So if you don't find yourself wishing for more performance, features, or efficiency, ride that 1080 Ti till its dying breath!
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Hassam Nasir is a die-hard hardware enthusiast with years of experience as a tech editor and writer, focusing on detailed CPU comparisons and general hardware news. When he’s not working, you’ll find him bending tubes for his ever-evolving custom water-loop gaming rig or benchmarking the latest CPUs and GPUs just for fun.

articles.title: Alles nur Hype? So wenige durch KI aufgedeckte Schwachstellen wurden tatsächlich aktiv ausgenutzt
articles.text:
Sicherheitsexperten zeigen: Nur ein Prozent der durch KI aufgedeckten Schwachstellen wurde wirklich ausgenutzt
Zahlreiche Verantwortliche von diversen Diensten, Webseiten und Anwendungen kämpfen aktuell mit demselben Problem. Durch KI-Tools, die Sicherheitslücken in ihren Werken in kürzester Zeit aufspüren können, werden sie mit Sicherheitsberichten überschwemmt. Das hat jetzt schon dazu geführt, dass unter anderem GitHub Änderungen am Bug-Bounty-Programm durchgeführt hat. Eine Untersuchung von Vuln Check zeigt indes, dass nur wenige der per KI aufgespürten Lücken wirklich zur aktiven Gefahr geworden sind.
So viele aktive Sicherheitslücken konnte KI aufspüren
Als Grundlage hat Vuln Check dafür zwei Datensets herangezogen. Zunächst analysierten die Sicherheitsforscher:innen Cybersecurity-Meldungen, bei denen Anthropics KI als Mitwirkende genannt wird. Die Daten gehen dabei bis zum April 2026 zurück, als Anthropic Project Glasswing angekündigt hatte. Dazu kommen Daten der Berkeley Vulnerability Research Initiative, die ebenfalls KI-gestützte Sicherheitsmeldungen aufzeichnet.
Insgesamt konnten die Sicherheitsforscher:innen so auf Daten von 1.061 KI-Meldungen zurückgreifen. Im Anschluss haben sie untersucht, ob es Anzeichen dafür gibt, dass die Lücken aktiv ausgenutzt wurden. Das Ergebnis: Nur 14 der über 1.000 gemeldeten Lücken wurden schon von Hacker:innen ausgenutzt. Alle anderen sind zwar echte Lücken in den Systemen, aber wurden weder von Angreifer:innen noch von Verteidiger:innen vorab gefunden.
Die Sicherheitsforscher:innen schreiben dazu, dass mit KI gefundene Sicherheitslücken zwar Wert für Angreifer:innen und Verteidiger:innen haben, aber die Daten nicht darauf hindeuten, dass die Schwachstellen häufiger als solche ausgenutzt werden, die händisch aufgespürt wurden. Sie ergänzen: „KI scheint die Anzahl der Schwachstellen, die entdeckt werden können, so zu erhöhen, dass Verteidiger:innen die Möglichkeit haben, sie zu identifizieren und zu schließen, bevor Angreifer:innen damit etwas machen können.“
Dennoch ist der Zeitraum, bis veröffentlichte Sicherheitslücken ausgenutzt werden, deutlich geschrumpft. Lag er 2025 noch bei 120 Tagen nach der Bekanntmachung einer Schwachstelle, sind es in der ersten Jahreshälfte 2026 lediglich noch 80 Tage. Sicherheitslücken werden also nicht schneller ausgenutzt, bevor sie bekannt werden, aber nach der Veröffentlichung schneller von Angreifer:innen rekonstruiert und gegen ungeschützte Dienste und Geräte eingesetzt.
Abschließend schreibt Vuln Check dazu: „Aktuell bekommen Verteidiger:innen durch den Zugang zu fortschrittlichen KI-Modellen eher einen Vorteil durch das Stärken ihrer Software, als Angreifer:innen darin, Sicherheitslücken vor den Softwareproduzent:innen zu finden. […] Das bedeutet aber nicht, dass das Risiko imaginär wäre. Es bedeutet, dass die echten Auswirkungen noch moderat sind und es trotzdem wichtig ist, ein genaues Auge darauf zu behalten, wie sich die Technologie entwickelt, als nur auf den Hype zu reagieren.“

articles.title: Why even the biggest brands have low AI readiness
articles.text:
Why even the biggest brands have low AI readiness
Brands must increase AI visibility and reduce AI misinformation risks
“AI readiness” tends to be used as umbrella phrase to describe the different range of activities that businesses need to carry out to get value of generative AI and minimize any associated risks.
AI readiness therefore takes into account everything from having the right data foundations and governance in place to supporting AI literacy among staff to establishing ethical guardrails.
Founder of AAAnow.
One area where businesses – including even large brands – are collectively not ready for AI is ensuring their brand is visible and faithfully represented across Large Language Models (LLMs) and in responses from associated AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude.
The outside-in view
Too many large companies have a digital estate that contains content that is outdated or contradictory. Because AI tools base their responses on the content they find, brands risk AI tools giving out misinformation or misrepresenting their brand, products or organization.
Similarly, there is also a risk of brands not being featured in responses or less than those compared to competitors, impacting future visibility and competitiveness.
This is effectively AI looking from the “outside in” and then presenting a picture of what it has surfaced. When we measured this “outside in” element of AI readiness across the websites of over 250 top global brands using an automated remote website assessment tool and an underlying AI maturity model, we found only approximately 3% of websites could be considered “leading” when it comes to AI readiness.
Why AI readiness is important
The way people search for information on the web is changing rapidly. Consumers are turning to ChatGPT rather than using traditional Google searches; surveys have suggested that 37% of consumers in the US who already use AI, now start their searches using AI tools rather than Google.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This means that rather than looking at a web page on a company’s own website, consumers’ perceptions about a brand are increasingly coming from AI responses as the first step rather than directly from a web page controlled by the company.
That’s a problem if a consumer asks AI to provide a list of suppliers or vendors, and your business isn’t listed when it should be, or the AI provides erroneous information about your company and products from the off.
Recognizing the speed at which consumers are turning to AI tools for search, digital marketing teams who have previously invested in Search Engine Optimization (SEO) are now investing in related practices like Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Answers Engine Optimization (AEO) with some urgency to optimize their digital footprint so it is successfully reflected in AI tools like ChatGPT.
But the reasons that even some of the world’s top brands still have a lot of work to do in this area is because in the past they have deprioritized basic governance and maintenance across their digital estate, with the risk of AI confidently presenting answers as facts or broadcasting perceptions that are based on information from content that is out of date and has been superseded.
Of course, the risks associated with erroneous answers may vary but they can be acute, particularly in heavily regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare or pharmaceuticals with strict compliance surrounding the information that businesses must provide to customers, or in areas such as products where health and safety instructions must be correct.
The hidden digital footprint
One of the key reasons where businesses slip up is by building up a digital footprint – often without realizing it – which is not actively managed and has old and inaccurate information.
Over time, businesses accumulate a surprisingly large number of digital assets that are accessible online, sometimes hosted on third-party platforms: websites for sub-brands or locations, online newsletters, campaigns, product launches, events, microsites, partner content, customer portals, forms, digital experiments, and so forth. In addition, there might be areas of a corporate website that have effectively been forgotten about.
Over the years, this digital footprint in some organizations has not been properly managed, so a site created to support a one-off event stays online indefinitely rather than being retired. Sometimes when a company acquires another, it also becomes responsible for this digital debris that has accumulated and which the new team have little awareness of the full footprint they have inherited.
Previous research we carried out between 2017 and 2023 shows that central digital teams can be unaware of up to 41% of their entire digital footprint.
The danger of poor document management
Another critical cause of a lack of AI readiness is an overreliance on documents. Many websites contain PDF attachments which don’t necessarily get updated and then accumulate over years and years, containing information which is no longer relevant or correct.
Annual reports, brochures, manual forms, product guides and more are all left accessible on websites. Our research suggests that as many as one in five (19%) website documents are duplicates which can create inconsistent signals for AI about which is the current and authoritative version
Not enough organizations take a structured approach to managing their documents across their digital estate, which means they cannot effectively update documentation for example to reflect brand, regulatory or operational changes, with AI now forming responses from these out-of-date files.
How to reduce risk exposure
As more businesses find AI is producing misinformation about them and the number of consumers who use AI tools for searching information increases, awareness of this problem is likely to rise.
To reduce the risk exposure, at a high-level, three things generally need to happen:
- The issue needs to be owned at the executive or board level with someone responsible to tackle it.
- Digital teams need to use automated assessment tools to measure and monitor the risk associated with their entire digital estate in order to track associated remedial action.
- The digital team need to put governance and lifecycle management processes in place that enables them to have more control and oversight over their digital footprint, so it avoids becoming a digital wild west again.
AI readiness covers many areas. A key priority for brands who want to maximize AI visibility while reducing the chance of misinformation is to get their digital estate under control. Of course, there are other important activities to consider including ensuring content is optimally structured, but reducing the amount of out-of-date content is a critical starting point.

articles.title: Operation Sindoor architect AK Bharti signs off after 39 years
articles.text:
Operation Sindoor architect AK Bharti signs off after 39 years
Air Marshal A.K. Bharti retired on 31 July 2026 after a distinguished career spanning frontline fighter operations, strategic appointments and a defining role in Operation Sindoor.
Air Marshal AK Bharti, the officer who became the public face of the Indian Air Force during Operation Sindoor, retired on 31 July 2026 after 39 years in uniform. He spent his last morning in service at the National War Memorial in New Delhi, laying a wreath for soldiers who never got a retirement of their own. He stepped down as Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, a post held since 1 June 2025, and was succeeded by Air Marshal Tejpal Singh on 1 August 2026.
The man nobody had heard of
Until the second week of May 2025, Awadhesh Kumar Bharti was a name known inside Air Headquarters and almost nowhere else. That changed on 11 May, when he sat at the National Media Centre in New Delhi alongside Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai and Vice Admiral AN Pramod for the first joint briefing on Operation Sindoor. He spoke in short sentences, declined to guess at figures he could not confirm, and recited a couplet from the Ramcharitmanas from memory to explain the shift in India's posture. The lines describe Lord Ram's patience with the sea running out after three days, after which he lifts his bow.
He was born in Jhunni Kala village in Bihar's Purnea district, to Jiwachh Lal Yadav, who worked in the finance department of the Kosi Irrigation Projects, and Urmila Devi. In 1977 he was one of 140 boys admitted to Sainik School Tilaiya. Six years later, 28 of that batch cleared the National Defence Academy examination. He was among them. At the NDA he won the President's Silver Medal and set a cross country record that stood for years, which is where the nickname Galloping Horse came from. At the Air Force Academy, Dundigal, he finished first in overall merit and took the Sword of Honour.
Four thousand hours and a Sukhoi squadron
Commissioned into the fighter stream on 13 June 1987, Bharti logged more than 4,000 hours across the MiG-21, MiG-29, Su-30MKI and Su-30MKM. He qualified as a Fighter Combat Leader and earned three stars for accident free flying. He was Flight Commander of No. 24 Squadron before taking command of No. 30 Squadron in August 2005, a tenure to September 2007 that placed him at the centre of operationalising the Su-30MKI's weapon systems. Under his command the squadron took part in exercises including Gagan Shakti, Indradhanush 2006 and Garuda 2007. He later commanded a frontline fighter base at Lohegaon, and as Air Attaché in Malaysia trained Malaysian pilots on the Su-30MKM.
The staff appointments mattered as much. At Strategic Forces Command and then Air Headquarters, he held jobs concerned with how India would fight rather than how it trains. Promoted to Air Marshal on 1 September 2023, he became Senior Air Staff Officer at Central Air Command in Prayagraj, and took over as Director General of Air Operations in October 2024.
What does the Director General of Air Operations actually do
The DGAO sits at Air Headquarters and owns the air operations brief for the entire service: target sets, force allocation, tasking across commands and the air defence picture over Indian territory.
A political decision to strike is not a flying programme. Somebody has to convert intent into aircraft, weapons, routes, timings and the defensive cover that brings crews home. That conversion happens at the DGAO's desk, which is also why offence and air defence sit under the same appointment.
Fifteen days, then nine targets
Operation Sindoor followed the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025, in which 26 civilians were killed. Fifteen days later, in the early hours of 7 May, India struck nine terrorist sites in Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir, including facilities at Bahawalpur and Muridke. When Pakistan retaliated, the IAF shifted to military targets while the air defence network absorbed drones and missiles.
Asked at the briefings what weapons had been used and what damage they had caused, Bharti said only that the methods chosen had produced the desired effects on enemy targets. On Pakistani aircraft, he said their planes had been prevented from crossing, that a few had been brought down, and that all Indian pilots were back home. He credited the Integrated Air Command and Control System and indigenous platforms such as Akash, and tied that capability to a decade of sustained budgetary backing. Pakistan has disputed Indian accounts of the exchange.
He was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal in 2008, the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal on Republic Day 2024, and the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal, the highest of India's wartime distinguished service awards, in the honours list announced on 14 August 2025.
What he leaves behind
As Deputy Chief, Bharti spent his final year pushing indigenisation harder than the timelines were comfortable with. At an industry event in September 2025, he told manufacturers that even 99% indigenous content counts for little if critical components remain import dependent, and that innovation needed to move off cruise setting. That argument, more than any single operation, is the brief his successor inherits, at a moment when the IAF is chasing squadron strength, an indigenous engine and the AMCA programme at once. The campaign made his name. The procurement fight will decide whether its lessons hold.

articles.title: Fotos hechas con IA antes de una cirugía estética: el peligro legal y sanitario de prometer resultados falsos
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial (IA) ha transformado múltiples áreas de la medicina, desde el diagnóstico temprano de enfermedades hasta la optimización de procesos clínicos. No obstante, uno de los errores más graves que se puede cometer en el sector de la estética es usar fotos hechas con IA para prometer resultados antes de una cirugía.
Esta práctica, lejos de ser una herramienta informativa, plantea riesgos éticos, legales y sanitarios que distintas sociedades científicas han comenzado a señalar con preocupación.
El uso de simulaciones algorítmicas que aseguran un resultado futuro vulnera la confianza en el acto médico. Puede inducir a los pacientes a tomar decisiones basadas en expectativas irreales o falsas.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué no se debe usar IA para prometer resultados antes de una cirugía estética
La International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS) y sociedades médicas nacionales recuerdan que la cirugía plástica constituye una “obligación de medios, no de resultados”. Esto significa que el cirujano se compromete a usar todos los recursos y conocimientos disponibles, pero nunca puede garantizar un resultado específico.
“Es muy difícil prometer un resultado a través de una imagen generada con IA”, advierte Caio Silva, Gerente de Mercadeo para Latam en Galderma. Mostrar imágenes generadas por IA como un resultado posible vulnera la ética médica porque comercializa una promesa que ningún profesional está en condiciones de asegurar.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, la situación es aún más delicada cuando se observa que numerosas revistas y sociedades científicas han prohibido expresamente el uso de IA generativa para alterar o crear imágenes quirúrgicas. Esta medida busca frenar la desinformación y proteger tanto a los pacientes como a la profesión.
Qué consecuencias legales hay por mostrar fotos con IA en la práctica médica
El consentimiento informado es uno de los pilares del acto médico. Para las autoridades de salud, si un paciente decide operarse guiado por una simulación irreal generada por inteligencia artificial, dicho consentimiento queda viciado.
PUBLICIDAD
Legalmente, el paciente no aceptó los riesgos del procedimiento real, sino las expectativas de una imagen algorítmica falsa. “Hay un riesgo por legalidad para los médicos. La gran mayoría de los consejos no permite que los doctores prometan resultados para sus pacientes”, señala Silva.
En este contexto, cualquier reclamación por insatisfacción podría derivar en conflictos legales, porque el paciente podría argumentar que la decisión fue influida por expectativas irreales.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son los riesgos sanitarios de prometer cambios estéticos con fotos con IA
El uso de imágenes alteradas puede conducir a procedimientos inadecuados o no indicados. Las diferencias individuales, como la calidad de la piel, la respuesta biológica y otros factores, hacen imposible predecir con exactitud el resultado de una cirugía.
El dermatólogo Boris Sánchez subraya que “estos son procedimientos médicos que requieren un conocimiento científico desde la anatomía hasta los dispositivos y herramientas inyectables”.
La falta de formación adecuada y la presión por cumplir expectativas irreales pueden generar complicaciones e incidentes en clínicas estéticas, lo que ha motivado a sociedades y autoridades a reforzar los controles y la transparencia.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué papel asumen las sociedades científicas y las instituciones ante el uso de IA
Las sociedades científicas han respondido con mayor rigor ante el auge de imágenes alteradas por inteligencia artificial en la promoción de cirugías estéticas. Según la normativa de la ISAPS y otras entidades, la prohibición es clara: no se permite el uso de IA para crear imágenes de supuestos resultados quirúrgicos.
La vigilancia institucional y el fortalecimiento de los protocolos éticos buscan evitar la desinformación y proteger la integridad de la práctica médica. “Lo más importante es que estos son procedimientos médicos. Tiene que realizarlo un especialista en medicina estética”, explica Sánchez.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, la responsabilidad profesional incluye informar con veracidad y evitar promesas que no tienen respaldo científico, especialmente cuando la tecnología puede inducir a error.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Aligning Managed IT And Consulting For Business Productivity - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Importance of Managed IT and Consulting Integration
In today’s fast-paced business environment, companies face escalating pressure to enhance operational efficiency while managing increasingly complex IT infrastructures. Many organizations turn to managed IT services and consulting firms to navigate these challenges. However, the greatest productivity gains come when these two functions are not siloed but aligned strategically.
Managed IT services provide the backbone of technology management-handling day-to-day operations, maintenance, and security. Consulting, on the other hand, focuses on high-level strategy, innovation, and transformation initiatives. When these disciplines collaborate effectively, businesses can optimize resources, accelerate digital transformation, and improve overall productivity.
For example, engaging with a trusted provider like PCS, Memphis’s top MSP can ensure your IT environment is robust and responsive. Such partnerships offer not only technical expertise but also strategic insight to align IT capabilities with business goals. This alignment helps companies avoid costly missteps and better leverage technology as a driver of growth rather than just a support function.
Why Integration Matters More Than Ever
Recent studies highlight the critical role of integrated IT management and consulting in driving business outcomes. According to a Deloitte survey, 70% of organizations that combine managed IT services with consulting report improved business agility and faster time-to-market for new products and services. This statistic underscores how integration not only enhances operational efficiency but also accelerates innovation cycles.
This integration allows businesses to identify inefficiencies and areas for innovation that might be overlooked when IT and consulting operate separately. For instance, consulting teams can leverage operational data from managed services to design targeted solutions that address specific pain points, such as network bottlenecks or cybersecurity vulnerabilities. This synergy creates a feedback loop where operational insights inform strategic planning, and strategic goals guide daily IT activities.
Moreover, a well-coordinated approach supports proactive risk management. Utilizing tools like a cloud assessment checklist helps organizations evaluate cloud security comprehensively, ensuring that migration strategies align with compliance requirements and business continuity plans. With cloud adoption projected to grow by 23% annually, according to Gartner, aligning consulting insights with managed IT execution is essential for sustainable growth. This alignment mitigates risks associated with rapid technology adoption and regulatory pressures.
Steps to Achieve Alignment Between Managed IT and Consulting
- Establish Clear Communication Channels
Effective collaboration begins with open communication. IT operations and consulting teams should have designated liaisons to share insights, challenges, and progress updates regularly. This transparency helps prevent duplicated efforts and ensures alignment with overarching business objectives. For example, scheduling joint weekly meetings or using integrated collaboration platforms can keep all stakeholders informed and engaged.
- Define Shared Goals and KPIs
Both teams must agree on measurable goals that directly impact productivity, such as system uptime, incident response times, and project delivery milestones. Tracking these KPIs enables continuous improvement and demonstrates the value of integration to stakeholders. According to a report by IDC, organizations that implement unified KPIs across IT and consulting functions see a 20% increase in project success rates and improved stakeholder satisfaction.
- Leverage Data for Informed Decision-Making
Managed IT services generate valuable operational data that consultants can analyze to identify trends and opportunities. For example, analyzing network performance metrics can inform infrastructure upgrades or cloud migration strategies. Access to real-time analytics fosters agile decision-making and rapid course corrections. Additionally, integrating AI-driven analytics tools can enhance predictive capabilities, allowing teams to anticipate issues before they impact business operations.
- Implement a Unified Technology Roadmap
A consolidated technology roadmap aligns IT initiatives with business strategy, avoiding fragmented efforts. This roadmap should accommodate input from both managed services and consulting teams, balancing immediate operational needs with long-term innovation. It acts as a living document that evolves with changing market conditions and technological advancements, ensuring that investments deliver maximum value.
- Foster a Collaborative Culture
Beyond processes and technology, fostering a culture of collaboration is critical. Encouraging cross-functional teams, joint problem-solving sessions, and shared accountability breaks down silos. Organizations that invest in cultural alignment report higher employee engagement and better project outcomes, as teams are more motivated to work toward common goals.
Realizing Productivity Gains Through Alignment
Businesses that successfully integrate managed IT and consulting functions report significant productivity improvements. For instance, companies experience up to a 30% reduction in downtime due to proactive IT management combined with strategic consulting initiatives. This reduction translates into substantial cost savings and improved customer satisfaction, as systems remain available and performant.
Additionally, aligned teams can reduce project delivery times by an average of 25%, accelerating time-to-value for new technology investments. Faster delivery means businesses can respond more quickly to market opportunities and competitive threats. Combined with improved agility, these gains position organizations for sustained growth.
Such productivity improvements also impact employee experience. By streamlining IT operations and aligning strategic objectives, employees face fewer disruptions and have better access to the tools they need. This boosts morale and retention, which are critical in today’s tight labor markets.
Overcoming Common Challenges in Integration
While the benefits are clear, aligning managed IT and consulting teams is not without challenges. Common obstacles include cultural differences, misaligned priorities, and siloed data systems. Addressing these issues requires strong leadership commitment and a focus on building a collaborative culture.
Investing in cross-training can help bridge knowledge gaps, enabling team members to appreciate each other’s roles and contributions. For example, IT staff can gain insights into strategic planning processes, while consultants learn the operational realities of IT systems. This mutual understanding fosters empathy and smoother collaboration.
Additionally, adopting integrated platforms that unify service management and consulting workflows enhances coordination and transparency. Technology solutions that support shared dashboards, real-time reporting, and automated alerts reduce friction and keep both teams aligned.
Leadership plays a pivotal role by setting expectations, providing necessary resources, and recognizing collaborative successes. Organizations that prioritize integration at the executive level see faster adoption and better outcomes.
Future Trends in Managed IT and Consulting Collaboration
Looking ahead, the convergence of managed IT and consulting is expected to deepen with advances in artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and cloud technologies. AI-driven analytics will provide deeper insights into IT operations, enabling consultants to design more precise and impactful strategies.
For example, AI can analyze vast datasets to detect anomalies, predict failures, and recommend optimization opportunities, which consultants can translate into actionable plans. Automation further streamlines routine IT tasks, freeing teams to focus on innovation and strategic initiatives.
Furthermore, as hybrid and multi-cloud environments become the norm, continuous assessment frameworks like this will be critical to maintaining security and compliance. Combining these frameworks with managed services ensures businesses can scale securely and efficiently. The complexity of managing diverse environments necessitates integrated approaches that encompass both operational execution and strategic oversight.
Moreover, emerging technologies such as edge computing and Internet of Things (IoT) devices will add layers of complexity and opportunity. Aligning managed IT and consulting will be essential to harness these technologies effectively while mitigating associated risks.
Conclusion
Aligning managed IT and consulting is a strategic imperative for businesses aiming to boost productivity and innovate effectively. By fostering collaboration, setting clear goals, and leveraging data-driven insights, organizations can transform their IT function from a cost center into a powerful enabler of business success.
Engaging with experienced providers such as offers a practical pathway to achieving this alignment. Together, managed IT and consulting teams can unlock new levels of operational excellence, agility, and growth potential in an increasingly digital world.
As businesses continue to evolve, the integration of managed IT and consulting will remain a key differentiator-driving not only efficiency but also the innovation necessary to thrive in a competitive landscape. Organizations that prioritize this alignment today will be best positioned to capitalize on tomorrow’s opportunities.

articles.title: Apple est débordé, l'IA fait exploser le nombre de failles découvertes par les chercheurs
articles.text:
Comme tous les géants de la technologie, Apple fait face à un problème inédit. Le géant de Cupertino croule actuellement sous les signalements relatifs à des failles de sécurité. En ce moment, les signalements de vulnérabilités arrivent bien plus vite que les équipes d’Apple ne peuvent les vérifier, les traiter et les corriger. C’est évidemment l’essor de l’IA générative qui est responsable de l’explosion des découvertes de bugs. Armés d’outils d’IA, les chercheurs débusquent des failles à tour de bras. Chaque rapport doit encore être validé manuellement par un chercheur humain, même si Apple utilise désormais elle-même l’IA pour aider à trier les signalements.
À lire aussi : 16 millions d’ordinateurs touchés – Claude lève le voile sur une faille Linux vieille de 9 ans
Apple serre la vis sur les rapports de failles
Face à cet afflux débordant, Apple a été contraint de prendre une série de mesures, rapporte le Financial Times. Tout d’abord, l’entreprise californienne a décidé de mettre en place un plafond de soumissions. Apple a commencé par limiter le nombre de rapports de sécurité que l’on peut déposer. Concrètement, une fois qu’un chercheur atteint le plafond défini, il ne peut plus soumettre de nouveaux signalements jusqu’à ce que ses rapports en cours soient examinés. La mesure doit éviter l’accumulation de signalements non traités.
En complément, Apple a aussi instauré une période d’attente obligatoire entre deux vagues de soumissions pour un même chercheur. Une fois le quota atteint, il ne peut tout simplement plus rien soumettre de nouveau pendant 30 jours, ce qui laisse un peu de répit aux équipes d’Apple.
« Face au volume croissant de rapports de sécurité générés par l’IA dans l’ensemble du secteur, nous avons récemment ajusté le nombre de nouveaux rapports qu’un chercheur peut avoir ouverts simultanément. Les chercheurs peuvent facilement demander à tout moment une augmentation de cette limite afin de garantir que les rapports critiques parviennent à nos équipes de sécurité », confirme Apple.
Plus de 50 failles potentielles dans macOS
La société italienne Bynario en offre un exemple frappant de l’explosion des signalements de failles à cause de l’IA. En trois semaines seulement, elle a identifié plus de 50 failles potentielles dans macOS grâce à ChatGPT. Parmi les failles débusquées, les chercheurs ont trouvé une défaillance qui aurait pu donner à un attaquant le contrôle total d’un Mac. L’entreprise s’est retrouvée temporairement incapable de déposer de nouveaux rapports à destination d’Apple.
« Le secteur traverse une période très difficile. Les prestataires de maintenance et les fournisseurs sont submergés par le nombre considérable de bugs découverts », explique Alfredo Pesoli, PDG et cofondateur de Bynario, au média.
Interrogé par le Financial Times, Apple pointe du doigt des rapports qui sont parfois de mauvaise qualité. En miroir de Linus Torvalds, le créateur de Linux, Apple estime que trop de signalements décrivent des risques purement théoriques, voire totalement inventés par les modèles d’IA. Il est parfois difficile de dénicher, parmi l’océan de signalements exagérés, des vulnérabilités bien réelles nécessitant un correctif urgent. En interne, Apple aurait même baptisé ce flot de rapports de piètre qualité de l’« AI slop », c’est-à-dire du contenu produit par IA sans réelle valeur.
À lire aussi : Avec iOS 26.6, Apple corrige près de 90 failles de sécurité, mettez à jour votre iPhone !
Le double impact de l’IA sur la traque de failles
Ruff Pilling, directeur du renseignement chez Sophos, abonde dans le même sens qu’Apple et estime que l’IA a deux effets majeurs sur la découverte de failles. L’IA facilite les signalements spéculatifs de la part de chercheurs amateurs, mais elle aide aussi les experts chevronnés à repérer des failles sérieuses plus rapidement qu’auparavant. Le bilan est à la fois positif et négatif. Pour inciter les chercheurs sérieux à continuer leur travail malgré les nouvelles restrictions, Apple a revu à la hausse son programme de primes. La récompense maximale pour les failles les plus critiques dépasse désormais les 5 millions de dollars.

articles.title: AirPods avec caméra : le projet secret d’Apple pourrait finalement débarquer dès la rentrée
articles.text:
AirPods avec caméra : le projet secret d’Apple pourrait finalement débarquer dès la rentrée
Alors que les AirPods équipés de caméras semblaient encore réservés à 2027, de nouvelles informations suggèrent qu'un premier modèle pourrait être dévoilé dès cet automne. Une évolution qui miserait moins sur la photo que sur la nouvelle génération de Siri dopée à l'intelligence artificielle.
Les rumeurs autour des AirPods équipés de caméras reviennent sur le devant de la scène. Alors que plusieurs informations laissaient penser que ce projet avait été repoussé à 2027, les dernières révélations de Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, relancent l'hypothèse d’une commercialisation quasi imminente. Apple pourrait finalement présenter une première version de ces écouteurs dès cet automne.
Apple AirPods Pro 3
Deux paires d'AirPods dans les tuyaux, dont une imminente
La confusion viendrait du fait qu'Apple développerait deux modèles distincts en parallèle. Le premier, connu sous le nom de code B798, reste bien attendu pour 2027. Il s'agirait de la version la plus aboutie du concept, après plusieurs reports du calendrier.
Un second modèle baptisé B790, semble quant à lui suivre une feuille de route différente. D'après Gurman, ce prototype est plus avancé que prévu et des références à ce produit ont déjà été découvertes dans le code d'iOS 27. Le développeur Sam Henri Gold avait d'ailleurs repéré ces mentions dans la deuxième bêta du système le mois dernier.
Si le calendrier est respecté, ces AirPods pourraient être dévoilés lors de la conférence de présentation de l'iPhone 18, attendue en septembre. Rien n'est encore officiel, mais la présence de ce modèle dans iOS 27 laisse penser que son développement est déjà bien avancé.
Des caméras avant tout conçues pour assister Siri
Contrairement à ce que l'on pourrait imaginer, ces caméras ne serviraient pas à prendre des photos ou à enregistrer des vidéos. Leur objectif serait plutôt d'alimenter les fonctions d'intelligence artificielle d'Apple en fournissant des informations visuelles sur l'environnement de l'utilisateur. Siri, agrémenté par Google Gemini, pourrait ainsi mieux comprendre ce qui se passe autour de vous et répondre à des questions en s'appuyant sur ce que "voient" les écouteurs, dans une approche similaire à celle des assistants IA capables d'analyser une scène en temps réel.
Plusieurs précédentes rumeurs évoquaient également quelques évolutions matérielles. Les AirPods pourraient adopter des tiges légèrement plus longues afin d'intégrer les capteurs, ainsi qu'une LED destinée à signaler lorsque certaines données visuelles sont envoyées vers le cloud pour être traitées. Par ailleurs, espérons que cette fonctionnalité n’impactera pas l’autonomie des écouteurs, notamment grâce à la possibilité de la désactiver ou à l'intégration d'un système de veille profond lorsqu’elle n’est pas utilisée.
Il reste toutefois plusieurs inconnues. Apple n'a toujours pas confirmé l'existence de ces écouteurs, les différences exactes entre les modèles B790 et B798 ne sont pas connues, et rien ne garantit que les deux versions seront commercialisées. Le prix est lui aussi un mystère, même si ces AirPods devraient logiquement se positionner au-dessus des AirPods Pro.

Estamos en la cuenta regresiva final hacia un nuevo evento Made by Google, donde se presentarán los Pixel 11. Pero ya no quedan sorpresas para los próximos móviles de la empresa californiana, pues una filtración acaba de exponer todo sobre estos, incluyendo su tabla de especificaciones y sus precios iniciales para Estados Unidos y Europa.
Los Pixel 11 protagonizaron varias filtraciones en lo que va de 2026, pero la más reciente expone todas sus características técnicas. El leak ratifica mucho de lo que ya se venía comentando respecto de los dispositivos. Vale remarcar que la propia Google ha entregado un primer vistazo oficial a sus dispositivos a través de una serie de teasers.
Tanto el Pixel 11 base como las variantes Pro no tendrán grandes modificaciones estéticas respecto de los modelos de 2025. La gran novedad de este año será la introducción de Pixel Glow, un indicador multicolor que se ubicará dentro del módulo de cámara y que supuestamente ocupará el lugar que en las últimas generaciones estuvo reservado para el sensor de temperatura en los modelos Pro. Todavía no hay detalles sobre su funcionamiento, pero los principales rumores apuntan a que servirá para las notificaciones.
Más allá de eso, los Pixel 11 traerán las actualizaciones lógicas de una nueva generación (un chip renovado, por ejemplo) y es lógico pensar que traerán noticias mayormente enfocadas en Android 17 y las funciones de IA impulsadas por Gemini. La filtración también ratifica la eliminación de la opción de 128 GB de almacenamiento en toda la gama, lo que trae consigo el encarecimiento implícito de los modelos de entrada.
