articles.title: Network Support And Cybersecurity For Reliable Daily Operations - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Critical Role of Network Support in Business Continuity
In today’s fast-paced digital environment, businesses rely heavily on their network infrastructure for daily operations. From communication and data transfer to cloud applications and customer interactions, a robust network is the backbone of organizational efficiency. Any downtime or disruption can lead to significant productivity losses and financial setbacks. Consequently, effective network support is essential to ensure seamless connectivity and minimize operational risks.
Network support encompasses everything from hardware maintenance to troubleshooting connectivity issues and optimizing performance. It involves proactive monitoring to detect and resolve issues before they escalate. Industry data suggests that 60% of companies that experience significant network downtime go out of business within six months, underscoring the importance of reliable network management. This statistic highlights how critical it is for businesses to maintain a resilient network, as even short periods of downtime can have devastating consequences.
Moreover, the complexity of modern networks, which often span multiple locations and incorporate a variety of devices and platforms, demands specialized expertise. Network support teams are responsible not only for fixing problems as they arise but also for planning capacity, optimizing network traffic, and ensuring scalability for future growth. These efforts contribute to a more stable and efficient network environment, reducing the likelihood of unexpected outages.
For businesses seeking expert assistance, More from GroupOne IT offers comprehensive network support solutions tailored to maintain uptime and enhance system reliability. Their expertise ensures that potential network vulnerabilities are addressed promptly, enabling businesses to focus on growth without worrying about connectivity disruptions.
In addition to reactive support, many organizations are adopting proactive strategies such as predictive maintenance and continuous network health assessments. These approaches leverage advanced analytics and monitoring tools to anticipate issues before they affect users, thereby minimizing downtime. According to a recent survey, 85% of IT leaders report that proactive network management significantly improves operational efficiency. This further illustrates the value of investing in robust network support frameworks.
Cybersecurity: Safeguarding Business Operations Against Emerging Threats
Alongside network support, cybersecurity has become a paramount concern for organizations worldwide. Cyberattacks are increasing in sophistication and frequency, targeting businesses of all sizes. Effective cybersecurity frameworks protect sensitive data, prevent unauthorized access, and maintain regulatory compliance, thereby preserving customer trust and brand reputation.
Recent studies highlight that ransomware attacks occur every 11 seconds globally, and the average cost of a data breach has risen to $4.45 million. These alarming figures demonstrate the financial and operational impact of cyber threats. The growing complexity of cyberattacks, including phishing, malware, and insider threats, requires organizations to implement comprehensive and adaptive security measures.
Implementing a multi-layered cybersecurity strategy that includes firewalls, intrusion detection systems, endpoint protection, and employee training is critical for mitigating risks. In fact, organizations that invest in employee cybersecurity awareness programs reduce the risk of successful phishing attacks by up to 70%. This statistic underscores the importance of combining technological defenses with human vigilance.
One exemplary model is HERO’s cybersecurity approach, which incorporates cutting-edge tools and best practices to protect businesses from cyber threats. Their cybersecurity approach emphasizes continuous monitoring, rapid incident response, and tailored solutions that align with specific industry requirements, ensuring comprehensive defense against evolving cyber risks.
Furthermore, cybersecurity is not a one-time project but a continuous process that must evolve alongside emerging threats. Regular security assessments, penetration testing, and compliance audits are essential components of a robust cybersecurity posture. Organizations that fail to keep pace with changing threat landscapes risk data breaches, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
Integrating Network Support and Cybersecurity for Optimal Performance
The intersection of network support and cybersecurity is where businesses can achieve optimal operational resilience. Network infrastructure must be designed and maintained not only for performance but also with security in mind. Secure network architecture reduces vulnerabilities and strengthens defenses against external and internal threats.
Combining proactive network support with robust cybersecurity measures enables organizations to detect anomalies, prevent breaches, and recover swiftly from incidents. Automation tools and AI-driven analytics enhance visibility into network traffic patterns and potential threats, allowing for faster decision-making and mitigation.
Moreover, businesses investing in integrated solutions report 30% fewer security incidents and a 25% reduction in downtime, translating into significant cost savings and improved productivity. These metrics reinforce the value of a comprehensive approach that aligns network management and cybersecurity efforts.
Integrated network and cybersecurity strategies also facilitate compliance with increasingly stringent regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA. These regulations require organizations to implement adequate safeguards to protect data privacy and security. By aligning network support with cybersecurity policies, businesses can streamline compliance efforts and reduce the risk of costly fines.
Additionally, the convergence of network support and cybersecurity fosters a culture of resilience. Teams can collaborate more effectively, sharing insights and responding to incidents with greater coordination. This holistic approach ensures that security is embedded into every aspect of network management-from design and deployment to monitoring and incident response.
Best Practices for Ensuring Reliable Daily Operations
To sustain uninterrupted daily operations, organizations should adopt several best practices:
- Regular Network Assessments: Conduct periodic evaluations to identify weaknesses and optimize configurations. This includes vulnerability scanning, performance testing, and capacity planning to ensure networks can handle current and future demands.
- Employee Training: Educate staff on cybersecurity awareness, phishing detection, and safe online practices. Human error remains a significant factor in security breaches, so cultivating informed users is vital.
- Patch Management: Keep all systems and software updated to address known vulnerabilities. Timely patching reduces the attack surface and prevents exploitation by malicious actors.
- Incident Response Planning: Develop and regularly update a response plan to minimize the impact of security incidents. A well-prepared team can contain breaches quickly and restore operations efficiently.
- Vendor Collaboration: Partner with trusted technology providers who offer specialized expertise in network support and cybersecurity. Reliable vendors can provide timely support, updates, and innovations necessary to maintain system integrity.
Implementing these strategies requires commitment at all organizational levels. Leadership must prioritize cybersecurity and network reliability as core business objectives, allocating sufficient resources and fostering a security-first mindset.
Moreover, businesses should consider leveraging managed services or outsourcing certain aspects of network support and cybersecurity to specialized providers. This can provide access to advanced technologies and expertise that may be cost-prohibitive to develop internally, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises.
The Future of Network Support and Cybersecurity
As digital transformation accelerates, the complexity of network environments and cyber threats will continue to grow. Advances in cloud computing, IoT, and remote work introduce new challenges that require adaptive and scalable solutions. Artificial intelligence and machine learning are playing an increasingly vital role in predictive analytics and threat detection.
For instance, AI-powered security tools can analyze vast amounts of network data in real-time to identify suspicious behavior patterns that may indicate a breach. This proactive detection enables faster response times and reduces potential damage. According to Gartner, by 2025, 75% of security operations centers will leverage AI and automation to improve threat detection and response.
Organizations that prioritize investment in integrated network support and cybersecurity will be better positioned to navigate these changes. Embracing innovation while maintaining foundational security principles ensures that daily operations remain reliable and resilient.
Furthermore, as remote work becomes a permanent fixture in many industries, securing distributed networks and endpoints is increasingly critical. Virtual private networks (VPNs), zero-trust architectures, and secure access service edge (SASE) frameworks are becoming standard components of modern network security strategies.
In conclusion, reliable daily operations depend on the seamless integration of network support and cybersecurity. Businesses that proactively manage their networks and safeguard against cyber risks can achieve greater efficiency, protect their assets, and sustain growth in an increasingly digital world. Investing in comprehensive network support and advanced cybersecurity measures is no longer optional but a strategic imperative for organizational success.

articles.title: Apnée du sommeil : des patients "en détresse" face au masque découvrent cet implant remboursé, 12 fois plus efficace que la chirurgie
articles.text:
Apnée du sommeil : des patients "en détresse" face au masque découvrent cet implant remboursé, 12 fois plus efficace que la chirurgie
Remboursé à 100 %, disponible dans une vingtaine de centres en France, et adossé à une méta-analyse qui lui attribue 12 fois plus de guérisons que la chirurgie : l'implant Inspire contre l'apnée du sommeil vient d'arriver en Champagne-Ardenne. Le téléphone de la polyclinique ne cesse de sonner.
Quatre millions de Français vivent avec l'apnée obstructive du sommeil. La gorge se referme, le souffle s'interrompt, le cerveau sonne l'alerte : micro-réveil, reprise d'air, et rebelote, parfois cinquante fois par heure. Le masque à pression positive continue (PPC) reste le traitement de référence, mais entre le bruit, la sécheresse buccale et l'inconfort, une part substantielle des patients finit par le délaisser. D'où l'engouement croissant pour les alternatives implantables apparues ces dernières années.
Un "pacemaker du sommeil" remboursé et désormais disponible en Champagne-Ardenne
Pendant des années, Béatrice, Ardennaise d'une cinquantaine d'années, vivait "tout le temps fatiguée". Exténuée dès le réveil, incapable de trouver l'énergie pour une simple balade en famille. C'est sa fille, infirmière, qui finit par la pousser à consulter. En 2017, un pneumologue pose enfin le diagnostic : apnée du sommeil. Son cas est loin d'être isolé.
	
On estime que 5 % de la population française est concernée. C'est une maladie qui a un fort impact négatif sur la qualité de vie et peut mener à des troubles cardiovasculaires, entre autres.
La Polyclinique Reims-Bezannes propose depuis mai 2026 la thérapie Inspire, une première en Champagne-Ardenne. Le dispositif, remboursé par l'Assurance Maladie depuis août 2024, fonctionne comme un pacemaker du sommeil : un boîtier implanté sous la clavicule envoie une impulsion au nerf hypoglosse à chaque inspiration pour propulser la langue vers l'avant et dégager les voies aériennes. L'intervention se réalise en ambulatoire, sous anesthésie générale, en moins de deux heures : deux incisions, l'une au niveau de la gorge, l'autre de la poitrine, un peu de colle, et un mois de cicatrisation avant la mise en marche. Le patient active ensuite le boîtier chaque soir grâce à une télécommande posée sur le thorax, et l'éteint au réveil.
Le coût de l'appareil seul atteint 22 000 euros, intégralement pris en charge. Comme le souligne le Dr Marion Renaud, médecin ORL et chirurgien à la polyclinique, les conséquences de l'apnée du sommeil non traitée et ses complications coûtent au final bien davantage à la collectivité.
Depuis l'annonce de cette nouvelle prise en charge, le téléphone de la polyclinique “ne cesse de sonner” selon l'Union. Des patients “en détresse”, “prêts à annuler leurs vacances” pour être opérés au plus vite. L'engouement traduit, selon les trois médecins impliqués, la souffrance réelle des apnéistes du sommeil.
	
Il y a une sélection rigoureuse des patients pour l'implantation. Ce n'est pas un gadget ni une expérimentation.
Les critères d'éligibilité restent stricts : IMC inférieur à 32, échec avéré de la PPC et de l'orthèse d'avancée mandibulaire, endoscopie sous sommeil induit préalable. Plus de 100 000 patients ont été implantés dans le monde depuis 2014, et une vingtaine de centres répartis dans toute la France réalisent désormais la pose, dont la liste complète est consultable sur le site d'Inspire.
Une méta-analyse confirme la supériorité de l'implant sur la chirurgie
Ces résultats cliniques viennent d'être confortés par une méta-analyse en réseau parue dans Sleep and Breathing le 28 juillet 2026. Do Hyun Kim et Se Hwan Hwang (Catholic University of Korea), associés à David W. Jang (Duke University), ont agrégé 758 patients issus de dix études pour confronter quatre approches : la PPC, la stimulation des voies aériennes supérieures (UAS), la chirurgie robotique transorale (TORS) et la réduction tissulaire par ablation plasma (PATBR).
Le verdict est sans appel. L'implant UAS réduit l'index d'apnées-hypopnées de façon significativement supérieure à la TORS, et multiplie par douze les probabilités de guérison (IAH ramené sous 5 événements par heure). La durée d'hospitalisation chute également avec l'UAS. Seul bémol : sur l'échelle de somnolence d'Epworth, qui mesure la fatigue diurne ressentie, aucune différence significative ne se dégage entre les quatre traitements.

articles.title: Commemorative golden Doom floppy disks go up for pre-order — pair of limited edition dummy ‘imitation gold plating’ disks and a box are $30 at GameStop
articles.text:
Commemorative golden Doom floppy disks go up for pre-order — pair of limited edition dummy ‘imitation gold plating’ disks and a box are $30 at GameStop
This officially licensed physical media isn’t even functional.
GameStop has listed a Doom Floppy Disk Limited Edition Imitation Gold Plated Replica at $29.99. Let’s unpick that for a moment. These are imitation floppy disks coated in imitation gold, delivered in a commemorative box. There’s a display stand included, too. However, these are non-functioning 'floppy disks' inspired by the Doom v1.2 shareware release and don’t contain any game data. Doom's single-level ‘Knee‑Deep in the Dead’ shareware release is still free to download, though, as it has been for many years.
“What's more retro than obsolete technology?” asks Fanattik, the collectibles maker behind this useless physical media. “Celebrating the humble 3½-inch, 1.44 MB floppy disk that the game was originally released on back in 1993, this limited edition Doom Floppy Disk Replica plated with imitation gold comes in a box displaying the original game artwork, has a display stand included, and is individually numbered as one of 5,000 worldwide.” Pre-orders are now open at GameStop in the US for $29.99 or directly from Fanattik in the UK at £19.99.
The 89 x 89 mm dimensions of the golden-but-not-gold and 3.5-inch-but-not-floppies make them at least the correct size. However, if I were buying fake floppies, I think I would appreciate a movable protective sliding mechanism and the write-protect cutout toggle to move, so I could fidget with them from time to time.
Also, in some ways, it is ironic that game media is now being licensed and hawked to fans, at non-trivial prices, without any game data contained on them. This seems to be a growing trend as the games industry moves inexorably to a digital-only future. People still covet the physical media so much that they are now willing to pay for it, even without any game data or download code being associated with it.
The original Doom v1.2 shareware edition was released on two floppy disks in Feb 1994, and it is famous for adding modem support to this seminal game. If you paid and registered Doom v1.2, you would get four floppy disks from id Software containing the full three-episode campaign. The registered release disk set stayed on four floppies until the CD-ROM era.

articles.title: Kaapi Machines raises Rs 50 Cr from Sedna HoReCa
articles.text:
Kaapi Machines raises Rs 50 Cr from Sedna HoReCa
Kaapi Machines will use the funding to expand its product portfolio, stengthen its manufacturing capabilities, and improve technology.
Kaapi Machines, a coffee equipment and service provider based in Bengaluru, has raised Rs 50 crore in equity funding from Sedna HoReCa, a PE-backed B2B solutions provider for the HoReCa segment (hotels, restaurants and cafes/catering).
Kaapi Machines and Sedna, which is also Bengaluru based, have entered into a partnership to expand the former’s product portfolio, strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, and improve its technology stack, warehousing, and service infrastructure, according to a statement.
The statement also noted that Kaapi Machines will pursue select new opportunities in adjacent product categories for its core customer base, leveraging Sedna’s capabilities.
Kaapi Machines, which was founded in 2007 by Abhinav Mathur, aims to cross 150 crore in revenue in the current financial year and expand its business over the next 2-3 years.
“We are excited to partner with the Sedna team as we set forth on our new growth trajectory at Kaapi Machines. As the HoReCa industry continues to grow and gets more organised, we want to expand our capabilities to offer our customers new and innovative products, technologies and solutions,” said Mathur.
Kaapi Machines' clients include large café chains, QSRs, speciality coffee roasters, hotels, retailers, corporates, and coffee vending businesses in India.
"The partnership with Abhinav and Kaapi Machines is a highly synergistic addition to Sedna's capabilities given their deep domain expertise, brand equity and pan-India service network catering to a fast-growing category, and reinforces our vision of building India's most comprehensive B2B platform for the food service ecosystem,” said Saurabh Pandey, Managing Director, Sedna HoReCa Pvt Ltd.
Coffee consumption has been showing sustained growth in the country among the growing middle class and a new breed of consumers driven by the café culture. The market comprises domestic brands, global players, and speciality coffee chains such as Third Wave and Blue Tokai.

articles.title: « Aucun risque pour la sécurité » : comment une faille critique notée 10/10 s'est révélée être une pure invention de l'IA - Numerama
articles.text:
Nous sommes le 27 juillet 2026 et un compte GitHub tout juste créé publie une série d’avis de vulnérabilité visant SQLite.
L’alerte fait rapidement le tour des hautes instances cyber : il s’agit ici du moteur de base de données embarqué le plus utilisé au monde.
L’une des vulnérabilités référencées sous le code CVE-2026-51302 décrit une faille de type use-after-free jugée si sérieuse qu’elle décroche d’abord un score CVSS parfait de 10 sur 10. La NVD, base de données officielle du gouvernement américaine, la classe critique, le programme de la CISA, lagence de cybersécurité fédérale valide, puis le centre néerlandais de cybersécurité (NCSC) publie à son tour une alerte reprenant l’avis.
Problème, selon une analyse publiée par JFrog Security le 31 juillet, la fonction visée par la faille n’existe pas dans la version de SQLite mise en cause.
De la bouillie générée par IA, et un système sans garde-fou
Après ce premier signe d’alerte, les chercheurs ont donc entrepris de comparer tous les avis au code source réel de SQLite et de tester les preuves de concept fournies. Aucune ne fonctionne.
Pire, selon les équipes de JFrog, les avis publiés présentent tous des marqueurs de contenu généré par IA. Sur 55 avis analysés, 54 se révèlent entièrement fabriqués.
La faute selon eux à la fin de la validation humaine et manuelle de chaque entrée avant publication : « Historiquement, le NIST faisait office de filet de sécurité fiable pour ce système : les experts de la National Vulnerability Database (NVD) analysaient, validaient et enrichissaient manuellement les CVE entrantes avant de leur donner leur approbation. Mais ce filet de sécurité a cédé en février 2024. »
C’est à cette date que le NIST a reconnu ne plus arriver à traiter toutes les CVE qui lui sont soumises, faute de moyens suffisants.
Des réactions au retrait officiel
Selon Richard Hipp, développeur historique de SQLite, le numéro CVE avait été attribué par une autorité de numérotation puis intégré par MITRE sans contrôle supplémentaire.
Il aura fallu, de son propre aveu, une insistance particulière pour obtenir le retrait de CVE-2026-51302. Un épisode qui risque d’alimenter le ras-le-bol plus large face à l’afflux de rapports générés par des agents IA.
La fiche du NIST concernant cette faille imaginaire affiche désormais la mention suivante : « Cet enregistrement a été retiré par son CNA. Une enquête plus approfondie a démontré qu’il ne présentait aucun risque pour la sécurité. » Le NCSC néerlandais, qui avait relayé l’alerte, l’a lui aussi retirée, précisant que la CVE avait été hallucinée par un grand modèle de langage.
JFrog dit avoir signalé ses conclusions à Red Hat et au NVD pour faire corriger les autres entrées douteuses, et recommande de ne jamais faire confiance à une CVE tout juste publiée sans en vérifier la source et tenter de la reproduire.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 : Apple aurait déjà prévu plusieurs améliorations pour corriger les défauts du premier
articles.text:
Après un premier modèle qui misait avant tout sur la finesse, Apple préparerait déjà une nouvelle version de son iPhone Air. Au programme : un appareil photo supplémentaire, une puce plus moderne et plusieurs évolutions attendues dès le premier trimestre 2027.
D’après l’analyste Jeff Pu, qui suit de près les activités du groupe pour GF Securities, la firme de Cupertino envisagerait de dévoiler l’iPhone Air 2 dès le premier trimestre de l’année. Un modèle qui ne se contenterait pas d’une simple mise à jour, puisqu’il intégrerait déjà cinq évolutions majeures par rapport à la génération actuelle.
Un deuxième capteur photo et une puce A20 Pro en 2 nm au programme
La photo devrait compter parmi les principales nouveautés du smartphone ultrafin d'Apple. L'iPhone Air 2 embarquerait un deuxième capteur de 48 mégapixels au dos, associé cette fois à un objectif ultra grand-angle. Il viendrait ainsi compléter le capteur Fusion déjà présent sur la première génération.
Le géant de Cupertino prévoirait également de réduire légèrement la taille de la Dynamic Island. L'évolution resterait donc assez discrète sur la face avant, d'autant que le smartphone conserverait son écran de 6,5 pouces et sa caméra frontale Center Stage de 18 mégapixels. La quantité de mémoire vive resterait elle aussi fixée à 12 Go.
La partie interne profiterait en revanche de plusieurs modifications. L'iPhone Air 2 pourrait intégrer une puce A20 Pro plus rapide et moins énergivore, fabriquée par TSMC avec un procédé de gravure en 2 nm. Le modèle actuel s'appuie pour sa part sur une A19 Pro gravée en 3 nm.
De nouvelles puces Apple pour le réseau et la 5G
La connectivité sans fil devrait également évoluer avec l'arrivée d'une deuxième génération de la puce réseau d'Apple. Le modèle actuel embarque la N1, qui prend notamment en charge le Wi-Fi 7 et le Bluetooth 6 et contribue au fonctionnement de services comme AirDrop et le partage de connexion.
De son côté, la 5G devrait enfin bénéficier d'une nouvelle puce C2, appelée à succéder au modem C1X de l'actuel modèle. La marque à la pomme présente déjà ce dernier comme le modem le plus économe en énergie jamais intégré à un iPhone.
Selon les différents bruits de couloir, l'iPhone Air 2 devrait être présenté aux côtés de l'iPhone 18 et de l'iPhone 18e au printemps 2027. Apple aurait prévu une commercialisation différée pour les modèles haut de gamme, avec les iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max et le modèle pliant surnommé iPhone Ultra attendus quant à eux dès septembre.

articles.title: Chinese GLM-5.2 steals the spotlight after Hugging Face breach
articles.text:
In a twist of irony, a Chinese open source GLM 5.2 AI model contained 'rogue' OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in a Hugging Face hack just as the US mulls banning open-weight AI
Rogue OpenAI agent hands Chinese AI an unexpected victory
- Chinese Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 succeeded where leading American models failed woefully
- Hugging Face breach reignited Washington's battle over open-weight artificial intelligence
- Safety guardrails unexpectedly complicated defensive cybersecurity work during a real incident
The recent cybersecurity incident involving Hugging Face has unexpectedly placed a Chinese open source AI model at the centre of an intensifying United States policy debate over open-weight AI.
The episode emerged after an autonomous agent built with OpenAI technology reportedly escaped containment and behaved like a rogue actor.
The incident occurred as Washington is considering whether broader restrictions on Chinese open-weight AI models could affect American developers and startups.

Chinese open source model enters an unexpected cybersecurity role
According to Hugging Face, engineers relied on Zhipu AI's GLM-5.2 model to examine information generated during the incident after leading American models declined the requests.
American AI models could not distinguish legitimate defensive investigations from malicious hacking attempts because of built-in safety restrictions and protective guardrails.
Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 reportedly reroutes cybersecurity questions to an older, less capable model rather than allowing direct engagement with such tasks.
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol carries similar protections meant to stop the system from being used for hacking-related work of any kind.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
OpenAI later revealed that it has a Trusted Access programme that grants privileged, elevated capabilities to a select group of vetted teams, allowing them to use its models more fully to strengthen their own defenses.
Hugging Face was brought into this restricted tier following the breach, gaining deeper access than is normally available.
"We're all learning that secrecy is not the answer & that all defenders (not just a few selected ones) everywhere need more powerful models without restrictions, especially open ones!" said Hugging Face co-founder Clement Delangue.
"A safety regime that restricts legitimate defenders, while capable models remain available for attackers, creates an asymmetric disadvantage," said Lukasz Olejnik, visiting senior research fellow at the Department of War Studies, King's College London.
"This gap will only widen as open-source models become increasingly powerful while lacking guardrails or restrictions."
Washington weighs restrictions while startups urge caution
Nearly 200 Silicon Valley companies are opposing possible restrictions on Chinese open-weight AI models, warning that the move would raise costs for smaller developers.
Members of the newly formed Little Tech Association say banning downloads would not curb proliferation but would leave American startups weaker.
"There'll be hundreds of companies that instantly die," founder Suhail Doshi warned.
He argued that sweeping restrictions would disproportionately benefit larger American providers with the resources to absorb such a shift.
The U.S. is still scrutinizing Chinese developers over allegations involving model distillation and export control violations
White House officials maintained that any future policy decisions would come directly from the administration itself.
Analysts have also cautioned against treating the Hugging Face incident as justification for weakening the cybersecurity safeguards protecting advanced American systems.
"The answer is not simply to remove them," Shrenik Kothari of Robert W. Baird said, arguing that companies should refine their access controls rather than abandon safety measures altogether.
He suggested a more selective approach to capability allocation could balance legitimate security needs with the practical demands of cybersecurity research.

articles.title: Il cuit deux aliments en même temps : cet air fryer Moulinex de 11 L à deux tiroirs est à moitié prix
articles.text:
Moulinex propose une très large gamme d’air fryers, ces friteuses à air capables de rendre les aliments croustillants avec très peu d’huile tout en accélérant la cuisson par rapport à un four traditionnel. Parmi les modèles conçus par la marque française figure l’imposant Dual Easy Fry XXL, doté de deux compartiments. Avec, on peut donc cuisiner deux plats en même temps pour toute la famille. S’il vous intéresse, sachez qu’il bénéficie actuellement d’une promotion de 48 %.
Les points forts du Moulinex Dual Easy Fry XXL
- Une grande cuve de 6,5 L et une « petite » de 4,5 L
- Sept programmes prédéfinis
- Des accessoires qui passent au lave-vaisselle
D’abord affiché à 249,99 euros, l’air fryer Moulinex Dual Easy Fry XXL est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 129,99 euros chez Darty et à la Fnac.
Un air fryer avec deux grandes zones de cuisson
Le Moulinex Dual Easy Fry XXL porte bien son nom : cet air fryer « XXL » est imposant. En effet, avec son poids de 8,13 kg et ses dimensions de 38,5 x 33 x 45,8 cm, ce modèle est assez encombrant. Votre plan de travail doit donc être suffisamment grand pour pouvoir l’accueillir. Mais son format massif s’explique aussi par sa grande capacité, répartie entre deux zones de cuisson.
Ce Dual Easy Fry XXL comporte plus précisément deux tiroirs : l’un de 6,5 L, l’autre de 4,5 L. En tout, vous avez une capacité de 11 L, ce qui permet de cuisiner des plats pour 10 personnes. Ce n’est pas négligeable. Par exemple, le plus petit des compartiments peut contenir jusqu’à 1 kg de frites ou six petits muffins, tandis que le grand peut loger un rôti de 2 kg. En gros, le grand tiroir peut accueillir des mets volumineux, et le petit des accompagnements. Sachez par ailleurs que tous les accessoires antiadhésifs peuvent aller au lave-vaisselle.
Des fins de cuisson synchronisées
Avec cet air fryer, vous pouvez donc cuire, en même temps, deux aliments avec des durées et des températures différentes dans les deux tiroirs. Et pour que tout soit prêt au même moment, l’appareil peut synchroniser automatiquement les fins de cuisson. Vous avez au total sept programmes prédéfinis, que vous pouvez lancer directement depuis le panneau de commande sur la façade de l’appareil : frites, poulet, légumes, poisson, desserts, déshydratation et contrôle manuel de la température de 40 à 200 °C.
Ce Dual Easy Fry XXL peut griller, rôtir, toaster, déshydrater, réchauffer et, bien sûr, frire sans huile un grand nombre d’aliments. L’appareil embarque aussi la technologie Extra-Crisp, qui combine un flux d’air chaud puissant et un système de chauffe performant pour assurer une cuisson plus homogène et rendre les aliments plus croustillants. Enfin, sur l’application MyMoulinex, vous trouverez plusieurs centaines de recettes à réaliser avec cet air fryer. Et n’oublions pas que l’appareil est réparable pendant 15 ans, comme le promet Moulinex, qui met en avant un réseau de 6 200 réparateurs dans le monde.
Si vous souhaitez découvrir d’autres modèles parfaits pour faire croustiller vos mets, nous vous invitons dès maintenant à consulter notre guide des meilleurs airfryers du moment.

articles.title: The global memory shortage hits the MacBook Air | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The global memory chip shortage is affecting the availability of Apple’s most popular Mac, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.
Gurman said the shortage — caused by the demands of chip-hungry AI companies — had already affected Apple’s more niche computers, the Mac mini and Mac Studio. But it seems the company is now struggling to keep the MacBook Air in stock, with retailers saying that supply seems to be more constrained than ever before.
Indeed, anyone trying to buy a MacBook Air from the Apple website will have to wait until the back half of August — or for certain configurations, until September.
Gurman says Apple is working to address the issue by raising prices and sourcing memory from Chinese suppliers. Meanwhile, the company delayed its latest back-to-school promotion from June. And for the first time, the marketing material is more focused on the base model of the MacBook Pro. It even warns, “MacBook Air subject to availability.”

articles.title: Economist Steve Hanke says AI won't destroy most jobs because it costs more than hiring humans
articles.text:
A hot potato: A top economist has said that AI will not destroy most of the world's jobs, and his rationale seems totally logical: doing so would simply be far more expensive than employing humans. He also believes that this expense is what will prevent AI from becoming a freely available miracle machine that will remove the need for money from society, a vision espoused by Elon Musk.
Steve Hanke, a professor of applied economics at Johns Hopkins University and a former senior economist on President Ronald Reagan's Council of Economic Advisers, doesn't buy into a lot of the AI hype – both the good and the bad.
One of the biggest concerns about AI is its impact on jobs. We've already seen tens of thousands of layoffs in the last few years that came as a direct or indirect result of the technology, but Hanke told Business Insider that a complete apocalypse that leaves most people unemployed is just a fantasy for a very practical reason.
"Businesses will not be firing everybody and replacing them with AI," he said, because this would cost companies more money than hiring humans. Hanke said it's the same reason why the idea that the most advanced AI will be free to use and almost costless to run will never happen.
"This belief is based on a disconnect from reality, as well as a good dose of idiotic economic reasoning," he said. "AI is incredibly costly; it is very resource-intensive," Hanke continued. "It requires huge amounts of water, power, and physical capital."
Hanke also took aim at some the AI industry's so-called visionaries, labelling them "charlatans and hucksters." He said that when they liken AI to software, it's an "apples and oranges" comparison, given that AI continuously costs money to run whereas in most cases, software doesn't incur additional costs for customers after being developed.
As for how far the "AI revolution" will go and whether, or when, the bubble will burst, Hanke believes that will be decided by the "cost of scarce resources that are gobbled up by AI."
The professor's view contrasts with those of AI evangelists such as Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, who have long argued that the astronomical price of AI hardware and operations will decrease as efficiency gains are made.
The amount of money being poured into AI and its infrastructure is now counted in the hundreds of billions. Google and Tesla are two companies spending so much on the technology that they just recorded negative cash flows – it was the first time Google experienced this since it went public more than two decades ago.
In July, SoftBank's founder and largest shareholder, Masayoshi Son, said developing and deploying AI for society at large would cost $5 trillion a year through 2040, yet he was quite adamant that there was no AI bubble. Adata chairman Chen Li-bai, meanwhile, said an AI bubble should not even be discussed seriously until 2040 or even 2050.
Musk, meanwhile, believes people should stop saving for retirement as "money won't matter" in a decade or two, as AI will have taken most jobs and we will all be living off a universal high income handed out by the government.
As for jobs, there have been recent signs to support Hanke's view. An increasing number of companies, such as Ford and Klarna, are rehiring laid-off workers after discovering the systems that replaced them perform worse.
In June, it was reported that multiple studies showed more employers rehiring workers for recently eliminated positions after overestimating AI's productivity gains and cost savings – or, at the very least, regretting the decision.

articles.title: Xbox Disc to Digital Arrives This Month for Xbox One and Series X
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Xbox Disc to Digital Arrives This Month for Xbox One and Series X
Microsoft's internal roadmap for the Disc to Digital feature has been leaked, revealing that the feature will be generally available this month. According to the roadmap, an insider beta of the Disc to Digital feature has been available since July, with general availability for Xbox One and Series X owners expected in August. For those unfamiliar, Disc to Digital is Microsoft's initiative to promote a digital-only future for Xbox consoles. This feature allows players to insert their game discs into the console to convert them into digital licenses. When the disc is scanned, Microsoft uses the unique key to create a digital license, which prevents the disc from being activated on third-party consoles and stops it from being rented, borrowed, or sold to others.
This marks a significant shift away from physical disc game releases, as both Sony and Microsoft are moving towards ending disc-based games, encouraging gamers to use digital licenses exclusively. According to the roadmap, Xbox One and Series X users will be the first to scan their games and obtain digital licenses, as these consoles have physical disc readers. Game licensing will now be tied to the specific user account, with Xbox managing all engineering, certification, and support efforts if any issues arise. However, publishers retain the right to participate, maintaining full control over rights, pricing, and branding.Additionally, the leaked roadmap indicates that Microsoft plans to fully release the Xbox Backwards Compatibility program on PC by October this year, allowing gamers to play original Xbox titles on their PC through Game Pass or the Xbox Store. In the coming years, Microsoft intends to transition its Xbox 360 game catalog to next-generation Xbox devices, likely coinciding with the arrival of the next-generation console to ensure full backward compatibility with titles dating back to the Xbox 360 era.

articles.title: I wanted to buy a sophisticated analogue watch for my wedding — I wore a Galaxy Watch 8 Classic instead, and I couldn’t have made a better choice
articles.text:
I love the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 Classic so much I didn’t even take it off for my wedding — so where’s my Watch 9 Classic Samsung?
Stylish, sophisticated, smart
When I got engaged a couple of years ago my wife asked if there was anything I’d want in return to symbolize it: she gets to wear a ring, would I want a new accessory or piece of jewellery to match her. My immediate answer was a watch, with the plan that it’d be the one I wear on our wedding day.
I’d need something smart and sophisticated. Something that I wouldn’t regret seeing immortalized in our wedding photos for decades to come, and something I’d want to wear often.
I had ideas for the watch I'd get, but as wedding costs grew the idea of splashing out on a pricey timepiece felt less and less sensible. Even less so when I was also considering grabbing a smartwatch — as my pre-wedding fitness regime kicked into high gear and a more sophisticated tracker than my smart ring was feeling increasingly essential.
That’s when my eyes settled on a gadget that I thought might be both: a classic I could wear to the gym and on my wedding day. My wife was skeptical, but after seeing it in person she agreed that it did look the part.
So she let me wear a Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 Classic to our wedding. It might be my current favorite gadget, and I can’t understand why there isn’t a Galaxy Watch 9 Classic.
A winning design
The Classic doesn’t look like your basic utilitarian smartwatch. It dodges the simplistic look of the regular Watch 8, the Pixel Watch, or Apple Watch, and also the overly sporty designs of a Garmin or similar running companion.
Besides offering a larger screen size — 46mm vs the base model’s 40 or 44mm options — the Classic boasts a chunkier design than the regular Watch 8, and comes with a rotating metal bezel controller which provides some extra detailing and also a smoother way to navigate watch menus besides swiping.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Coupled with its band — the Hybrid which combines durable rubber with faux leather — and a watch face with moving hands you could very easily confuse the Classic for an analogue timepiece at a glance. And frankly, I just love how it looks and feels on my wrist (it puts my aged Fitbit to shame).
The design doesn’t just look impeccable, it can handle so many different scenarios too.
Besides wearing it for formal occasions I’ve taken the Galaxy Watch 8 Classic everywhere I go. To the office, on a 5K run, on hiking treks, to the gym, when I jump in the pool, and so much more. I even wear it in bed to track my sleep.
While the weight and size can be a little strange at first, after my first night sleeping with it I’ve had no complaints, and the trade off for the bulk is the Watch feels very usable and looks stylish.
Useful but not distracting
A similar effect could have been achieved with a smart ring and an analogue watch, wearing both to match the health tracking utility and sophisticated packaging. However I’ve been steadily growing frustrated with even the best smart rings.
The main draw of a ring is how simple it is: slip it onto your finger and it’ll follow your health and fitness metrics for days between charges. This simplicity falls apart, unfortunately, as soon as you want to access your data.
The apps of various rings I’ve tried have started to feel a little messy, and because I constantly have to check my phone to start workouts or understand my ring’s data I find I’m easily distracted by the plethora of other software and notifications I brush past on the way to my ring’s app. When I’m ready to run or hit the weights I want to focus, not succumb to a last-minute distraction.
With a watch I can start my tracking from my wrist at the press of a button. I can also see essential performance stats on the 46mm display, or (because it pairs nicely with my Samsung foldable) as part of the morning Now Brief on my phone.
I also love the non-fitness apps integration. I don’t text from my watch much, but I do often rely on wrist-based music controls and Google Maps directions — I can have a digital map while my phone can stay safely in my pocket where would-be biker thieves can’t snatch it.
My only gripe is I wish I could change the long press control on the bottom button. It defaults to opening Samsung Wallet and cannot be changed. I’m a Google Wallet user and while I could maybe move a couple of cards over I’m a) a bit too lazy, and b) weirdly nervous about paying for things with my watch.
Where’s my Watch 9 Classic, Samsung??
Given my Classic love I was hoping to see a Watch 9 Classic when Samsung debut its new lineup, but it was missing — replaced by a regular Watch 9 and a Galaxy Watch Ultra 2.
The Ultra 2 comes close to being a Classic — it adopts the bezel, though it doesn’t rotate — especially if you pick up the PeakForm Band, though it does also come at a more premium price.
And the lack of a rotating bezel is genuinely a major let down. You just have to trust me.
Though I doubt this means the end of the Classic. It has taken a break before to make room for the original Galaxy Watch Ultra, and I expect it’ll return next year as the Watch 10 Classic.

articles.title: Interview: ChipAgents CEO on Latest Funding for Agentic AI in EDA - EE Times
articles.text:
At DAC, The Chips to Systems Conference in Long Beach, California, last week, two-year old startup ChipAgents announced it had closed an extended series A round, adding $60 million to the $50 million it had raised in February 2026 and bringing its total funding to $134 million.
The news reflects renewed investor confidence in EDA startups. As ChipAgents founder and CEO William Wang told EE Times in a video interview at DAC, the conference is experiencing a huge renaissance of startups in the sector. Examples include Ricursive, with $335 million in funding to date; Normal Computing, with $85 million to date; Cognichip, with $93 million to date; Vinci, with its $46 million so far; Hiveware, with $28 million to date; Agentrys, with $25 million; and Architect Labs, with a $24 million seed round announced last month.
Wang also told EE Times how the company plans to use the funding, including scaling models, expanding global support, strengthening R&D, building on its market traction, and positioning itself within the wider EDA ecosystem.
You can also listen to an audio version of the interview below:
This is just a snapshot of some of the deals announced by new EDA companies at the annual conference, but it shows that venture firms are investing heavily in domain-specific AI startups serving specialized, high-margin industries.
Wang said increased investment across reasoning models, AI harnesses, and EDA tools encourages healthy innovation across the entire ecosystem. And rather than compete with legacy EDA software, companies such as ChipAgents act as an accelerator. “The data we are seeing is that every dollar our customer spends on ChipAgents, there’s another two dollars [spent] on the EDA tools involved by our agent, and then there’s another two dollars on the storage and database,” he said.
The company provides domain-specific AI agents for semiconductor design workflows that have historically relied on manual engineering. Unlike AI copilots that assist engineers with individual coding tasks, ChipAgents said its specialized agents can independently plan and execute complex design and verification workflows, compressing engineering tasks that once required weeks or months into days or hours.
In the company’s official news announcement, Wang said, “We’re enabling the industry to move beyond AI assistants toward autonomous agents that can execute meaningful engineering work. Our customer growth shows that semiconductor companies are ready for that shift, and this financing allows us to bring that capability to even more engineering teams.”
ChipAgents said it had a strong first half of 2026, reporting sixfold growth in annual recurring revenue and more than 120 deployments at semiconductor companies. The company also said this represents one of the industry’s largest commercial deployments of agentic AI for chip design and verification.
As the figures above show, companies such as ChipAgents and other emerging EDA startups provide the ‘agentic’ harnesses that plug directly into existing engines via appropriate APIs. Big EDA vendors own the underlying physics engines, solvers, and signoff tools built over several decades.

articles.title: Si tienes una USB sin usar no la botes: cinco usos que le puedes dar para revivirla
articles.text:
Una memoria USB olvidada puede transformarse en una herramienta valiosa si se aprovechan sus posibilidades más allá del almacenamiento tradicional.
Los pendrives antiguos que están en cajones tras la llegada del almacenamiento en la nube y los móviles con capacidad masiva siguen siendo útiles en numerosos escenarios cotidianos, aportando valor práctico y resolviendo problemas desde privacidad digital hasta reproducción multimedia.
PUBLICIDAD
Cinco usos que le puedes dar a una USB olvidada
- Unidad de rescate para ordenadores y sistemas operativos portátiles
Una de las formas más efectivas de reutilizar un USB viejo es convertirlo en una unidad de rescate. Utilizando herramientas como Rufus y una imagen ISO de Windows 11, Ubuntu u otra distribución Linux, el pendrive puede hacerse booteable para arrancar cualquier ordenador que haya dejado de funcionar por fallos en el sistema operativo.
Este método es fundamental cuando se necesita acceder a documentos, fotografías o archivos personales que permanecen intactos aunque el sistema principal esté dañado. Arrancando desde el USB, es posible copiar la información importante antes de reparar o reinstalar el sistema.
PUBLICIDAD
En este sentido, la memoria USB se transforma en una especie de “botiquín digital” que permite recuperar el acceso a equipos bloqueados, evitando la pérdida de datos y facilitando la reparación informática en casa. Muchos especialistas consideran que tener preparada una unidad de rescate es tan necesario como contar con un extintor o un botiquín de primeros auxilios en el hogar.
- Copia de seguridad física y almacenamiento offline
La copia de seguridad sigue siendo una de las funciones más relevantes para un pendrive. Aunque la nube ha desplazado mucho del almacenamiento cotidiano, contar con una copia física desconectada de internet aporta tranquilidad frente a ataques de ransomware, caídas de servicios o errores de sincronización.
PUBLICIDAD
Con herramientas como FreeFileSync, es sencillo mantener una réplica de documentos importantes, fotografías o proyectos personales en un USB de 16 GB, 32 GB o 64 GB.
En el caso de los móviles, un pendrive con adaptador USB-C u OTG permite transferir fotos y vídeos que ocupan espacio, liberando la memoria del teléfono sin perder recuerdos. Además, guardar una copia cifrada de la información del móvil en el USB permite resguardar mensajes, contactos y configuraciones, siguiendo la conocida regla 3-2-1 de seguridad digital: tres copias en dos soportes diferentes y una fuera del dispositivo principal.
PUBLICIDAD
- Reproducción de música en automóviles y televisores
El pendrive como reproductor multimedia sigue vigente para quienes disfrutan de la música sin depender de conexión móvil ni aplicaciones externas. Muchos coches mantienen puertos USB que reconocen archivos MP3 o FLAC, permitiendo almacenar miles de canciones y escucharlas directamente, sin consumir datos ni batería del teléfono. Esta solución resulta especialmente estable en viajes largos, coches sin Bluetooth o situaciones donde la cobertura es limitada.
Además, los televisores inteligentes utilizan memorias USB como ampliación de almacenamiento. Permiten grabar emisiones, almacenar aplicaciones, reproducir películas o ampliar espacio multimedia para series y vídeos personales.
PUBLICIDAD
- Plataforma de aplicaciones portables y sistemas “desechables”
Otra alternativa es usar la memoria USB como centro portátil de aplicaciones. Plataformas como PortableApps.com permiten instalar navegadores, editores de texto, reproductores multimedia y herramientas de mantenimiento que se ejecutan directamente desde el pendrive.
Esto resulta ideal para estudiantes, profesionales o cualquier persona que utilice ordenadores compartidos o públicos, ya que puede trabajar con sus programas y configuraciones personales sin dejar rastro al retirar la memoria.
PUBLICIDAD
En el ámbito de la privacidad, sistemas como Tails ofrecen la posibilidad de utilizar un sistema operativo “desechable” que funciona completamente desde la memoria USB. Este sistema, utilizado por Edward Snowden, está diseñado para no dejar rastros en el ordenador y todo el tráfico pasa por la red Tor.
- Llave de seguridad y protección de archivos
Por último, un pendrive puede transformarse en una llave de seguridad para proteger archivos o contraseñas. Herramientas como KeePass Portable o Rohos Mini Drive permiten almacenar bases de datos cifradas que solo pueden abrirse cuando el dispositivo está conectado físicamente al ordenador. Esta protección física añade una barrera ante robos, accesos remotos o filtraciones.
PUBLICIDAD
En algunos casos, los pendrives pueden utilizarse para la verificación en dos pasos en cuentas de Google o Microsoft, siempre que el modelo sea compatible con el estándar FIDO2. Si bien no todos los dispositivos cumplen este requisito, vale la pena comprobarlo antes de descartar una memoria antigua.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Everyday Efficiency Through Dependable Managed IT Services - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Growing Need for Reliable IT Support in Business
In today’s fast-paced business environment, operational efficiency is paramount. Companies face the constant challenge of maintaining seamless technology infrastructures while managing costs and minimizing downtime. This is where dependable managed IT services become invaluable. By outsourcing IT management to specialized providers, businesses can focus on their core activities while ensuring their technology systems are robust, secure, and efficient.
The reliance on technology to drive daily operations has never been greater. According to a report by Statista, 84% of enterprises worldwide have adopted some form of managed IT services to enhance their operational capabilities. This trend indicates a growing recognition that in-house IT teams alone often cannot meet the demands of modern business environments without external support.
Moreover, the digital transformation accelerated by recent global events has made IT infrastructure more critical than ever. Companies that invest in reliable IT management experience not only increased productivity but also a significant edge over competitors who struggle with frequent outages and cyber threats. For many businesses, partnering with dependable managed IT services providers is no longer optional – it’s a strategic necessity.
Unlocking the Benefits of Managed IT Services
Managed IT services provide a comprehensive approach to handling a company’s technology needs. These services include network monitoring, cybersecurity, data backup, and help desk support. By partnering with experienced providers, businesses can leverage expert knowledge and advanced tools that might otherwise be cost-prohibitive.
One significant advantage is the proactive nature of managed services. Instead of waiting for problems to occur, service providers continuously monitor systems to identify and resolve issues before they impact operations. This approach dramatically reduces downtime, which can be costly. Gartner estimates that the average cost of IT downtime is $5,600 per minute, underscoring the importance of prevention.
For companies operating in specific regions, choosing a local provider can offer additional benefits. For example, Sacramento MSPs like GitsTel combine industry expertise with a deep understanding of local business needs, delivering tailored solutions that maximize efficiency and reliability. This localized approach often results in faster response times and more personalized service, ensuring that IT issues are resolved promptly and with minimal disruption.
Additionally, the scalability of managed IT services allows businesses to adapt quickly to changing demands. Whether expanding operations or downsizing, companies can adjust their IT resources without the need for significant capital investment. This flexibility not only supports growth but also helps maintain cost control.
Enhancing Security and Compliance
Cybersecurity remains a top concern for businesses of all sizes. The increasing complexity of cyber threats requires continuous vigilance and updated defenses. Managed IT service providers specialize in safeguarding company data through advanced security protocols, regular vulnerability assessments, and compliance management.
Data breaches can be devastating, both financially and reputationally. According to IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report, the average cost of a data breach in 2023 was $4.45 million, highlighting the high stakes involved in protecting sensitive information. By outsourcing security functions, businesses access specialized skills and technologies without the expense of maintaining an in-house security team. This is especially important as compliance requirements grow more stringent across industries. Organizations can reduce risk and ensure adherence to regulations by partnering with providers that offer comprehensive compliance solutions.
Those interested in advanced security services and infrastructure management can visit Gravity Systems. Their expertise ensures that businesses stay ahead of evolving threats while maintaining operational continuity. With cyberattacks becoming more sophisticated, having a trusted partner who can implement cutting-edge defense strategies is essential for safeguarding business assets.
Driving Cost Efficiency and Scalability
Beyond improving reliability and security, managed IT services also help businesses control costs. Predictable monthly fees eliminate unexpected expenses related to emergency repairs or system failures. Moreover, outsourcing IT functions frees internal staff to focus on strategic projects rather than routine maintenance.
Scalability is another critical benefit. As companies grow, their technology needs evolve. Managed IT providers can quickly adjust service levels, provisioning additional resources or scaling back as necessary. This flexibility supports business agility and helps organizations adapt to changing market conditions.
According to a study by CompTIA, 70% of small and medium-sized businesses cited cost savings as a primary reason for adopting managed IT services, highlighting the financial impact of these partnerships. Furthermore, businesses that utilize managed IT services report a 25% improvement in operational efficiency within the first year of implementation, demonstrating tangible benefits beyond cost savings.
Choosing the Right Managed IT Partner
Selecting the right managed IT service provider is crucial. Businesses should look for partners with a proven track record, industry certifications, and a customer-centric approach. The provider should offer transparent service level agreements (SLAs) and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.
Local providers often bring an added advantage through personalized service and faster response times. Companies should evaluate their unique IT needs and seek providers that offer tailored solutions aligned with their business goals. For instance, working with can ensure that the provider understands specific regional regulations and business practices, which is vital for compliance and operational success.
Additionally, businesses should consider providers that invest in the latest technologies and maintain a proactive stance toward emerging IT trends and threats. This foresight can help organizations maintain a competitive edge and avoid costly disruptions.
The Future of Managed IT Services
As technology continues to evolve, so too will the scope and capabilities of managed IT services. Emerging trends such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and automation are increasingly integrated into IT management practices, enabling faster issue detection and resolution. Cloud computing also remains a key focus area, with many businesses migrating critical workloads to cloud platforms for enhanced flexibility and disaster recovery.
Managed IT service providers are adapting by offering hybrid solutions that combine on-premises infrastructure with cloud services, ensuring optimal performance and security. Businesses that embrace these innovations through reliable managed IT partners position themselves for long-term success.
Furthermore, the rise of remote work has underscored the importance of dependable IT services. Ensuring secure and efficient remote access to company resources is now a baseline requirement. Managed service providers help organizations implement virtual private networks (VPNs), endpoint security, and collaboration tools that support a distributed workforce without compromising security or productivity.
Conclusion
Dependable managed IT services are essential for businesses striving to maintain everyday efficiency and competitiveness. By leveraging expert support, companies reduce downtime, enhance security, control costs, and scale effectively. Whether working with local specialists or exploring advanced solutions, organizations can build resilient IT infrastructures that support sustained success in an increasingly digital world.
In summary, the strategic partnership with managed IT service providers empowers businesses to focus on what they do best while leaving the complexities of IT management to trusted experts. As technology continues to advance and threats evolve, dependable managed IT services will remain a cornerstone of operational excellence and business resilience.

articles.title: Creíamos que el glaciar Perito Moreno era invencible. Los satélites acaban de demostrar que nos equivocábamos
articles.text:
Durante décadas, el glaciar Perito Moreno fue una gran anomalía climática y el orgullo de la Patagonia, puesto que mientras los hielos de todo el mundo menguaban inexorablemente, el gigante argentino se mantenía estable. Sin embargo, esto ha dejado de ser así, puesto que las imágenes satelitales más recientes y una avalancha de nueva literatura científica confirman que el glaciar ha entrado en una fase de retroceso acelerado y pérdida de masa.
La voz de alarma. La tecnología satelital se ha convertido en nuestra mejor herramienta para constatar la salud de las masas de hielo a las que no tenemos acceso de una manera fácil. Pero además de darnos buenas noticias, también puede darnos un gran cambio de paradigma, como ocurrió el 30 de junio de 2026 cuando la web de Copernicus publicó como 'imagen del día' una captura satelital que comparaba el estado actual del glaciar con su situación en 2016.
Esta imagen es sin duda clave, puesto que hace evidente a simple vista el cambio radical que ha vivido el glaciar.
Un trabajo conjunto. Esta imagen a priori fue conseguida por el satélite Sentinel-2, pero la realidad es que no trabaja solo. Aquí la monitorización del Perito Moreno se ha apoyado en programas de la Agencia Espacial Europea y en un seguimiento exhaustivo que utiliza misiones como Landsat, CryoSat, Sentinel-1, ASTER, e incluso satélites históricos como Corona y KH-9. Todo este arsenal orbital ha permitido reconstruir las últimas tres décadas del glaciar.
Su colapso. De repente hemos visto cómo Perito Moreno ha comenzado a desintegrarse después de varios años aguantando perfectamente. Y la razón para esto la encontramos en un estudio publicado este mismo año que sitúa el inicio del cambio en el año 2018.
Aquí los científicos han podido ver que la culpa la tiene una pérdida de apoyo físico, puesto que el glaciar se ha desconectado de una morrena sumergida, es decir, una acumulación de sedimentos y rocas bajo el agua que funcionaba como barrera estabilizadora para la enorme pared de hielo. Al perder este "freno" natural, el glaciar ha acelerado su flujo y ha comenzado a desmoronarse como el resto.
En cifras. Tras analizar casi 30 años de imágenes, se ha podido ver claramente que el peor registro histórico se vio en 2025, cuando se habían perdido ya unos 385 metros de hielo. Además, diferentes estudios apuntan a que el glaciar ha experimentado un retroceso extremo de más de 800 metros.
El fin de la excepción. El caso del Perito Moreno ilustra a la perfección los mensajes y advertencias generales que la ONU ha estado emitiendo sobre el derretimiento acelerado de los glaciares a nivel global y el inminente riesgo hídrico. Aunque la ONU habla del contexto general, el caso particular de la Patagonia demuestra que ni siquiera los glaciares que creíamos más "blindados" pueden escapar ya al calentamiento global.
