articles.title: Nike, Adidas and Puma once sourced from this Punjab city. What happened?
articles.text:
Nike, Adidas and Puma once sourced from this Punjab city. What happened?
Jalandhar once dominated India’s sports goods exports and manufactured equipment for global brands. Chinese competition, automation and rising costs have since transformed its fortunes.
For decades, footballs, rugby balls, cricket bats, and hockey sticks stamped with names like Nike, Reebok, Adidas, Puma, Slazenger, and Webb Ellis were quietly manufactured not in Europe, but in Jalandhar, a mid-sized city in Punjab that rarely comes up in conversations about global sport. At its peak, this single cluster supplied products to more than 130 countries. Today, the story has grown more complicated, and understanding why is its own lesson in how manufacturing dominance can be built and then slowly lost.
A trade that migrated across a border
Jalandhar's sporting goods industry didn't originate there. It traces back to Sialkot, now in Pakistan, where the industry took root under British colonial influence, sports-obsessed administrators created early demand for locally made cricket and hockey equipment. After Partition in 1947, entrepreneurs and skilled workers migrated across the new border, rebuilding the trade from scratch in Jalandhar and, to a lesser extent, Meerut. It grew into a genuinely major industrial cluster: at its height in the 1980s and 90s, industry estimates put Jalandhar at roughly 90% of India's sports goods export market.
Where the dominance actually came from
The industry that grew here wasn't built on cheap, low-skill assembly. It was built on labour-intensive craftsmanship, hand-stitched footballs, precision-carved cricket bats using Kashmir willow, hockey sticks requiring skilled woodworking, much of it produced by small and medium enterprises and home-based contracted labour rather than large factories. Inflatable balls alone account for roughly 60% of what Jalandhar makes, and India became a leading sourcing destination in that category for global brands including Mitre, Lotto, Umbro, and Wilson, alongside its cricket and hockey equipment lines.
The competition that changed everything
By the most recent detailed industry assessments, Jalandhar's share of India's sports goods exports had fallen from that 90% peak to roughly 35%, with neighbouring Meerut in Uttar Pradesh at around 45% and now India's largest cluster. Unit counts for both clusters vary widely depending on whether household and micro units are included, but the direction of the shift is not disputed.
The reason is almost entirely external: cheap Chinese imports flooded both the domestic and international markets, and Chinese manufacturers gained a decisive edge through automation, lower production costs, and sophisticated technology that Jalandhar's traditional, craftsmanship-heavy small units struggled to match at scale. India's exports across the broader sporting goods category, which also covers toys, board games, and fitness and recreation items, reached $400.1 million in FY25, up about 8% year on year. Exports of sports equipment specifically are a fraction of that, and a fraction again of China's position in the same global market.
Why the industry hasn't disappeared, despite the pressure
What's kept Jalandhar in the game at all is precisely the thing that made competing on pure cost difficult: specialised craftsmanship in categories that don't automate easily. Hand-stitched balls and traditional protective gear remain areas where the cluster still holds a genuine edge, and its manufacturers continue to serve buyers across Europe and North America, with the UK, the US, Germany, France, and Australia among the largest destinations. Meerut, for its part, has leaned on its own pre-independence-era buyer linkages and faster adoption of technology in quality testing and logistics. Across India, the sports goods sector supports more than 500,000 livelihoods directly and indirectly, the large majority of them tied to these two clusters, and disproportionately including women workers in a historically labour-intensive trade.
Why this story matters
Jalandhar's arc, from near-total dominance of India's sports goods exports to a shrinking but still significant share, is a cautionary tale as much as a success story. Owning an industry completely doesn't guarantee owning it forever, especially in labour-intensive manufacturing where a lower-cost, more automated competitor can erode decades of accumulated market share within a generation. The next time you unwrap new sports gear from a well-known international brand, there's still a reasonable chance the hands that made it belonged to a small workshop in Punjab, holding onto a shrinking but still real piece of a business it once almost entirely owned.

articles.title: Tu celular Android puede quedarse sin acceso a Google Play: por qué esto es un problema
articles.text:
Muchos usuarios de teléfonos Android han comenzado a notar que sus dispositivos ya no pueden acceder a la tienda oficial de aplicaciones Google Play Store. Este cambio, silencioso pero de gran impacto, marca un antes y un después para quienes poseen celulares con sistemas operativos más antiguos.
La actualización reciente de la tienda ha elevado el requisito mínimo de compatibilidad y está dejando fuera a una porción de la base instalada de Android.
PUBLICIDAD
Durante años, la política de soporte para versiones antiguas del sistema operativo fue uno de los pilares que mantuvo vigente a millones de dispositivos en todo el mundo. Sin embargo, esa era ha llegado a su fin para una generación entera de teléfonos, que ahora enfrentan nuevas dificultades y riesgos.
Cuál es la versión de Android que se queda sin acceso a Play Store
La actualización que ha realizado Google establece que solo los dispositivos con Android 7.0 Nougat o versiones posteriores pueden seguir accediendo a los servicios clave de Google Play. La versión Android 6.0 Marshmallow —lanzada hace casi 11 años— ha quedado oficialmente fuera de soporte para la tienda, estableciendo un récord de longevidad en actualizaciones, pero también marcando su retiro definitivo.
PUBLICIDAD
El fin del soporte no fue anunciado con grandes comunicados, sino que se detectó a través de un hilo en Reddit y la actualización discreta de una página de soporte oficial. Capturas de pantalla de junio aún mostraban a Marshmallow como requisito mínimo, pero actualmente el sitio indica claramente que solo se admite Android 7.0 en adelante.
Este movimiento pone fin a la cobertura más prolongada que una versión de Android haya tenido en la historia, ya que Marshmallow fue compatible durante casi 11 años. Cuando se retiró el soporte para Lollipop (Android 5), esa versión llevaba más de nueve años en el mercado. Hacia fines de 2025, los equipos con Android 6 o inferior apenas representaban el 0,4 % de todos los dispositivos que accedían a los servidores de Google.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué implica perder acceso a la Play Store
Para quienes aún utilizan un teléfono con Android 6.0, el cambio no significa que el teléfono deje de funcionar por completo. Las llamadas y los mensajes de texto siguen estando disponibles. El verdadero problema surge en el uso de aplicaciones que dependen de la Play Store para instalarse, actualizarse o funcionar correctamente.
Algunas aplicaciones, como YouTube, ya han elevado sus propios requisitos mínimos y exigen Android 10 para su funcionamiento pleno. En otros casos, como Gmail, la compatibilidad aún se mantiene, pero la incertidumbre crece respecto a cuánto tiempo más durará.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta realidad se extiende a muchas otras apps populares, por lo que el usuario puede seguir usando su equipo para tareas básicas, pero encontrará cada vez mayores obstáculos en el uso como “teléfono inteligente”.
El núcleo del problema es el acceso fluido a las aplicaciones. Las normativas técnicas para los desarrolladores de software se vuelven cada vez más estrictas: cada actualización debe adaptarse a las funciones y características de las versiones más nuevas de Android, lo que deja a los equipos antiguos sin acceso a las últimas versiones de las apps o incluso imposibilita su descarga.
PUBLICIDAD
Riesgos de seguridad y otros peligros de no tener Play Store
El mayor riesgo de continuar usando un dispositivo sin acceso a Play Store radica en la seguridad digital. Sin actualizaciones de los servicios de Google Play, los teléfonos quedan expuestos a vulnerabilidades que no serán corregidas. Esto convierte a los equipos en potenciales objetivos de malware y robo de datos, ya que los sistemas operativos desactualizados son mucho más fáciles de atacar para los ciberdelincuentes.
Las aplicaciones bancarias, por ejemplo, han implementado bloqueos estrictos para equipos que no han recibido parches de seguridad en el último año. Por eso, muchas entidades financieras han decidido restringir el acceso a cuentas y transferencias desde dispositivos que no cumplen con los estándares modernos de protección.
PUBLICIDAD
Aunque existen alternativas para descargar aplicaciones desde repositorios de terceros, estas vías presentan los mismos problemas de compatibilidad y, además, eliminan la protección que brindaba el sistema de escaneo de la Play Store. Cuando este sistema deja de recibir actualizaciones, incluso la navegación web básica puede volverse insegura en equipos antiguos.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Managed IT And IT Outsourcing For Streamlined Daily Workflows - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Introduction to Managed IT and IT Outsourcing
In today’s fast-paced and technology-driven business environment, organizations are continually searching for ways to enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and maintain a competitive edge. One of the most effective strategies to achieve these goals is through managed IT services and IT outsourcing. These approaches allow businesses to delegate their IT management and support functions to specialized external providers, enabling them to streamline daily workflows, improve productivity, and focus more on their core business functions.
Managed IT and outsourcing services have become increasingly critical as companies face the challenges of rapidly evolving technology, cybersecurity threats, and the growing complexity of IT infrastructure. By partnering with expert providers, businesses gain access to advanced technology, proactive support, and scalable resources without the need to build and maintain large in-house IT departments. This shift not only reduces overhead costs but also increases agility, helping organizations respond swiftly to market changes and customer demands.
According to a recent report by Grand View Research, the global IT outsourcing market size was valued at USD 333.7 billion in 2021 and is projected to expand at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.4% from 2022 to 2030. This growth underscores the rising adoption of outsourcing as a strategic business practice.
The Value Proposition of Managed IT Services
Managed IT services represent a proactive approach to IT management, where external providers take responsibility for the oversight, maintenance, and optimization of an organization’s IT systems. This model ensures that IT infrastructure remains secure, updated, and efficient, minimizing the risk of downtime and costly disruptions.
One of the key advantages of managed IT services is their ability to offer continuous monitoring and rapid response to potential issues before they escalate. Automated tools used by managed service providers (MSPs) handle routine tasks such as patch management, system backups, and network monitoring, freeing internal staff from repetitive duties and reducing human error.
A report by MarketsandMarkets projects that the global managed services market size will grow from USD 223 billion in 2021 to USD 329 billion by 2026, reflecting widespread recognition of its benefits among businesses aiming to optimize IT operations.
A notable example in this space is ANC Group in the IT sector, a leader known for delivering tailored IT solutions that support businesses in maintaining seamless workflows. Their expertise allows clients to align their IT infrastructure with evolving business needs, ensuring agility and operational continuity. With services ranging from cybersecurity to cloud management, they offer comprehensive support that helps organizations stay ahead of technological trends and compliance requirements.
IT Outsourcing: A Strategic Advantage
Complementing managed services, IT outsourcing enables companies to delegate specific IT functions or entire operations to external experts. This approach provides several strategic benefits, including cost savings, access to specialized skills, and the ability to scale resources flexibly.
Outsourcing IT allows companies to convert fixed IT costs into variable expenses, paying only for the services they need when they need them. This financial flexibility is particularly valuable for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that may not have the budget to maintain extensive IT teams or infrastructure.
Further, outsourcing partners often bring niche expertise in areas such as cybersecurity, cloud computing, or software development, which may be difficult or expensive to cultivate internally. This access to advanced capabilities enables businesses to implement cutting-edge technologies and best practices without the learning curve or recruitment challenges.
A survey conducted by Deloitte found that 70% of businesses that outsource IT functions report improved service quality and cost efficiency, highlighting the tangible benefits of this approach.
For companies operating in competitive urban markets, collaborating with firms like APC Integrated for Boston businesses can provide customized IT outsourcing services tailored to local business environments. These partnerships help streamline workflows by managing routine IT maintenance, help desk support, and infrastructure administration, freeing internal teams to focus on strategic projects and innovation.
How Managed IT and Outsourcing Streamline Daily Workflows
The integration of managed IT services and outsourcing into business operations plays a pivotal role in streamlining daily workflows. This is achieved through several mechanisms:
– Automation of Routine Tasks: Managed service providers employ automation tools to handle patch management, system updates, backups, and network monitoring. Automating these repetitive tasks reduces manual errors and ensures consistent maintenance without burdening internal staff.
– Enhanced Network Reliability: Continuous monitoring and rapid incident response reduce downtime, ensuring that critical business applications remain available. Reliable IT infrastructure supports uninterrupted workflows and improves overall productivity.
– Improved Security Posture: Proactive threat detection, vulnerability assessments, and compliance management protect sensitive data and minimize the risk of cyberattacks. This security focus safeguards business continuity and customer trust.
– Scalable IT Resources: Outsourcing allows companies to adjust their IT capacity quickly in response to changing business demands, such as seasonal spikes or rapid growth, without the delays and capital expenditure associated with hiring and infrastructure expansion.
A recent IDC report revealed that organizations utilizing managed IT services experienced a 25% increase in operational efficiency within the first year of adoption. This efficiency translated into faster project completion, reduced downtime, and higher employee satisfaction.
Additionally, a report by CompTIA found that 59% of companies using managed services observed measurable improvements in end-user productivity due to enhanced IT support and reduced system disruptions.
Best Practices for Selecting Managed IT and Outsourcing Partners
Selecting the right managed IT or outsourcing provider is crucial to realizing the full benefits of these services. Businesses should carefully evaluate potential partners based on several criteria:
– Industry Expertise: Providers with experience in your industry will better understand the specific challenges and regulatory requirements you face.
– Service Level Agreements (SLAs): Clearly defined SLAs with measurable performance indicators ensure accountability and provide benchmarks for service quality.
– Technology Compatibility: Ensure the provider’s technology stack integrates seamlessly with your existing systems to avoid disruptions and facilitate smooth workflows.
– Flexibility and Scalability: Providers should offer customizable services that can evolve with your business needs, accommodating growth or changes in strategy.
– Proven Track Record: Look for client testimonials, case studies, certifications, and industry recognition that demonstrate the provider’s reliability and expertise.
Engaging with established firms offers the advantage of proven methodologies and extensive experience, which are invaluable for smooth onboarding and ongoing support. Their experience helps mitigate risks associated with IT transitions and ensures continuity during periods of change.
Similarly, partnering provides specialized knowledge of local market dynamics and customized IT outsourcing solutions, helping organizations optimize operations and focus on innovation.
Overcoming Challenges in IT Outsourcing and Managed Services
Despite their advantages, managed IT and outsourcing arrangements can present challenges, including communication gaps, data security concerns, and perceived loss of control.
To overcome these issues, organizations should:
– Establish Clear Communication Protocols: Regular meetings, transparent reporting, and defined escalation paths foster effective collaboration between internal teams and external providers.
– Implement Robust Data Protection Measures: Contracts should include clauses ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations such as GDPR or HIPAA, and providers should demonstrate strong security controls.
– Maintain Internal Liaison Teams: Designating internal staff to coordinate with providers helps preserve organizational knowledge and facilitates quick resolution of issues.
By proactively addressing these factors, companies can build strong, trust-based partnerships that deliver continuous improvement and align IT services with business goals.
Conclusion
Managed IT services and IT outsourcing have become indispensable strategies for businesses seeking to streamline daily workflows and enhance operational agility. By leveraging specialized expertise, advanced technologies, and scalable resources, organizations can reduce operational burdens, improve system reliability, and focus on strategic growth initiatives.
For companies looking to maximize these benefits, partnering with reputable providers offers a pathway to transform IT from a cost center into a strategic asset. Similarly, collaborating with
exemplifies how expert service providers can tailor solutions to meet evolving business needs, ensuring seamless workflows and sustained competitive advantage.
In an increasingly digital world, embracing managed IT and outsourcing is not merely an option but a strategic imperative. Organizations that adopt these approaches position themselves to thrive amid technological change, operational complexity, and market pressures-turning IT into a driver of innovation and efficiency.

articles.title: Visa to Acquire Fraud Intelligence Firm BioCatch for $2.4 Billion
articles.text:
Visa has agreed to acquire fraud prevention company BioCatch for $2.4 billion in cash as the payments giant looks to expand its cybersecurity and financial crime detection capabilities.
Founded in 2011, BioCatch provides behavioral biometrics technology that analyzes application, device, network and user activity to distinguish legitimate customers from fraudsters in real time.
Its artificial intelligence and machine learning models examine thousands of signals, including keystrokes, mouse activity, touchscreen gestures, device handling and signs that a user may be acting under coercion. The technology is designed to identify account takeovers, scams, money mule activity, application fraud and other financial crimes before a transaction is completed.
BioCatch says its technology analyzes 19 billion online banking sessions each month and protects 760 million users across 1.8 billion devices. The company serves more than 350 financial institutions in 21 countries, including over 100 of the world’s largest banks.
“BioCatch will help our clients stop fraud before it reaches the point of payment,” said Andrew Torre, president of value-added services at Visa. “This acquisition is part of our strategy to help clients prevent cyber threats upstream, building trust into every transaction.”
The acquisition will add BioCatch’s behavioral and device intelligence to Visa’s existing portfolio of cyber, fraud, risk and security products. Visa said it has invested more than $13 billion in technology and infrastructure over the past five years to protect the payments ecosystem.
Permira initially invested in BioCatch in 2023 and acquired a majority stake the following year in a transaction that valued the company at $1.3 billion.
The deal is part of a broader push by major payment companies to expand beyond transaction processing into cybersecurity and fraud intelligence. Mastercard completed its $2.65 billion acquisition of threat intelligence firm Recorded Future in 2024, while Visa acquired fraud prevention company Featurespace that same year.
BioCatch is being acquired from funds advised by private equity firm Permira and other shareholders. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions and is expected to close by the end of Visa’s fiscal second quarter of 2027.

Motorola Edge 60 Pro (256 GB) cai 34% em oferta no Mercado Livre
Edge 60 Pro (256 GB) tem até 24 GB de RAM e tela POLED de 120 Hz; celular bom para games da Motorola sai 34% mais barato que preço original no Pix
O Edge 60 Pro de 256 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 2.649 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O celular da Motorola com tela POLED de 6,7″ de 120 Hz, câmeras de 50 MP e até 24 GB de RAM recebe desconto de 34% sobre o preço original de R$ 3.999.
A tela POLED de 6,7″ do Edge 60 Pro possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de até 4.500 nits, que reproduz cores vibrantes com alta fluidez nas transições entre telas, além de visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Gorilla Glass 7i protege-a contra arranhões e pancadas.
Este é um ótimo celular para quem curte games, graças ao chip MediaTek Dimensity 8350 Extreme de 4 nanômetros e aos até 24 GB de RAM via RAM Boost, que sustentam alto desempenho mesmo nos títulos mais exigentes. Os 256 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço adequado para instalar vários jogos.
O kit de câmeras inclui uma wide com OIS e uma ultrawide, que captam ótimas cenas em ambientes amplos, e uma frontal que tira ótimas selfies, todas de 50 MP. A telefoto com zoom óptico de 3x possui 10 MP. Todas filmam em 4K.
O Edge 60 Pro possui um botão dedicado à suite Moto AI, para acionar recursos como edição inteligente de imagens e chatbots. A construção traz certificações militar MIL-STD-810H e IP68/IP69, que conferem resistência em cenários como poeira intensa, mergulhos acidentais e altas temperaturas.
Sua bateria de 6.000 mAh resiste até 45 horas de uso moderado, segundo a Motorola. O carregamento rápido de até 90 W via USB-C permite injetar uma carga para um dia inteiro de uso em apenas 6 minutos, um recurso excelente para quem quer jogar sem se preocupar com tomadas.
O Edge 60 Pro de 512 GB (apenas R$ 2.649 no Pix) foi atualizado para o Android 16 e deve receber apenas mais duas atualizações do sistema operacional. O gadget conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth e NFC.

articles.title: Doom now "runs" in Microsoft Paint thanks to a wildly inventive clipboard trick
articles.text:
WTF?! It's long been established that Doom can be made to run on pretty much anything with a screen, but this ability goes beyond mere devices. The latest example of the classic FPS's legendary portability involves Microsoft Paint essentially being used as a monitor that displays the original shareware version of the game – and the project was developed by Microsoft Azure CTO Mark Russinovich.
Called DoomPaint, Russinovich's creation doesn't literally execute Doom inside Microsoft's drawing app. Instead, ViZDoom, a ZDoom-based platform designed primarily for AI research, runs the engine and renders it headlessly. It loads the genuine shareware DOOM1.WAD for the first episode, while maps not included with that release use the BSD-licensed Freedoom WADs.
Every rendered frame is placed on the Windows clipboard as a bitmap and pasted onto the Paint canvas as a genuine document edit. A low-level keyboard hook captures the usual movement, strafing, shooting, and door-opening controls while Paint remains the active window, preventing the keystrokes from affecting the drawing app.
Making the process work smoothly required more than endlessly hammering Ctrl+V. Russinovich writes that an early version repeatedly overwrote the clipboard, sometimes replacing frame data before Paint had finished reading it. DoomPaint instead publishes a single OLE data object and updates the image bytes it supplies. Paint's reads also signal when the next frame can be made available, avoiding the race condition.
Performance depends on the PC and selected resolution, which can range from Doom's native 320 x 200 up to 640 x 480. The engine runs on its own thread at Doom's native 35Hz tic rate, meaning the displayed frame rate is capped at 35 fps and may be lower depending on how quickly the machine can make Paint process and composite the pasted images.
The setup brings some entertaining side effects. Because every frame is a real Paint edit, Ctrl+Z can move backward through them, while choosing File > Save produces a PNG screenshot. The project also includes the original Episode One music, converted from Doom's MUS format to MIDI on the fly, alongside sound effects supplied by the engine.
"Paint renders the game but does not compute it. Paint computes nothing. Paint has never computed anything. That's the joke," Russinovich explains.
DoomPaint is available on GitHub under an MIT license. Running its batch file creates a Python virtual environment and installs the required dependencies. ViZDoom boots directly into a map, so there are no title screens, demos, or in-game menus, and performance can sometimes fall to what Russinovich calls "spreadsheet-tier."

articles.title: AMD RDNA 5 Patches for DCN6 Display Engine Arrive in Linux Kernel
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
AMD RDNA 5 Patches for DCN6 Display Engine Arrive in Linux Kernel
AMD has released the latest set of patches for its RDNA 5 GPU IP, initiating the enablement of the Display Core Next (DCN) 6 display engine. Although the launch of AMD's next-generation RDNA 5 graphics cards is still a few months away, Linux support is already being developed to ensure every part of the stack is operational before the official release. According to the latest patch noted by Phoronix, the DCN6 display engine is associated with the AMD GFX13, which corresponds to the RDNA 5 GPU family. AMD's DCN display engine handles a variety of functions, including display output, image scaling, monitor ratio output, pixel manipulation, and much more. This engine is a highly complex component crucial for graphics output in AMD RDNA graphics cards.
For this DCN6 version, AMD has introduced new scaling integrity and costing surfaces, a UPSP pre-scaler to sample 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 content before scaling, and new pixel formats within the display logic. For the final GPU, this means that modern high-refresh and high-resolution gaming will be possible across a range of aspect ratios and configurations, with content being delivered smoothly. However, the final implementation will ultimately depend on what AMD includes in its actual GPU silicon.This marks the first appearance of the new DCN6 display engine, indicating that AMD is getting closer to shipping these RDNA 5 GPUs. The first wave of shipments will be to its add-in board partners, who will collaborate with AMD to deliver custom designs, though the timeline for this is still unknown. Interestingly, AMD has provided little public documentation on the DCN versions between DCN 4.2.1 and DCN 6.0.0. There is a single mention of the DCN5 display engine, but it is unclear if AMD decided to skip the DCN5 generation entirely, as the company might be planning interesting developments with DCN6 and chose to move directly to that version.

 Points forts
- Écran bien calibré et très lumineux.
- Présence du Snapdragon 8 Elite.
- Volet photo complet.
- Excellente autonomie.
- Expérience One UI 7.
Points faibles
- Design déjà vu.
- Téléobjectif assez décevant.
- Charge limitée à 25 W en 2025 !?
Alors oui, ce Galaxy S25 a tout d’un S24 amélioré, mais le résultat est là : le millésime 2025 surpasse le précédent. Son format compact, son écran réussi et sa puce surpuissante et économe en énergie en font un modèle aussi fluide qu’endurant. L’expérience photo gagne en précision, même si tout n’est pas parfait, notamment du côté du téléobjectif. On peut aussi regretter une puissance de charge encore limitée par rapport à la concurrence. Cependant, l’expérience offerte par One UI 7 et les nombreuses fonctions d’IA apportent un vent de modernité. À moins de posséder le modèle de 2024, cette itération est donc hautement recommandable. Samsung prouve ici que dans la tech comme en amour, il ne faut pas se fier aux apparences, et que l’important, c’est ce qu’il y a à l’intérieur.

articles.title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Could Let Model Repositories Execute Arbitrary Code
articles.text:
Three high-severity security flaws have been disclosed in Hugging Face's Diffusers library that could allow crafted model repositories to stealthily execute arbitrary code on machines that load it, opening the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain to security risk.
"These vulnerabilities are bypassing trust_remote_code, the safeguard designed to stop unreviewed code from running in the custom pipelines loading process," Zafran Labs researchers Gal Zaban and Ido Shani said in an analysis published last week.
The shortcomings have been collectively named FaceHugger.
With Hugging Face becoming the "GitHub of the AI era" and its libraries and repositories prevalent in enterprise environments, vulnerabilities in libraries like Diffusers can grant attackers extensive access owing to how the library is embedded into production pipelines, CI/CD systems, and container images.
Diffusers is a Python package that serves as a library of state-of-the-art (SOTA) pretrained diffusion models for generating videos, images, and audio. According to statistics shared on pepy.tech, the package has been downloaded more than 8.1 million times in July 2026.
One of the key capabilities of the library is to locally load a model from a Hugging Face hub repository via the DiffusionPipeline API, which, in turn, makes use of a configuration file to initialize specific pipeline and component classes, along with custom pipeline code.
The "trust_remote_code" parameter in Diffusers is a security safeguard that controls whether custom Python code hosted inside a model repository is allowed to execute during "from_pretrained()" loading. Setting it to "True" permits custom code execution, while "False" or omitting it blocks unverified code from running.
"The root cause of all different RCE variants [...] is that the trust check lives entirely in the first phase," Zafran explained. "Therefore, any method that makes the loader see custom code that the gate did not, allows bypassing the trust_remote_code mechanism."
Each variant has been traced back to a case of Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU), with the model download designed as two sequential, non-atomic HTTP requests instead of one a "single atomic operation" and the "trust_remote_code" security gate configured to run only against the first.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-44827 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A code injection vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be loaded through the custom_pipeline flow from a Hub repository by means of a crafted pipeline with the name "None.py" despite passing trust_remote_code=False (or omitting it, which is the default).
- CVE-2026-45804 (CVSS score: 7.5) - A race condition vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be introduced to a repository by modifying the configuration between the hf_hub_download and snapshot_download HTTP calls to the Hub, leading to code execution.
- CVE-2026-44513 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A code injection vulnerability that allows arbitrary code to be loaded through the custom_pipeline flow from a Hub repository despite passing trust_remote_code=False (or omitting it).
Following responsible disclosure, the vulnerabilities were addressed in Diffusers version 0.38.0, released in early May 2026. Any user who invokes "DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained" with custom pipelines is impacted.
"The underlying problem is that artifacts pulled from AI repositories are frequently treated as passive data, when configuration files, loaders, and custom pipeline code can quietly cross into executable code and turn a routine model load into an initial-access vector," the researchers added.
If immediate patching is not an option, the project maintainers have recommended the following workarounds -
- Only call from_pretrained with pretrained_model_name_or_path, custom_pipeline, and local snapshot directories from fully trusted sources that have been audited.
- Do not pass custom_pipeline= pointing at a Hub repository different from the primary pretrained_model_name_or_path before reading its pipeline.py.
- Before calling from_pretrained on a local snapshot, inspect the snapshot for unexpected *.py files, especially under component subdirectories (unet/, scheduler/, etc.) and at the snapshot root.
"These vulnerabilities underscore the critical need to treat AI model repositories as untrusted code, particularly as enterprise reliance on platforms like Hugging Face continues to grow," Zafran said. "A routine model download can easily become a vector for arbitrary code execution if security boundaries like trust_remote_code are bypassed."

articles.title: RTX 5060 Ti survives car crash after being bent in half — short PCB saves the day, single memory chip resolder restore full performance
articles.text:
RTX 5060 Ti survives car crash after being bent in half — short PCB saves the day, single memory chip resolder restore full performance
Because it had a rather short PCB.
Buying a new GPU is always a joyous occasion, but the celebration was cut short for an unfortunate customer in China. Right after buying an AX Gaming RTX 5060 Ti, they got into a serious car crash that ended up totaling the car — and the card along with it. Fortunately, the driver was safe, and somehow the GPU survived, too, with no major electronic damage. Despite being bent in half, the card ended up only requiring minor repair work and was brought back to life quickly by Brother Zhang.
Visually, the card didn't look salvageable, and midrange GPUs like these often don't make for feasible repair jobs either because of the high labor cost. The backplate and cooler were completely destroyed, so Brother Zhang separated them from the actual PCB. Luckily, this variant of the 5060 Ti used a very short PCB that just barely touched the point of curvature, so the internals were mostly fine.
The technician checked all the power rails for a short circuit but saw no abnormal resistance, which confirmed the core and memory weren't dead. He then proceeded to quickly test the GPU with its bare PCB, and it booted successfully. Brother Zhang devised a makeshift cooler that consisted of the bent fin stack straightened back to the best of his abilities, and two 120mm fans strapped on top via zip ties. This seemed enough to keep the card cool.
However, as soon as he tried to install drivers, the PC would black screen and hard crash, showing consistent signs of instability. At this point, Brother Zhang reopened the card and inspected the PCB. He inspected the flex point and decided to resolder the memory module closest to the edge of the board since it experienced the most torque. A simple removal and reapplication fixed the issue, and the card was detected correctly as a 5060 Ti with the full 8GB of VRAM.
Brother Zhang rechecked for any short circuits to ensure no solder bridges were created during the BGA work before moving on to benchmarking. In Furmark, the temps peaked and stabilized at 64°C with no visual artifacts. He then ran a full 3DMark loop to test the PCIe 5.0 x8 link speeds — the card passed with a high 98.9% stability score. It drew around 92% of its maximum power limit during the run, with core temps peaking at around 67°C. This 5060 Ti was officially a survivor.

articles.title: Truth Social vende acesso rápido a posts de Trump para empresas
articles.text:
A Truth Social, rede social de Donald Trump, lançou um serviço pago que permite a clientes institucionais receberem publicações selecionadas antes do público geral. A ferramenta mira organizações interessadas em mensagens com potencial impacto nos mercados.
Chamado Truth API, o recurso transforma as postagens mais relevantes da plataforma em um produto comercial de acesso rápido, gerando discussões sobre informação privilegiada.
Serviço promete entregar publicações em milissegundos
A Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), dona do Truth Social, apresentou o Truth API como uma ferramenta voltada a empresas que precisam acompanhar informações com máxima velocidade.
O sistema oferece um feed direto, licenciado e atualizado em tempo real com publicações consideradas capazes de influenciar decisões financeiras. Segundo a empresa, a distribuição pode ocorrer em milissegundos e inclui um arquivo histórico de posts desde 2022.
A novidade chama atenção porque Trump utiliza o Truth Social como principal canal para divulgar anúncios sobre temas como tarifas comerciais, economia e assuntos internacionais.
Entre os principais recursos anunciados estão:
- Acesso antecipado às publicações de contas relevantes da plataforma;
- Distribuição rápida de conteúdos para clientes institucionais;
- Arquivo histórico de mensagens publicadas desde 2022;
- Operação contínua para organizações que acompanham atualizações.
Mensagens de Trump já movimentam mercados
O interesse pelo serviço está ligado ao impacto que algumas publicações do presidente americano passaram a ter sobre investidores.
Empresas financeiras já acompanham as mensagens de Trump por meio de plataformas de dados e serviços que coletam informações das redes sociais. A diferença, segundo a TMTG, é que o Truth API oferece acesso direto ao conteúdo publicado dentro da própria rede.
“Mercados já se movimentam com publicações do Truth Social”, afirmou Kevin McGurn, CEO interino da TMTG, durante o anúncio da ferramenta.
A empresa também destacou que o serviço faz parte de uma estratégia para transformar recursos próprios da plataforma em novas fontes de receita recorrente.
Segundo informações divulgadas pela Reuters, a Trump Media chegou a avaliar uma cobrança de até US$ 100 mil (cerca de R$ 508 mil) por mês pelo acesso ao Truth API.
Ferramenta provoca debate político nos EUA
O lançamento do serviço também trouxe questionamentos. Os senadores Elizabeth Warren e Adam Schiff solicitaram uma investigação da Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos Estados Unidos (SEC) para avaliar possíveis impactos da ferramenta.
Na visão dos parlamentares, oferecer acesso mais rápido às mensagens do presidente poderia criar uma vantagem para grandes investidores e prejudicar participantes comuns do mercado.
“Isso parece ser um abuso escandaloso do cargo de presidente para benefício pessoal, que prejudica os investidores comuns e a integridade dos mercados, ao mesmo tempo em que enriquece Wall Street e outros participantes privilegiados e abastados”, escreveram os senadores em uma carta enviada à SEC.
Criado em 2022 após o banimento de Trump de outras redes sociais, o Truth Social se tornou o principal espaço digital usado pelo presidente para divulgar comunicados públicos.
O Truth API transforma esse fluxo de informações em uma oportunidade de negócio para a TMTG, mas também coloca em discussão uma questão central: quem deve ter acesso primeiro a mensagens capazes de influenciar decisões econômicas?
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: 5 películas de terror que seguro no conoces y que puedes ver ahora mismo en streaming
articles.text:
El género de terror atraviesa una de sus épocas más lucrativas y creativas. Lo que le ha convertido en un pilar fundamental del cine en la actualidad. Con experimentos como Weapons, dirigida por Zach Cregger, y Los pecadores de Ryan Coogler, las historias espeluznantes han logrado una nueva importancia. Eso, mientras éxitos de sagas queridas como Expediente Warren: El último rito dejaban claro que el terror era algo más que solo accidentes afortunados. Sin olvidar cine independiente del género como Devuélvemela y Obsesión.
Esta combinación demuestra que el horror actual no solo confía en la nostalgia de sagas recurrentes como Scream o Insidious. A la vez, se sostiene sobre la frescura de nuevos realizadores que conectan con los miedos de las audiencias modernas. Pero sobre todo, que el cine de terror contemporáneo es mucho más que solo historias creadas para provocar sobresaltos y aterrorizar por medios sencillos. Lo que hace de los más curiosos estrenos, una combinación entre temática, apartado visual y una elegante visión de lo terrorífico.
Todo un festín para fanáticos que además, deja a su paso una buena cantidad de cintas ideales para satisfacer incluso el gusto cinematográfico más raro. Si ese es tu caso, esta lista es para ti. Te dejamos cinco películas raras de terror que seguramente no conoces y que puedes ver ahora mismo en streaming. De una pieza de arte visual a lo más novedoso del horror folk. Todo para los fanáticos de terror de hueso rojo que disfrutan de un tipo de cinta sorprendente y que los servicios por suscripción hacen mucho más accesible.
Gaua (Prime Video)
Este recorrido mitológico por el País Vasco del siglo XVII es una de las grandes películas de terror que puedes encontrar en streaming. Escrita y dirigida por el aclamado cineasta Paul Urkijo Alijo, la producción sigue los pasos de Kattalin (Yune Nogueiras). Esta, una joven que huye de su violento esposo y que termina perdida en la densa penumbra del bosque. Para después, enfrentar a lo sobrenatural desde una óptica por completo nueva.
El gran triunfo de Urkijo radica en su capacidad para dignificar y empoderar la figura de las brujas. Además, de introducir de manera orgánica a seres espectrales del folclore como Gaueko o Inguma. Para lo que huye de los clichés inquisitoriales tradicionales. Visualmente apabullante, la cinta destaca por una impecable fotografía a cargo de Gorka Gómez Andreu. También, un soberbio uso de efectos especiales prácticos, maquillaje y vestuario, apartados que le valieron múltiples nominaciones en los prestigiosos Premios Goya.
Primate (Movistar+)
Esta rareza del subgénero del terror de supervivencia animal, sorprende por su premisa compacta, salvaje y sumamente eficaz. Dirigida por el cineasta británico Johannes Roberts, la cinta destaca por su ritmo implacable. También por un guion que emula de forma directa la tensión claustrofóbica de clásicos literarios y cinematográficos como Cujo de Stephen King.
La trama se sitúa en un idílico entorno tropical en Hawái, donde Lucy (Johnny Sequoyah) planea disfrutar de unas tranquilas vacaciones. Sin embargo, la atmósfera festiva se torna en una pesadilla sangrienta cuando Ben, el inteligente chimpancé mascota de la familia, es mordido por una mangosta rabiosa. Lo que desata un brote de agresión salvaje e incontrolable.
Primate evita la solemnidad pretenciosa, apostando por un festival de tensión pura y cruda. Roberts saca el máximo provecho de un elenco sólido que incluye a Jessica Alexander y al ganador del Óscar Troy Kotsur. Este, interpretado de manera entrañable, al padre sordo de la protagonista. Si estás buscando una rareza del género, esta es ideal para ti.
Keeper (Movistar+)
Dirigida por Osgood Perkins (reconocido por éxitos como Longlegs y The Monkey), es una de esas películas de terror que pasan desapercibidas. Pero que terminan por convertirse en pequeños clásicos. Con un ajustado presupuesto de 6 millones de dólares, la cinta brilla al transformar una premisa aparentemente sencilla en una experiencia surrealista y profundamente asfixiante. La trama sigue a Liz (Tatiana Maslany) y Malcolm (Rossif Sutherland), una pareja que decide celebrar su aniversario con una escapada de fin de semana. Lo que les lleva a una cabaña completamente aislada en el bosque.
Sin embargo, la aparente tranquilidad se quiebra por completo cuando Malcolm debe regresar repentinamente a la ciudad por una emergencia. Por lo que deja a Liz sola en la propiedad ante la manifestación de presencias siniestras y un mal indescriptible que devela los oscuros e históricos secretos del lugar. Ideal para fanáticos del gran plot-twist final.
Stopmotion (Prime Video)
Escrita y dirigida por el aclamado cortometrajista británico Robert Morgan, la cinta explora las fronteras entre la cordura, el arte macabro y la cruda realidad. La trama sigue los pasos de Ella Blake (Aisling Franciosi), una talentosa animadora atrapada bajo la absorbente sombra de su dominante madre. Esta, una leyenda de la animación.
Tras una tragedia familiar, Ella se vuelca obsesivamente en la creación de un retorcido cortometraje con marionetas hechas de materiales grotescos. Un proyecto que poco a poco empieza a cobrar una siniestra vida propia. La gran genialidad de la producción radica en utilizar la extenuante y milimétrica técnica del cuadro por cuadro (stop-motion) no solo como un formato visual. También, como una retorcida alegoría sobre el trauma heredado, el aislamiento absoluto y el perfeccionismo destructivo.
Morgan combina de forma magistral secuencias de acción real con una animación espeluznante y de texturas orgánicas. Además, con un sobresaliente diseño de sonido que acentúa cada crujido y deformación acústica. El filme prescinde por completo de los sustos fáciles para edificar una atmósfera de pesadilla pura y existencial. Es una auténtica obra cumbre sobre la locura del creador que atrapa y fascina de principio a fin.
El ritual (Netflix)
Dirigida por David Bruckner y escrita por Joe Barton esta adaptación de la aclamada novela homónima de Adam Neville, es ideal para los amantes del folk horror. En especial, por la capacidad de la cinta de entrelazar de forma orgánica el terror sobrenatural con un desgarrador drama sobre la culpa, el duelo y la cobardía. La trama sigue a cuatro amigos de la universidad que se reúnen para hacer senderismo en los densos y desolados bosques de Suecia. Todo como homenaje a un amigo trágicamente asesinado.
Sin embargo, tras tomar un atajo equivocado, el grupo queda atrapado en un laberinto natural. En medio de la cual, una presencia ancestral y malévola comienza a acecharlos y a desenterrar sus peores traumas nocturnos. Pero en lugar de ser evidente, la obra prefiere edificar una atmósfera de tensión asfixiante e incómoda basada en símbolos de ocultismo pagano. Sin embargo, su gran éxito es la criatura final, Moder: un gigante jötunn de la mitología nórdica. Una entidad retorcida de impresionante diseño visual que se alza como uno de los más creativos del cine de horror moderno.

articles.title: New Russian electronic warfare system aims directly at Starlink satellites
articles.text:
Russia debuts anti-Starlink EW system that can blind terminals by overloading 'satellites' receiving antennas'
Russia’s Volna Kupol Garant takes down Starlink satellites
- Russia unveils an electronic warfare system designed to interfere with Starlink satellite communications
- Volna Kupol Garant focuses on satellites instead of disrupting ground communication terminals
- The new Russian system reportedly jams eight Starlink transmission bands using directed radio signals
Russia has unveiled a new electronic warfare system designed to disrupt Starlink communications by interfering directly with satellites instead of attacking ground terminals.
The system, dubbed Volna Kupol Garant, directs concentrated radio signals toward Starlink satellites, preventing them from receiving transmissions from users within its operating area.
Russian officials say the approach temporarily interrupts communications without physically damaging spacecraft.
The system aims to interfere directly with satellites
Volna Kupol Garant reportedly relies on a narrow-beam high-frequency radio signal that differs from conventional electronic warfare systems.
According to Russian officials, the transmission overloads receiving antennas aboard Starlink satellites, temporarily preventing them from detecting signals transmitted from terminals beneath the affected coverage area.
"Volna does not physically destroy the spacecraft, but for the duration of the 'illumination,' it blocks the ability of a specific satellite to serve ground terminals," said Dmitry Kuzyakin, general designer of the Center for Integrated Unmanned Solutions.
The disruption reportedly continues beyond the active transmission because affected satellites require several additional minutes before normal communications capability returns after interference ends.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Volna Kupol Garant generates interference across eight Starlink data transmission bands, each measuring 62.5 MHz, using a directional phased-array antenna system.
Kuzyakin said Starlink satellites orbit about 500 km above Earth, adding that the phased-array system was designed to interfere with its receiving antennas.
This device also has the capacity to disrupt and even disable spacecraft operations.
Modular battlefield design claims tactical coverage
Volna Kupol Garant is equipped with six trailer-mounted modules, each carrying two steerable satellite antennas enclosed beneath radio-transparent protective radomes.
The modular arrangement reportedly allows antennas to remain trailer-mounted or operate from separate ground installations, providing greater flexibility across different operational environments and deployment requirements.
According to reports, one complete complex can reportedly create a Starlink jamming zone covering as much as 20 km² through narrow-beam interference techniques.
This system creates operational challenges for satellite communications within affected areas.
However, the installation's considerable size could increase visibility to electronic intelligence assets because numerous exposed antennas remain active during operations.
This development is unlikely to sit well with the United States and Ukraine, both of which are already weighing how future conflicts might extend into orbit.
Reports suggest the US has explored controlling which nations can operate satellites, a shift that could reshape the trajectory of regional conflicts if it materializes.
Russia is likely to defend its satellite capabilities aggressively, given the growing role they play in modern warfare.
That role includes supporting communications, intelligence gathering, navigation, and operations involving unmanned military systems.
As of the time of writing, Volna Kupol Garant has not been independently verified, nor has it reportedly been used in the war.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 €
articles.text:
Alors que la pénurie mondiale de puces mémoire pousse Google à relever le prix de ses futurs Pixel 11 de 100 €, Amazon prend le contre-pied avec l'iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go, proposé à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 €. Une remise de 100 € qui tombe à point nommé pour qui hésitait à investir dans le haut de gamme Apple.
Présenté le 9 septembre 2025, l'iPhone 17 Pro inaugure un châssis unibody en aluminium forgé à chaud avec un système de refroidissement par chambre à vapeur, une première pour la gamme Pro. Il embarque la puce A19 Pro, gravée en 3 nm, avec un CPU 6 cœurs, un GPU 6 cœurs intégrant du ray tracing matériel et 12 Go de RAM. Côté photo, le système Fusion 48 MP repense entièrement les trois capteurs arrière, avec un téléobjectif tétraprisme offrant un zoom optique jusqu'à 8x, une première sur iPhone.
Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir cet Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go ?
- Un zoom optique 8x inédit sur iPhone, porté par un téléobjectif tétraprisme de 200 mm
- Une puce A19 Pro avec chambre à vapeur, pensée pour encaisser les charges intensives sans surchauffe
- Une remise de 100 € qui arrive alors que le marché s'oriente vers des prix plus élevés, Google et Samsung ayant tous deux annoncé des hausses récentes
Si l'offre présentée dans cet article n'est plus disponible, consultez la liste de prix ci-dessous pour trouver d'autres bons plans sur ce même produit. La mise à jour des prix est automatique.
Une promo à contre-courant d'un marché sous tension
Le contexte rend cette baisse d'autant plus notable : Google prépare une hausse d'environ 100 € sur ses futurs Pixel 11, avec la disparition pure et simple de l'option 128 Go, une décision justifiée par une pénurie de puces mémoire DRAM dont les prix ont bondi de plus de 70% depuis début 2025. Samsung a suivi une logique similaire sur le Galaxy S26, en doublant le stockage de base tout en augmentant son prix conseillé. Selon IDC, le prix de vente moyen des smartphones a progressé de 14% en 2026, un climat qui rend une remise de 100 € sur un iPhone Pro d'autant plus rare.
Ce que la puce A19 Pro change concrètement
Le Neural Engine 16 cœurs et le GPU avec Neural Accelerators par cœur ciblent avant tout les usages gourmands : montage vidéo 4K, jeux avec ray tracing ou traitement photo avancé en temps réel. Le système photo profite lui aussi de cette puissance supplémentaire, avec une prise en charge du ProRes RAW et de la vidéo 4K à 120 images par seconde sur le téléobjectif. Pour un usage quotidien plus classique, ces capacités restent en réserve : l'essentiel du gain perceptible se ressent surtout sur la fluidité générale et l'autonomie, portée à 31 heures de lecture vidéo contre 25 heures sur le modèle précédent.
✅ Les points forts
- Zoom optique 8x, une première sur iPhone, porté par un téléobjectif tétraprisme
- Refroidissement par chambre à vapeur, une nouveauté pour limiter la surchauffe lors d'usages intensifs
- Autonomie en hausse, jusqu'à 31 heures de lecture vidéo
❌ Les limites
- Prix qui reste élevé malgré la remise, dans l'absolu comme face à la concurrence Android d'entrée de gamme
- Stockage de base à 256 Go, sans option 128 Go, comme la tendance générale du marché haut de gamme
- Gains de la puce A19 Pro surtout perceptibles sur des usages avancés (montage vidéo, ray tracing), moins visibles au quotidien
Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 € sur Amazon
À 1229 €, l'iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go profite d'une remise qui détonne dans un marché des smartphones où la tendance est plutôt à la hausse des prix, comme le confirme l'annonce récente de Google sur ses futurs Pixel 11. Une occasion à saisir pour accéder au haut de gamme Apple sans attendre une éventuelle prochaine augmentation généralisée du secteur.

articles.title: Namen, Reisepässe und Bewegungen: Öffentlich zugängliches Dashboard überwachte Ausländer in China
articles.text:
Name, Reisepass und Bewegungen: Öffentlich zugängliches Dashboard überwachte Ausländer in China
Der Cybersicherheitsforscher Marc Hofer hat sich auf China spezialisiert. Genauer gesagt, recherchiert er immer wieder, wie die chinesische Regierung ihre Bürger:innen mit moderner Technik trackt. Bei einer seiner Untersuchungen Anfang des Jahres stieß er auf ein Dashboard mit dem Titel „Dynamische Kontrollplattform für ausländisches Personal“.
So werden Ausländer:innen in China getrackt
Das Dashboard zeigt dabei ein digitales Abbild der chinesischen Stadt Zhangjiakou. Die Seite zeigte an, dass in der Stadt mehr als 700 Ausländer:innen getrackt werden. Insgesamt konnte aber auch auf eine Datenbank von mehr als 12.000 Einträgen zurückgegriffen werden, die auch Personen außerhalb der Stadt inkludierte, die noch nie in Zhangjiakou gewesen waren.
Die Einträge listeten den Namen, ein Bild sowie das Herkunftsland, Geschlecht, Geburtsdatum, Telefonnummer und die Reisepassnummer auf. Einige Personen wurden sogar auf Schritt und Tritt mit dem Dashboard getrackt. Im Profil einer Frau aus der Mongolei standen genaue zeitliche Abläufe über einen Besuch im Einkaufszentrum sowie in Restaurants. Das deutet darauf hin, dass das System auf die Kameraüberwachung und Gesichtserkennung der Stadt zugreifen kann.
Darauf lassen auch Aufnahmen von Studierenden und Tourist:innen schließen. In den Profilen von ausländischen Studierenden wurden Aufnahmen gefunden, die sie vor der Universität zeigten. Tourist:innen wurden hingegen im beliebten Skigebiet der Stadt aufgenommen. Durch die Aufnahmen wurden auch Bewegungs- und Beziehungsprofile erstellt. Das Profil eines pakistanischen Mannes war mit dem von zwei anderen Pakistanern verknüpft. In einem Mindmap war zu sehen, dass sie schon zusammen gereist sind.
Gegenüber der New York Times sagte Hofer dazu: „Wer auch immer die Informationen dort eingetragen hat, hat Zugriff auf echte Daten. Das ist mehr als nur ein paar Typen, die herumspielen, und auch kein Low-Level- oder Studierendenprojekt.“ Laut Hofer soll die Seite für das Public Security Bureau der Stadt angelegt worden sein, dem Polizeirevier der Stadt.
Welches Sicherheitsrisiko das Dashboard birgt
Doch nicht nur das reine Sammeln von Daten war ein Problem, auf das der Sicherheitsforscher gestoßen ist. Um sich Zugang zu der Plattform zu verschaffen, war keinerlei Umweg notwendig. Als Hofer die Seite aufrief, waren schon Username und Passwort eingetragen. Er musste sich nur noch einloggen. Er schließt deshalb darauf, dass das System eigentlich noch nicht live genutzt wurde, sondern zu Demonstrationszwecken diente. Trotzdem wurde es zu Anschauungszwecken mit echten Daten gefüllt, auf die im Grunde jeder zugreifen konnte.
Im Rahmen der Recherche verifizierte die New York Times so, dass mindestens sieben der Datensätze mit den Daten echter Personen übereinstimmten, darunter auch Sicherheitsforscher Marc Hofer selbst. Zudem hatten die Behörden Zugriff auf die Daten eines NYT-Reporters, der in Beijing arbeitet, sowie auf die seines Kindes. Mittlerweile ist das Dashboard nicht mehr verfügbar. Laut Hofer wurde es schon im Mai 2026 offline genommen. Dabei bleibt fraglich, ob die chinesischen Polizeibehörden nur den öffentlichen Zugang gesperrt haben und das Tool jetzt trotzdem weiterhin nutzen.

articles.title: Windows 11 consomme trop de mémoire : Microsoft va enfin réduire la gourmandise de son OS
articles.text:
Sur un PC équipé de 8 Go de RAM, Windows 11 en occupe déjà près de 6 Go au repos, avant même que vous ouvriez la moindre application. Microsoft le reconnaît noir sur blanc et s’engage à alléger son système d’ici fin 2026.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
L’annonce vient de Pavan Davuluri, président de la division Windows and Devices, dans un bilan d’étape publié sur le blog Windows Insider. Il y cite « l’optimisation mémoire pour 8 Go et au-delà » parmi quatre chantiers prioritaires pour la fin de l’année, aux côtés d’une installation plus rapide des nouveaux PC, du contrôle parental et de la saisie vocale. Microsoft veut que Windows garde moins de mémoire pour lui, pour en laisser plus au navigateur et aux applications de tous les jours.
Une promesse sans chiffre ni date précise
Les améliorations arriveront d’abord sur les versions de test Insider, puis par petites touches sur les autres PC, sans grande mise à jour unique qui réglerait tout d’un coup. Microsoft n’a communiqué ni objectif chiffré ni gain de mémoire attendu. La piste technique consiste à basculer davantage d’éléments de l’interface vers WinUI, la brique native de Windows, plus légère que les composants web qui pèsent lourd sur la RAM.
Le message détonne avec les choix récents de l’entreprise. Microsoft a d’abord imposé 16 Go comme socle de ses PC Copilot+, avant de commercialiser un Surface Laptop à 1 299 dollars avec seulement 8 Go de RAM. Comme le souligne Windows Latest, c’est aussi la première fois que la firme reconnaît que le système lui-même est en cause, au-delà des seules applications.
Pour les possesseurs d’un PC portable à 8 Go, la nouvelle est bonne sur le principe, puisque leur machine pourrait respirer un peu mieux sans dépenser un centime. Encore faut-il que Microsoft tienne parole, et le premier vrai déploiement n’est pas attendu avant l’automne. On jugera sur preuves à ce moment-là.

articles.title: The $60 million startup tackling Africa's travel payments problem | TechCabal How African hotels can reduce international payment costs
articles.text:
Every year, international travellers spend billions of dollars on African safaris, luxury lodges and holiday experiences. Yet before much of that money reaches the businesses providing those experiences, a portion is lost to payment processing fees, foreign exchange charges and the cost of moving money across borders.
For African tourism operators, getting paid can be surprisingly expensive.
TurnStay, a South African fintech that helps travel businesses accept payments from international guests, believes that problem has been overlooked for too long.
Alon Stern, TurnStay’s chief executive officer (CEO) and co-founder, said the three-year-old startup processed over R1 billion ($60.6 million) in travel payments during the first six months of 2026. The company provides payment infrastructure for hotels, safari lodges, tour operators and villa agencies, helping them reduce the cost of accepting international bookings.
The milestone underscores a broader challenge facing Africa’s tourism sector. While many operators compete for the same global travellers as hotels and tour companies elsewhere in the world, they often pay significantly more simply to receive payment. Card network fees, foreign exchange spreads, cross-border acquiring costs, and can collectively consume a meaningful share of booking revenue, eroding margins and reducing the amount of tourism income that ultimately remains on the continent.
“Getting paid can be expensive in the travel industry, and for a long time African merchants have carried a much heavier cost than their overseas counterparts for doing exactly the same job,” said Stern.
He stated that traditional payment processing for international travel bookings can cost African merchants as much as 8% of a transaction. By combining a merchant-of-record model with modern payment rails, including stablecoins for cross-border settlement, TurnStay says it can reduce fees to as little as 1.6%.
“The less merchants pay in fees, the more money stays in Africa,” Stern said. “That’s the philosophy behind everything we build. The experiences African travel businesses offer are already world-class. We think the payment infrastructure behind them should be too.”
Rather than relying solely on traditional banking infrastructure, TurnStay uses digital payment rails to move money across borders faster and at lower cost before settling funds with merchants.
“Global platforms have used this model for years,” stated Stern. “But what we have done is bring that same infrastructure to African travel merchants directly, so a lodge or tour operator doesn’t have to be the size of Airbnb to access it.”
The company counts luxury hospitality brands including Singita, Londolozi, Safari.com and The Capital among its customers, with operations expanding beyond South Africa into Kenya, Tanzania, Botswana and Mauritius.
TurnStay raised a $300,000 pre-seed round in 2024 followed by a $2 million seed round in 2025 and is now preparing for a Series A fundraising round to accelerate its pan-African expansion.
For Stern, the company’s rapid growth is less about payment volumes than correcting a structural imbalance in Africa’s tourism economy.
“Three years ago there were two of us and an idea,” he said. “Now we’re processing over a billion rand every six months for some of the best-known names in African travel, and we have just begun.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: HubSpot Redesigns JITA Authorization with Rule Engine Architecture
articles.text:
HubSpot has redesigned its Just-In-Time Access (JITA) authorization system using a rule engine architecture to make access decisions more observable and explainable. The system evaluates temporary access requests through independent rules instead of embedded conditional logic, allowing engineers to inspect how individual policies contribute to access decisions and manage authorization requirements as they change.
HubSpot’s JITA system processes approximately 5,500 access requests per business day across a workforce of about 10,000 employees. The previous implementation relied on increasingly complex conditional logic as new access scenarios were introduced. While this approach supported existing requirements, engineers found it difficult to determine why a request was approved or denied and which individual checks contributed to processing latency.
The redesigned architecture introduces a rule engine where authorization policies are evaluated as independent rules organized through a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Each rule produces structured output containing evaluation results, execution timing, and metadata used to understand the authorization decision.
Simplified DAG showing role-based branching and parallel rule evaluation (Source: HubSpot Blog Post)
HubSpot engineers identified decision visibility as a key requirement during the redesign. The team described the challenge as moving beyond determining whether the authorization system worked to understanding the reasoning behind individual decisions.
The question wasn't just does this work?
It was Can we explain every decision this system makes, to anyone, at any time?
The architecture separates shared request data from individual authorization rules through a common context object. User attributes, team information, and request details are collected before evaluation and passed to rules during execution. This approach reduces duplicate data retrieval and provides consistent inputs across authorization checks.
The system also introduces observability at the rule level. Instead of measuring only the overall authorization request, engineers can inspect individual rule execution times, failures, and outcomes. This provides visibility into slow evaluations and the contribution of specific policies to authorization processing.
HubSpot uses isolated rule execution to handle failures during evaluation. If a rule encounters an error because of an unavailable dependency or unexpected condition, the failure is recorded while other rules continue evaluation. Access decisions continue to rely on the results defined by authorization rules.
The migration process included running the legacy and new authorization systems in parallel and comparing decisions before routing production authorization requests through the new implementation. The team also introduced periodic reviews involving security, product, and operational stakeholders to evaluate whether rules remain appropriately scoped and aligned with access requirements.
Recertification dashboard showing usage metrics and execution statistics per rule (Source: HubSpot Blog Post)
Similar approaches have emerged across the industry, although implementations vary based on the type of access being managed. Open Policy Agent (OPA) provides a policy-as-code model that separates authorization decisions from application logic through a dedicated policy engine. Google Cloud’s Privileged Access Manager focuses on temporary activation of privileged cloud permissions with approval workflows and audit tracking. Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management similarly manages just-in-time activation of privileged roles. These systems emphasize declarative policies or identity governance, while HubSpot’s implementation focuses on application-specific access workflows with rule-level execution visibility.
By introducing a rule engine, structured decision metadata, and governance processes, HubSpot has moved JITA authorization from embedded conditional logic toward a system where access decisions can be evaluated, monitored, and reviewed over time.

articles.title: Las gafas inteligentes tienen una luz que avisa de que están grabando. Para la Agencia de Protección de Datos eso no basta
articles.text:
Si un cacharro tiene una cámara seguro que tarde o temprano se usa. Es probable que no de la mejor manera, tampoco sin que se garantice por completo la privacidad. Es lo que ocurre con las gafas inteligentes, un dispositivo que Meta ha terminado popularizando y que no tardará en extenderse a la mayoría de marcas de móviles. Con sus ventajas y con sus problemas, algunos de los cuales ya pasaron hasta por los juzgados.
El problema. Las gafas con cámara y micrófono no hacen mucho más que un smartphone corriente. Lo que cambia es la comodidad de grabación, la sencillez a la hora de tomar vídeo o fotos y, sobre todo, que unas gafas son más fáciles de ocultar. Tienen un LED que avisa, sí, pero es diminuto, hay que estar mirando para verlo y durante un tiempo bastó con taparlo.
He probado varias gafas inteligentes, incluso analicé unas hace poco. Comprobé que facilitan la toma de vídeos en primera persona con respecto al smartphone. Y también aprecié las reticencias de la gente al verme con ellas puestas, incluso sin encender: la sensación de vulnerar la privacidad está muy presente. Usarlas no es en sí ilegal, como la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos ha corroborado. Lo que sí destaca es de qué lado recae la responsabilidad.
El responsable es quien graba. Las gafas son un dispositivo legal que, como cualquier otro que pueda registrar contenido público, no tiene un cheque en blanco sobre lo que puede o no hacer. No entraña problemas si las grabaciones se hacen en un entorno privado, con la aceptación de todos los que salen en pantalla. En un lugar público se pueden usar siempre que quien graba no se centre en las personas que no han autorizado la grabación. Y el audio tiene su propia línea roja: grabar conversaciones ajenas en las que no participas es delito, estés donde estés.
Los fabricantes se refugian en el LED. Han conseguido una cámara que puede camuflarse y que pasa desapercibida con facilidad. Esto podría derivar en claros problemas legales para ellos, por eso se escondieron tras un chivato: la bombillita de aviso. Cuando las gafas inteligentes graban, o hacen una foto, se enciende una luz para avisar a quien está delante de la cámara. Por eso Meta lo tuvo claro: el LED es el eje de sus normas de uso responsable. Toda la responsabilidad recae en el dueño de las gafas.
Y lo han blindado. El problema es que el chivato se podía tapar, y hasta hay quien pagaba por inutilizarlo. Meta lleva tiempo cerrando esa puerta: taparlo con cinta ya desactivaba la cámara desde la segunda generación de gafas, pero apareció quien iba más allá y la manipulaba físicamente (o directamente la destruía). Desde julio de 2026 las Ray-Ban Meta también detectan esa manipulación y apagan la cámara: sin LED brillando no hay foto.
La compañía presume de que el LED de captura no tiene interruptor de apagado, de que retira los anuncios de servicios de manipulación y emprende acciones legales contra quienes los venden. Me parece una buena medida, pero no reduce la desconfianza ante quien ve a alguien con las gafas puestas.
Para la AEPD, la luz no basta. La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos publicó sus buenas prácticas para gafas inteligentes el 13 de julio de 2026, seis días después de que Meta recalcase el buen uso del LED. Aun así, la segunda recomendación de la agencia pide avisar de viva voz cuando vayas a grabar, aunque el dispositivo lo indique con una luz.
La tercera recomendación de la AEPD advierte del micrófono: las voces también son datos personales, grabar conversaciones ajenas sin que lo sepan vulnera la normativa de privacidad. Y la séptima recomendación recuerda que hay sitios donde directamente no se graba: baños, vestuarios, edificios públicos, domicilios...
Cuidado con compartir. El chivato no traslada la responsabilidad a ninguna parte, solo la deja donde siempre estuvo. Mientras grabas para ti, para enseñárselo a tu familia, estás fuera del RGPD por la excepción doméstica. En cuanto lo publicas sales de esa excepción y pasas a responder tú de lo que hay en el vídeo. No responde Meta, ni Rokid, ni lo hará Samsung cuando tenga sus gafas o Google. Los fabricantes se refugian en el LED porque les funciona, pero a ti no te va a cubrir.

articles.title: Pocketpair et Garena annoncent Palworld Online, un véritable MMORPG sur iOS et Android
articles.text:
Attendez-vous à manger du Palworld à toutes les sauces dans les mois à venir. Alors que la version 1.0 du jeu principal vient tout juste d’être déployée (avec de nouveaux gros chiffres à la clé), qu’un TCG a été lancé et qu’une version mobile est en préparation du côté de chez Krafton, Garena Online Private Limited officialise, ce 3 août 2026, Palworld Online.
Palworld Online est bien évidemment un produit qui est le fruit d’un partenariat officiel avec le studio Pocketpair, et non pas un énième scam opportuniste. Prévu en 2026 sur iOS et Android, il entend « réinventer la profondeur, la liberté et l’échelle du jeu de survie avec collecte de créatures original ». Pas une mince affaire en soi, mais l’assurance qu’il ne s’agira pas d’une simple copie repensée pour une nouvelle plateforme.
C’est quoi Palworld Online ?
Comme son nom l’indique, Palworld Online entend être un vrai MMORPG tiré de l’univers de Palworld. Garena Online Private Limited nous promet un monde ouvert interconnecté, où les joueuses et les joueurs partiront à l’aventure en équipe, « n’importe quand, n’importe où ». Palworld Online aura aussi sa propre histoire, avec différentes quêtes narratives pensées pour enrichir le lore que l’on connaît déjà.
Palworld Online encouragera à jouer à plusieurs, que ce soit pour participer à des activités en PvE (joueurs contre IA) ou des matchs en PvP (joueurs contre joueurs). « Celles et ceux qui recherchent une expérience avec un rythme plus reposant pourront visiter la base des autres ou faire équipe pour combattre des boss dans le monde ouvert ou chasser des Pals rares ensemble », révèle Garena Online Private Limited.
À noter qu’il sera possible d’établir un QG en coopération, grâce à un gameplay axé sur la collaboration. On retrouvera d’ailleurs l’un des éléments du jeu principal, en l’occurrence la possibilité de confier des tâches répétitives aux créatures que l’on a précédemment capturées. Un élément controversé, car renvoyant à une image d’exploitation.
Aucun détail sur le modèle économique n’a été fourni par Garena Online Private Limited, mais on peut miser sur un accès gratuit (free-to-play), avec une tonne de microtransactions et des paiements réguliers pour débloquer des contenus exclusifs (pass de saison). Il faudra surveiller ce point pour s’assurer que Palworld Online ne tombe pas dans une logique pay-to-win.
Les ambitions sont en tout cas énormes pour cette adaptation. Concernant le format mobile, l’entreprise rassure : « Spécifiquement optimisé pour le jeu mobile, Palworld Online s’appuie sur une interface tactile et fluide, avec des contrôles one-tap optionnels, rendant la gestion de la base, la construction, le repositionnement ou encore le déploiement des Pals simple sur une plateforme mobile, sans sacrifier la profondeur ou la flexibilité, sur une configuration large d’appareils. »
